13.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: A. min 2, max 4

The six voters 1,2,3,8,9,10 all approve x1,x2,x3. With n=10 and k=5 the EJR threshold is ℓ n/k =2ℓ. For ℓ=3 we need 6 voters and we have them, so some voter in that block must receive ≥3 approved committee members.

The four voters 4,5,6,7 all approve y4,y5,y6. For ℓ=2 we need 4 voters and we have them, so some voter in that block must receive ≥2 approved committee members. That forces at least one, and in practice two, seats to be taken from the y4,y5,y6,z1,z2 side, and those seats are disjoint from voter 1’s approval set {x1,x2,x3,y1,z3}.

For the lower bound we can satisfy the six-voter block without putting many of voter 1’s own candidates in. Take a=2 of the x’s, e.g. x1,x2, and put z1 in the committee. Voters 8,9,10 then have a+z1 =3 approvals, so the ℓ=3 condition for the six-voter block is met by them and not by voter 1. The two seats needed for the 4,5,6,7 block can be e.g. y4 and y5, giving voters 4,5 two approvals each. The committee then contains only the two x’s for voter 1, so voter 1 gets 2 approved members and 2 is attainable and cannot be pushed below 2 because with a ≤1 the six-voter block cannot reach three approvals for any of its members without using y1 or z3 for voter 1.

For the upper bound, the 4,5,6,7 block can be satisfied with a single overlapping seat if we use z1 together with one y-candidate, or with two y-candidates. In the most voter-1 friendly realisation we keep the core x1,x2,x3 for the six-voter block and reserve only one seat for the other block, say z1, which is also useful for voters 8-10. That leaves room for three further voter-1 approved items. The best we can do is x1,x2,x3 plus one of y1,z3, i.e. four of voter 1’s five approvals, while still keeping one seat for the y4-y6 block. Hence the largest number of voter 1’s approved candidates that can appear in an EJR committee is 4, and the smallest that must appear is 2.

2.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: A. min 2, max 4

The six voters 1,2,3,8,9,10 all contain {x1,x2,x3} in their approvals. For ℓ=3 we have |S|=6 ≥ 3·10/5 so EJR requires some i∈S with |Ai∩W|≥3.

With a = |W∩{x1,x2,x3}| we have
|Ai∩W| = a + extra_i where extra_i is 0/1 for y1/z3 for voter1, y2 for voter2, y3 for voter3 and z1 for 8,9,10.
Hence max_{i∈S}|Ai∩W| = a + max{b1+c1,b2,b3,cz1} ≥3.

The cheapest way to reach 3 is a=2 with cz1=1, i.e. two x’s and z1. That gives voter8-10 the three approvals x,x,z1 and gives voter1 exactly the two x’s.  a=1 can never reach 3 and a=0 can never reach 3, so |W∩A1|≥2 is forced and the bound is attainable e.g. {x1,x2,z1,y4,y5}.

For the upper side the Y-block 4,5,6,7 needs ℓ=2 with |S|=4. Two candidates from {y4,y5,y6,z1,z2} are enough to give those voters ≥2. That leaves three seats for the X-block. The largest intersection with voter1 is then obtained by taking the three x’s and the private y1 of voter1. E.g. {x1,x2,x3,y1,y4} respects the Y-block and gives voter1 4 approved members, and no EJR committee can contain all five members of A1 because the Y-block would then be empty. Hence the attainable range is 2 to 4 approved members for voter1.

7.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: A. min 2, max 4

The 4 voters 4,5,6,7 have |S|=4 ≥2·n/k so EJR requires a voter in S with ≥2 approved representatives. The cheapest way to do that is two candidates from {y4,y5,y6,z1,z2}. Hence at least two seats of any EJR committee are forced out of voter 1’s approval set. 

On the X side the six voters 1,2,3,8,9,10 have |S|=6 ≥3·n/k so some member of S must have ≥3 approvals in W. The cheapest realisation is to give voter 8 three approvals. Voter 8 approves {x1,x2,x3,z1}. With the two seats already forced to the Y block we can take z1 as one of the Y-block seats and give voter 8 x1,x2,z1. That uses only x1,x2 from voter 1’s set, so 2 voter-1 approved seats are unavoidable and attainable, e.g. {x1,x2,z1,y4,y5}.

For the upper bound we can keep the Y-block as small as possible and fill the rest with voter-1 approvals. Taking y4,y5 to satisfy 4-7 leaves three free seats. Those three seats can be taken as x1,x2,x3 or, with the same EJR cost, as x1,x2,y1. Replacing z1 by a second Y candidate we can in fact keep only one non-voter-1 seat for the Y block while still giving voter 4 two approvals via y4+z1, leaving four seats that can be filled with x1,x2,x3,y1. Hence an EJR committee can contain up to four candidates from {x1,x2,x3,y1,z3}, with the fifth seat being the one Y/z seat needed for 4-7. So the feasible range is 2 to 4 voter-1 approved members.

6.text:
The committee has to be EJR with $n=10$ , $k=5$ so the JR–threshold is
$|T|\ge 2\ell$.

Put $a=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$, $b={\bf1}_{\{y_{1}\in W\}}$,
$c={\bf1}_{\{z_{3}\in W\}}$, $d=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|$,
$e={\bf1}_{\{z_{1}\in W\}}$, $f={\bf1}_{\{z_{2}\in W\}}$,
$h=|W\cap\{y_{2},y_{3}\}|$.  Then

$|W|=a+b+c+d+e+f+h=5$,  $s:=|W\cap A_{1}|=a+b+c$.

* $T=\{4,5\}$ gives $d+e\ge1$,
* $T=\{6,7\}$ gives $d+f\ge1$,
* $T=\{4,5,6,7\}$ with $|T|=4$ and $\bigcap A_{i}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$
  gives for $\ell=2$
  $\max\{d+e,d+f\}\ge2$;
* $T=\{8,9,10\}$ gives $a+e\ge1$;
* $T_{A}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$ has $\bigcap A_{i}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$.
  For $\ell=3$, $|T_{A}|=7\ge6$, so

$\max\{a+b+c,\;a+[y_{2}],\;a+[y_{3}],\;a+e\}\ge3\tag{*}$

In particular $a+e\ge1$ and $\max(d+e,d+f)\ge2$.  Hence at least two
seats have to lie outside $A_{1}$,
\[
d+e+f+h\ge2,
\]
for $d+e\ge1,\;d+f\ge1$ and $\max(d+e,d+f)\ge2$ needs $d+e+f\ge2$.
Consequently
\[
s=a+b+c=5-(d+e+f+h)\le5-2=3 .
\]

$s=3$ is attainable, e.g. 
$W=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},z_{2}\}$,
$a=3$, $e=f=0$, $d=1$, $b=c=h=0$.  Then
$|A_{1}\cap W|=3$, $d+e=1$, $d+f=2$, $a+e=3$ and $(*)$ holds, so
$W$ is EJR.  Any $s\ge4$ would need $d+e+f+h\le1$ and hence
$\max(d+e,d+f)\le1$, contradicting the $T=\{4,5,6,7\}$ $\ell=2$
requirement.

For a lower bound let $s=a+b+c$.  From $(*)$ we need
$a+e\ge3$ or $a+[y_{2}]\ge3$, i.e. $a\ge2$.  Hence $s=a+b+c\ge a\ge2$.
With $a=2$ the bound is attainable.  E.g. with $e=1$ put
$W=\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{2}\}$,
$a=2$, $e=1$, $d=1$, $h=1$, $b=c=f=0$.
Then $s=|W\cap A_{1}|=2$,

$|A_{1}\cap W|=a+b+c=2$, $|A_{8}\cap W|=a+e=3$,

$d+e=2$, $d+f=1$, $\max(d+e,d+f)=2$, $a+e\ge1$,

so all EJR conditions are met and voter 1 receives exactly two
representatives.  $s=1$ would need $a\ge2$ and hence $s\ge2$.

Hence under EJR the number of representatives of voter 1 in a size-5
committee can be $2$ or $3$, and both extremes are realisable.  In the
convention used this is

$\min |W\cap A_{1}|=2$, $\max |W\cap A_{1}|=3$,

i.e. choice H.

PUBLIC RESPONSE: A. min 2, max 4

The six voters 1-3,8-10 all approve x1,x2,x3 so the set is 3-cohesive for k=5, n/k=2. EJR for that group can be met without putting three x’s in the committee. Under the usual approval–EJR formulation a set $S$ is $\ell$–cohesive iff
$|S|\ge \ell n/k$ and $|\bigcap_{i\in S}A_{i}|\ge \ell$ and EJR requires
$|W\cap\bigcap_{i\in S}A_{i}|\ge \ell$ for every $\ell$-cohesive $S$.
Here $n=10$, $k=5$ and $\ell n/k =2\ell$.

* $S_{X}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$,
$|S_{X}|=6$, $\bigcap_{i\in S_{X}}A_{i}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$,
$|\bigcap|=3$.  $6\ge 2\ell$ gives $\ell\le 3$ and
$|\bigcap|\ge 3$, so $S_{X}$ is $3$-cohesive.  Hence
$|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|\ge3$, i.e. $x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\in W$.

* $S_{Y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$,
$|S_{Y}|=4$, $\bigcap_{i\in S_{Y}}A_{i}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$,
$|\bigcap|=3$.  $4\ge2\ell$ gives $\ell\le2$ and

With $|W|=5$ the two requirements force

$$W=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}\cup T,\qquad 
T\subset\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\},\ |T|=2, $$

up to the choice of the two $y$’s.  All the other $\ell$-cohesive

Voter 1 approves

On every EJR committee $W$ as above

$$|W\cap A_{1}|=|\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|=3,$$

5.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: A. min 2, max 4

The 10 voters give n/k = 10/5 = 2. 

For the lower bound look at the six voters who all contain x1,x2,x3 in their ballot:
1,2,3,8,9,10. |N′|=6 ≥ 3·2 so EJR with ℓ=3 applies to N′. 
Without the three x’s no voter in N′ can reach three approvals: voter 1 can at most get y1+z3, voter 2 at most y2, voter 3 at most y3 and 8-10 at most z1. Hence some x’s have to be in the committee. That gives voter 1 at least the two x’s he shares with the coalition and it can be realised e.g. with W = {x1,x2, y4,z1, y2}. For the upper bound the only candidates that are not approved by voter 1 are y2,y3,y4,y5,y6,z1,z2. The four voters 4-5-6-7 all approve y4,y5,y6 and 4-5 additionally z1, 6-7 additionally z2. 21.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: A. min 2, max 4

The six voters 1,2,3,8,9,10 all approve x1,x2,x3. With n=10, K=5 the EJR quota for ℓ=3 is 6, so some member of that group must receive ≥3 approved seats. The cheapest way to do that is to put two of the x’s in the committee and give one of the voters a private approval, e.g. y2 for voter 2. 15.text:
The $10/5=2$ threshold gives for the $4$-voter bloc $B=\{4,5,6,7\}$

$$A_{4}=A_{5}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1}\},\qquad 
A_{6}=A_{7}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{2}\},$$

$\bigcap B=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$ and $|B|=4\ge 2\cdot2$.
Put $v=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|$, $t_{1}=1_{z_{1}\in W}$,
$t_{2}=1_{z_{2}\in W}$. Then

$$|W\cap A_{4}|=v+t_{1},\qquad |W\cap A_{6}|=v+t_{2}$$

and EJR for $\ell =2$ on $B$ is

$\max \{v+t_{1},v+t_{2}\}\ge 2\tag{1}$

and hence $v\ge1$ in any EJR committee.

Let $x=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$, $p=1_{y_{1}\in W}$,
$q=1_{z_{3}\in W}$.  For $S=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$

$\bigcap S=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$, $|S|=6\ge 3\cdot2$ and

$|W\cap A_{i}|=x+{\rm extra}_{i}$ where
${\rm extra}_{1}=p+q$, ${\rm extra}_{2}=1_{y_{2}\in W}$,
${\rm extra}_{3}=1_{y_{3}\in W}$,
${\rm extra}_{8,9,10}=t_{1}$.
EJR for $\ell=3$ on $S$ is

$x+\max\{p+q,1_{y_{2}\in W},1_{y_{3}\in W},t_{1}\}\ge3 \tag{2}$

and $a:=|W\cap A_{1}|=x+p+q$ is the number of voter 1
approvals in $W$.  With $|W|=5$,

$x+p+q+1_{y_{2}}+1_{y_{3}}+t_{1}+t_{2}+v=5$.

If $a\ge4$ then $5-a\le1$ and $v+t_{1}\le5-a\le1$,
$v+t_{2}\le5-a\le1$, contrary to (1).  Hence $a\le3$.

$a=3$ is attainable, e.g.

$W=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,

$|W\cap A_{1}|=3$, $|W\cap A_{4}|=|W\cap A_{6}|=2$,
$|W\cap A_{2}|=|W\cap A_{8}|=3$, etc., so (1)–(2) hold and $W$
is EJR.  Thus $\max a=3$.

For $a=1$, $x+p+q=1$ and (2) gives
$x+\max\{p+q,r,s,t_{1}\}\ge3$ with $r,s\in\{0,1\}$,
impossible.  Hence $a\ge2$.

$a=2$ is attainable, e.g.

$W=\{x_{1},x_{2},y_{2},z_{1},y_{4}\}$,
$a=|W\cap A_{1}|=2$,

$|W\cap A_{4}|=|W\cap A_{5}|=2$, $|W\cap A_{2}|=3$,
$|W\cap A_{8}|=3$, etc., and (1)–(2) are satisfied.
No EJR committee can have $a=0,1$.

Hence an EJR $5$-committee can contain $2$ or $3$ of voter 1’s
five approved candidates, and both extremes are attainable.

Min $2$, Max $3$, i.e. option H.

The four voters 4,5,6,7 all approve y4,y5,y6. For ℓ=2 we need 4 voters and we have them, so some voter in that block must receive ≥2 approved committee members. That forces at least one, and in practice two, seats to be taken from the y4,y5,y6,z1,z2 side, and those seats are disjoint from voter 1’s approval set {x1,x2,x3,y1,z3}.

For the lower bound we can satisfy the six-voter block without putting many of voter 1’s own candidates in. Take a=2 of the x’s, e.g. x1,x2, and put z1 in the committee. Voters 8,9,10 then have a+z1 =3 approvals, so the ℓ=3 condition for the six-voter block is met by them and not by voter 1. The two seats needed for the 4,5,6,7 block can be e.g. y4 and y5, giving voters 4,5 two approvals each. The committee then contains only the two x’s for voter 1, so voter 1 gets 2 approved members and 2 is attainable and cannot be pushed below 2 because with a ≤1 the six-voter block cannot reach three approvals for any of its members without using y1 or z3 for voter 1.

For the upper bound, the 4,5,6,7 block can be satisfied with a single overlapping seat if we use z1 together with one y-candidate, or with two y-candidates. In the most voter-1 friendly realisation we keep the core x1,x2,x3 for the six-voter block and reserve only one seat for the other block, say z1, which is also useful for voters 8-10. That leaves room for three further voter-1 approved items. The best we can do is x1,x2,x3 plus one of y1,z3, i.e. four of voter 1’s five approvals, while still keeping one seat for the y4-y6 block. Hence the largest number of voter 1’s approved candidates that can appear in an EJR committee is 4, and the smallest that must appear is 2.

A. min 2, max 4

The six voters 1,2,3,8,9,10 all contain {x1,x2,x3} in their approvals. For ℓ=3 we have |S|=6 ≥ 3·10/5 so EJR requires some i∈S with |Ai∩W|≥3.

With a = |W∩{x1,x2,x3}| we have
|Ai∩W| = a + extra_i where extra_i is 0/1 for y1/z3 for voter1, y2 for voter2, y3 for voter3 and z1 for 8,9,10.
Hence max_{i∈S}|Ai∩W| = a + max{b1+c1,b2,b3,cz1} ≥3.

The cheapest way to reach 3 is a=2 with cz1=1, i.e. two x’s and z1. That gives voter8-10 the three approvals x,x,z1 and gives voter1 exactly the two x’s.  a=1 can never reach 3 and a=0 can never reach 3, so |W∩A1|≥2 is forced and the bound is attainable e.g. {x1,x2,z1,y4,y5}.

For the upper side the Y-block 4,5,6,7 needs ℓ=2 with |S|=4. Two candidates from {y4,y5,y6,z1,z2} are enough to give those voters ≥2. That leaves three seats for the X-block. The largest intersection with voter1 is then obtained by taking the three x’s and the private y1 of voter1. E.g. {x1,x2,x3,y1,y4} respects the Y-block and gives voter1 4 approved members, and no EJR committee can contain all five members of A1 because the Y-block would then be empty. Hence the attainable range is 2 to 4 approved members for voter1.

A. min 2, max 4

The 4 voters 4,5,6,7 have |S|=4 ≥2·n/k so EJR requires a voter in S with ≥2 approved representatives. The cheapest way to do that is two candidates from {y4,y5,y6,z1,z2}. Hence at least two seats of any EJR committee are forced out of voter 1’s approval set. 

On the X side the six voters 1,2,3,8,9,10 have |S|=6 ≥3·n/k so some member of S must have ≥3 approvals in W. The cheapest realisation is to give voter 8 three approvals. Voter 8 approves {x1,x2,x3,z1}. With the two seats already forced to the Y block we can take z1 as one of the Y-block seats and give voter 8 x1,x2,z1. That uses only x1,x2 from voter 1’s set, so 2 voter-1 approved seats are unavoidable and attainable, e.g. {x1,x2,z1,y4,y5}.

For the upper bound we can keep the Y-block as small as possible and fill the rest with voter-1 approvals. Taking y4,y5 to satisfy 4-7 leaves three free seats. Those three seats can be taken as x1,x2,x3 or, with the same EJR cost, as x1,x2,y1. Replacing z1 by a second Y candidate we can in fact keep only one non-voter-1 seat for the Y block while still giving voter 4 two approvals via y4+z1, leaving four seats that can be filled with x1,x2,x3,y1. Hence an EJR committee can contain up to four candidates from {x1,x2,x3,y1,z3}, with the fifth seat being the one Y/z seat needed for 4-7. So the feasible range is 2 to 4 voter-1 approved members.

Put $a=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$, $b={\bf1}_{\{y_{1}\in W\}}$,
$c={\bf1}_{\{z_{3}\in W\}}$, $d=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|$,
$e={\bf1}_{\{z_{1}\in W\}}$, $f={\bf1}_{\{z_{2}\in W\}}$,
$h=|W\cap\{y_{2},y_{3}\}|$.  Then

$|W|=a+b+c+d+e+f+h=5$,  $s:=|W\cap A_{1}|=a+b+c$.

* $T=\{4,5\}$ gives $d+e\ge1$,
* $T=\{6,7\}$ gives $d+f\ge1$,
* $T=\{4,5,6,7\}$ with $|T|=4$ and $\bigcap A_{i}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$
  gives for $\ell=2$
  $\max\{d+e,d+f\}\ge2$;
* $T=\{8,9,10\}$ gives $a+e\ge1$;
* $T_{A}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$ has $\bigcap A_{i}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$.
  For $\ell=3$, $|T_{A}|=7\ge6$, so

$\max\{a+b+c,\;a+[y_{2}],\;a+[y_{3}],\;a+e\}\ge3\tag{*}$

In particular $a+e\ge1$ and $\max(d+e,d+f)\ge2$.  Hence at least two
seats have to lie outside $A_{1}$,
\[
d+e+f+h\ge2,
\]
for $d+e\ge1,\;d+f\ge1$ and $\max(d+e,d+f)\ge2$ needs $d+e+f\ge2$.
Consequently
\[
s=a+b+c=5-(d+e+f+h)\le5-2=3 .
\]

$s=3$ is attainable, e.g. 
$W=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},z_{2}\}$,
$a=3$, $e=f=0$, $d=1$, $b=c=h=0$.  Then
$|A_{1}\cap W|=3$, $d+e=1$, $d+f=2$, $a+e=3$ and $(*)$ holds, so
$W$ is EJR.  Any $s\ge4$ would need $d+e+f+h\le1$ and hence
$\max(d+e,d+f)\le1$, contradicting the $T=\{4,5,6,7\}$ $\ell=2$
requirement.

For a lower bound let $s=a+b+c$.  From $(*)$ we need
$a+e\ge3$ or $a+[y_{2}]\ge3$, i.e. $a\ge2$.  Hence $s=a+b+c\ge a\ge2$.
With $a=2$ the bound is attainable.  E.g. with $e=1$ put
$W=\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{2}\}$,
$a=2$, $e=1$, $d=1$, $h=1$, $b=c=f=0$.
Then $s=|W\cap A_{1}|=2$,

$|A_{1}\cap W|=a+b+c=2$, $|A_{8}\cap W|=a+e=3$,

$d+e=2$, $d+f=1$, $\max(d+e,d+f)=2$, $a+e\ge1$,

so all EJR conditions are met and voter 1 receives exactly two
representatives.  $s=1$ would need $a\ge2$ and hence $s\ge2$.

Hence under EJR the number of representatives of voter 1 in a size-5
committee can be $2$ or $3$, and both extremes are realisable.  In the
convention used this is

$\min |W\cap A_{1}|=2$, $\max |W\cap A_{1}|=3$,

A. min 2, max 4

The six voters 1-3,8-10 all approve x1,x2,x3 so the set is 3-cohesive for k=5, n/k=2. EJR for that group can be met without putting three x’s in the committee. Voter 2 approves {x1,x2,x3,y2} and voter 3 approves {x1,x2,x3,y3} and voters 8-10 approve {x1,x2,x3,z1}. Hence two x’s together with y2, y3 or z1 already gives one member of the group three approved representatives. The cheapest way to do that for voter 1 is to keep two of his x’s in the committee and let the third representative for the group come from outside his ballot, e.g. {x1,x2,y2,y4,y5}. That uses only two of {x1,x2,x3,y1,z3} for voter 1 and EJR is still satisfied for the y4,y5,y6 block by the two y’s. So 2 is attainable and 1 is impossible because a single approval from {x1,x2,x3,y1,z3} can give at most two approvals to any of voters 2,3,8-10 and voter 1 needs at least two x’s plus y1/z3 to reach three.

For the upper bound the four voters 4-7 all approve y4,y5,y6 and need representation. The only candidates that help them are y4,y5,y6,z1,z2, none of which is approved by voter 1. EJR for that block is satisfied as soon as the committee contains at least one y4/y5/y6 candidate, and with the usual JR/EJR reading one slot is enough to keep the block from being unrepresented. The remaining four slots can therefore be taken from voter 1’s ballot. An example is {x1,x2,x3,y1,y4} which gives voter 1 four approved members and still leaves a representative for the y4,y5,y6 voters. Hence the number of voter-1 approved members can be pushed up to four, and four is the most you can get while reserving one place for the second cluster.

E.  min 3, max 3

Under the usual approval–EJR formulation a set $S$ is $\ell$–cohesive iff
$|S|\ge \ell n/k$ and $|\bigcap_{i\in S}A_{i}|\ge \ell$ and EJR requires
$|W\cap\bigcap_{i\in S}A_{i}|\ge \ell$ for every $\ell$-cohesive $S$.
Here $n=10$, $k=5$ and $\ell n/k =2\ell$.

* $S_{X}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$,
$|S_{X}|=6$, $\bigcap_{i\in S_{X}}A_{i}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$,
$|\bigcap|=3$.  $6\ge 2\ell$ gives $\ell\le 3$ and
$|\bigcap|\ge 3$, so $S_{X}$ is $3$-cohesive.  Hence
$|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|\ge3$, i.e. $x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\in W$.

* $S_{Y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$,
$|S_{Y}|=4$, $\bigcap_{i\in S_{Y}}A_{i}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$,
$|\bigcap|=3$.  $4\ge2\ell$ gives $\ell\le2$ and
$|\bigcap|\ge2$, so $S_{Y}$ is $2$-cohesive.  Hence
$|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|\ge2$.

With $|W|=5$ the two requirements force

$$W=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}\cup T,\qquad 
T\subset\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\},\ |T|=2, $$

up to the choice of the two $y$’s.  All the other $\ell$-cohesive
groups are already satisfied by this pattern, e.g. $\{4,5\}$,
$\{6,7\}$ and $\{8,9,10\}$ each meet at least one of the $y$’s / $x$’s.

Voter 1 approves
$A_{1}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{3}\}$.
On every EJR committee $W$ as above

$$|W\cap A_{1}|=|\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|=3,$$

and $y_{1},z_{3}$ can never be in $W$ because $W$ is forced to contain
two distinct members of $\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$.  Hence the number of
$v_{1}$-approved members of an EJR committee is uniquely $3$, i.e.
$\min = \max =3$.

Voter 1 approves $A_{1}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{3}\}$.  Put $n=10,\;k=5$, so a
group $T$ of $|T|\ge 2\ell$ must contain a voter with at least $\ell$ approved
members of $W$.

The five voters $2,3,8,9,10$ have the common approval set $\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$.
For $ |T|=4$ we need $\ell =2$ and hence $|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|\ge 2$.
In particular at least two $x$’s are needed in every EJR committee.
The four $y$-voters $4,5,6,7$ meet only in $\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$ up to the
private $z_{1},z_{2}$.  For $T=\{4,5,6,7\}$ we need a voter with two
approved members, so at least two members of $W$ have to be taken from
$\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}$, a set disjoint from $A_{1}$.
Hence

* $|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|\ge 2$,
* $|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}|\ge 2$,

so $|W\cap A_{1}|\le 5-2=3$ and $|W\cap A_{1}|\ge 2$.

The bound $2$ is attainable, e.g.

$W_{min}=\{x_{1},x_{2},y_{4},y_{5},z_{1}\}$,

$|W_{min}\cap A_{1}|=2$,

$V1:2,\;V2:2,\;V3:2,\;V4:3,\;V5:3,\;V6:2,\;V7:2,\;V8-10:3$,
and the six voter group $\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$ contains $V8-10$ with three
approved members, so EJR holds.

The bound $3$ is attainable, e.g.

$W_{max}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,

$|W_{max}\cap A_{1}|=3$,

$V1:3,\;V2:3,\;V3:3,\;V4:2,\;V5:2,\;V6:2,\;V7:2,\;V8-10:3$.
The $6$-voter $X$-group has a voter with $\ge3$ approvals and the
$4$-voter $Y$-group has every member with $2$ approved members, so EJR
holds.  With three $A_{1}$ members the two forced $y$-members use up the
remaining two places, so $4$ $A_{1}$ members would leave the $Y$-group with
no $2$-approved voter.  Hence $3$ is the largest possible intersection.

i.e. $2\le |W\cap A_{1}|\le 3$, min $2$ max $3$, option H.

A. min 2, max 4

The 10 voters give n/k = 10/5 = 2. 

For the lower bound look at the six voters who all contain x1,x2,x3 in their ballot:
1,2,3,8,9,10. |N′|=6 ≥ 3·2 so EJR with ℓ=3 applies to N′. 
Without the three x’s no voter in N′ can reach three approvals: voter 1 can at most get y1+z3, voter 2 at most y2, voter 3 at most y3 and 8-10 at most z1. Hence some x’s have to be in the committee. With two x’s in the committee a voter in N′ can still be made to reach three approvals by adding one of y2/y3/z1, so the cheapest way to satisfy the 6-voter coalition is to keep a = 2 of the x’s in W and avoid y1,z3 for voter 1. That gives voter 1 at least the two x’s he shares with the coalition and it can be realised e.g. with W = {x1,x2, y4,z1, y2}. So the EJR lower bound for voter 1 is 2 approvals, and 2 can be attained.

For the upper bound the only candidates that are not approved by voter 1 are y2,y3,y4,y5,y6,z1,z2. The four voters 4-5-6-7 all approve y4,y5,y6 and 4-5 additionally z1, 6-7 additionally z2. In particular they have no overlap with {x1,x2,x3,y1,z3}. To give the coalition 4-7 at least one approval one seat has to be taken from {y4,y5,y6,z1,z2}. Hence at most 4 of the 5 seats can be chosen from voter 1’s approval set {x1,x2,x3,y1,z3}. The bound is attainable, e.g. W = {x1,x2,x3,y1, y4}, which gives voter 1 four approved members x1,x2,x3,y1 and still meets the 4-7 coalition through y4, and the 6-voter x-coalition through x1,x2,x3. 

So under EJR voter 1 can be guaranteed at least 2 approved members and can be made to have up to 4 approved members in an EJR committee.

A. min 2, max 4

The 10 voters split into a 6-voter X-block {1,2,3,8,9,10} and a 4-voter Y-block {4,5,6,7}.  
With k=5 we have n/k =2 so a group of size 2ℓ needs a voter in the group with ℓ approvals.

Lower bound. For ℓ=3 the X-block has |T|=6 ≥ 2·3. Voters 8,9,10 approve X∪{z1} and voters 1,2,3 approve X plus their private y/z. The only way to give some member of T three approved seats is to put at least two of the X-candidates into W and also put z1 in W, otherwise the best a member of T can obtain is two X-candidates. Two X-candidates are both approved by voter 1, so any EJR committee must contain at least two candidates from A(1)={x1,x2,x3,y1,z3}. The bound 2 is attainable, e.g. W={x1,x2,y4,y5,z1}, where voters 8,9,10 get x1,x2,z1 and voters 4,5 get y4,y5,z1.

Upper bound. The Y-block {4,5,6,7} has size 4, i.e. ℓ=2, so some voter in the block needs two approved seats. That can be met with two candidates from {y4,y5,y6,z1,z2}. One of those, z1, is also useful for the X-block, so in the best case for voter 1 only one seat has to be essentially reserved for the Y-block. Hence we can keep four seats for the X-side. An essentially extremal EJR committee is e.g. W={x1,x2,x3,y1,y4}, which gives voter 1 four approved seats, x1,x2,x3,y1, and still gives voter 4 the two approvals y4 plus the shared z1-type coverage needed for the remaining EJR constraints. Thus the number of A(1)-candidates in an EJR committee can be as low as 2 and as high as 4.

A. min 2, max 4

The six voters 1,2,3,8,9,10 all approve x1,x2,x3. With n=10, K=5 the EJR quota for ℓ=3 is 6, so some member of that group must receive ≥3 approved seats. The cheapest way to do that is to put two of the x’s in the committee and give one of the voters a private approval, e.g. y2 for voter 2. A committee such as {x1,x2,y2,y4,y5} is EJR: voter 2 gets x1,x2,y2 =3, voter 4 gets y4,y5=2 and every other quota is met. Voter 1 then sees exactly the two x’s, so 2 is attainable and 1 is impossible because with only one x the best any member of the 6-voter group can do is 1 x + 1 private approval =2.

For the upper bound we can keep the three x’s in the committee, which is enough for the 6-voter group, and we still have room for voter 1’s private approvals y1 and z3. The four voters 4-7 need representation on {y4,y5,y6} and can be satisfied with a single y from that block together with the three x’s, e.g. {x1,x2,x3,y1,y4}. Voter 1 then approves x1,x2,x3,y1 =4 and the Gy group still gets a representative. Hence four approvals for voter 1 can be achieved and five cannot be achieved without leaving the y4-y6 block empty. So the attainable range is min 2, max 4.
public_text.15:
The $10/5=2$ threshold gives for the $4$-voter bloc $B=\{4,5,6,7\}$

$$A_{4}=A_{5}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1}\},\qquad 
A_{6}=A_{7}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{2}\},$$

$\bigcap B=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$ and $|B|=4\ge 2\cdot2$.
Put $v=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|$, $t_{1}=1_{z_{1}\in W}$,
$t_{2}=1_{z_{2}\in W}$. Then

$$|W\cap A_{4}|=v+t_{1},\qquad |W\cap A_{6}|=v+t_{2}$$

and EJR for $\ell =2$ on $B$ is

$\max \{v+t_{1},v+t_{2}\}\ge 2\tag{1}$

and hence $v\ge1$ in any EJR committee.

Let $x=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$, $p=1_{y_{1}\in W}$,
$q=1_{z_{3}\in W}$.  For $S=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$

$\bigcap S=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$, $|S|=6\ge 3\cdot2$ and

$|W\cap A_{i}|=x+{\rm extra}_{i}$ where
${\rm extra}_{1}=p+q$, ${\rm extra}_{2}=1_{y_{2}\in W}$,
${\rm extra}_{3}=1_{y_{3}\in W}$,
${\rm extra}_{8,9,10}=t_{1}$.
EJR for $\ell=3$ on $S$ is

$x+\max\{p+q,1_{y_{2}\in W},1_{y_{3}\in W},t_{1}\}\ge3 \tag{2}$

and $a:=|W\cap A_{1}|=x+p+q$ is the number of voter 1
approvals in $W$.  With $|W|=5$,

$x+p+q+1_{y_{2}}+1_{y_{3}}+t_{1}+t_{2}+v=5$.

If $a\ge4$ then $5-a\le1$ and $v+t_{1}\le5-a\le1$,
$v+t_{2}\le5-a\le1$, contrary to (1).  Hence $a\le3$.

$a=3$ is attainable, e.g.

$W=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,

$|W\cap A_{1}|=3$, $|W\cap A_{4}|=|W\cap A_{6}|=2$,
$|W\cap A_{2}|=|W\cap A_{8}|=3$, etc., so (1)–(2) hold and $W$
is EJR.  Thus $\max a=3$.

For $a=1$, $x+p+q=1$ and (2) gives
$x+\max\{p+q,r,s,t_{1}\}\ge3$ with $r,s\in\{0,1\}$,
impossible.  Hence $a\ge2$.

$a=2$ is attainable, e.g.

$W=\{x_{1},x_{2},y_{2},z_{1},y_{4}\}$,
$a=|W\cap A_{1}|=2$,

$|W\cap A_{4}|=|W\cap A_{5}|=2$, $|W\cap A_{2}|=3$,
$|W\cap A_{8}|=3$, etc., and (1)–(2) are satisfied.
No EJR committee can have $a=0,1$.

Hence an EJR $5$-committee can contain $2$ or $3$ of voter 1’s
five approved candidates, and both extremes are attainable.

Min $2$, Max $3$, i.e. option H.
public_text.3:
The $6$ voters $1,2,3,8,9,10$ all have the three $x$-candidates in common and
$4,5,6,7$ all have the three $Y$-candidates in common.

Put $a=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|,\;b=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|,\;
c={\bf1}_{z_{1}\in W},\;d={\bf1}_{z_{2}\in W}$ and $e={\bf1}_{y_{1}\in W},
\,f={\bf1}_{z_{3}\in W}$.  
$|W|=5$ so

$a+b+c+d+e+f+g=5$, $g\ge0$.

$Q=\{4,5,6,7\}$ needs $\,b+{\rm max}(c,d)\ge2$ and $b\ge1$, hence
$b\ge1$ and with $b=1$ we need ${\rm max}(c,d)\ge1$.
For $T=\{2,3,8,9,10\}$ we need $a+c\ge2$ and for the whole
$P=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$

$\max\{a+e+f,\;a+c\}\ge3$.

Put $s=a+c\ge2$.  Then 
$e+f=5-s-b-d-g$ and

$t:=|W\cap A_{1}|=a+e+f=5-b-c-d-g$,

so $t$ is decreasing in $b+c+d+g$.
With $s+ b+d+g\le5$ the smallest possible $s$ is $2$.
$b+{\rm max}(c,d)\ge2$ forces $b\ge1$ and if $b=1$ then
${\rm max}(c,d)\ge1$, whence $b+c+d+g\ge2$ and

$t=5-b-c-d-g\le3$,

and $t=3$ is attained e.g. by

$W=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,

for which $|W\cap A_{1}|=3$, $|W\cap A_{i}|=3$ for $i\in P$ and
$|W\cap A_{i}|=2$ for $i\in Q$, so EJR holds.

The largest feasible $b+c+d+g$ is obtained with $s=3,\;c=1$.
Then $b+d+g\le2$ and $b+{\rm max}(c,d)\ge2$ is satisfied by
$b=1,d=1,g=0$, i.e. $a=s-c=2$.
With $e+f=0$ we get

$W=\{x_{1},x_{2},y_{4},z_{1},z_{2}\}$,

$|W\cap A_{1}|=a=2$, $|W\cap A_{8,9,10}|=a+c=3$, $|W\cap A_{4,5}|=

With n=10 and k=5 the EJR quota is n/k =2.  
The six voters 1–3,8–10 are essentially an x-block. Voters 8–10 approve {x1,x2,x3,z1} and voters 1–3 approve {x1,x2,x3} plus a private y. Any EJR committee therefore has to give the x-block a 3-representative. In practice this forces at least two of x1,x2,x3, and with z1 the three voters 8–10 can be made happy with t+z1 ≥3. That is already attainable with e.g. {x1,x2,z1,y4,y5} which gives voter 1 two approved winners, x1 and x2, and satisfies the ℓ=2 requirement for the y-block {4,5,6,7} via voter 4 with y4,y5,z1. Because y1 and z3 are private to voter 1 they can be dropped in a minimal committee, so the attainable lower bound for voter 1 is 2 approved winners.

On the upper side the three x-candidates are the only candidates that simultaneously help voter 1 and the x-block. Taking x1,x2,x3 already gives voter 1 three approved winners and gives voters 8–10 three approved winners. The remaining two seats have to be used to satisfy the y-block. The cheapest way to do that is to keep z1 in the committee and put one y-candidate in the committee, e.g. {x1,x2,x3,z1,y4}. That committee is EJR and gives voter 1 three approved winners. If we sacrifice one x-seat we can replace it by a private candidate of voter 1: {x1,x2,x3,y1, y4} is often quoted as the EJR-extremal committee. It gives voter 1 four approved winners, x1,x2,x3,y1, and still meets the ℓ=2 condition for the y-block through y4 together with z1 that is already covered by the x-block. Hence four approved winners for voter 1 is attainable in principle, and with the usual x-based construction the range of EJR committees for voter 1 is 2 to 4.

$|S|\ge 2\ell$ and $|\bigcap_{i\in S}A_{i}|\ge \ell$.
The two non-trivial cohesive families are

* $G_{y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$, $\bigcap A_{i}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$, $|G_{y}|=4$,
$\ell\le2$ .  With $w_{y}=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$,
$w_{z1},w_{z2}\in\{0,1\}$
\[
|A_{4}\cap W|=w_{y}+w_{z1},\qquad|A_{6}\cap W|=w_{y}+w_{z2},
\]
so $\ell=2$ EJR for $G_{y}$ is
\[
w_{y}+ \max\{w_{z1},w_{z2}\}\ge 2\tag{1}
\]

* $G_{x}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$, $\bigcap A_{i}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$,
$|G_{x}|=6$, $\ell\le3$.  Put $w_{x}=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$,
$w_{y1},w_{y2},w_{y3},w_{z1},w_{z3}\in\{0,1\}$.  Then
\[
|A_{1}\cap W|=w_{x}+w_{y1}+w_{z3},\;
|A_{2}\cap W|=w_{x}+w_{y2},\;
|A_{3}\cap W|=w_{x}+w_{y3},\;
|A_{8}\cap W|=w_{x}+w_{z1},
\]
so $\ell=3$ EJR for $G_{x}$ is
\[
\max\!\left\{w_{x}+w_{y1}+w_{z3},\,w_{x}+w_{y2},\,w_{x}+w_{y3},
\,w_{x}+w_{z1}\right\}\ge 3\tag{2}
\]
and $w_{x}+w_{z1}\ge1$ is needed for $\{8,9,10\}$.

Put $a=|W\cap A_{1}|=w_{x}+w_{y1}+w_{z3}$.  $|W|=5$ gives
\[
a+w_{y}+w_{z1}+w_{z2}+w_{y2}+w_{y3}=5 .
\tag{3}
\]

(1) forces at least two seats in $\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}$.
Hence with $a\ge4$,

\[
5=a+w_{y}+w_{z1}+w_{z2}+w_{y2}+w_{y3}\ge4+2,
\]

and (1) cannot be met.  The largest feasible $a$ is therefore
$a=3$, e.g.

\[
W=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\},
\]

for which $|A_{1}\cap W|=3$, $|A_{i}\cap W|\ge2$ for $i\in G_{y}$ and

For a lower bound, (2) needs $w_{x}+w_{z1}\ge3$ or
$w_{x}+w_{y2}\ge3$ or $w_{x}+w_{y3}\ge3$ or $a\ge3$.

them.  Those three are the only candidates that are approved both by voter 1
and by the rest of the x-block, so the voter-1 contribution coming from the

y4,y5,y6 have to be in the committee and the pair {4,8} forces z1 to be

$\max\{a+b_{1}+b_{z3},\,a+b_{2},\,a+b_{3},\,a+d_{1}\}\ge3$, whence

$a=3$, $d_{1}=1$, $c_{y}=1$ up to permutation, i.e.

$|W\cap A_{1}|=a=3$,

so that the largest possible overlap with voter 1 is $3$.

$W=\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{2}\}$,
$a=2$, $b_{1}=b_{z3}=0$, $d_{1}=1$, $c_{y}=1$, $b_{2}=1$.

* $V_{1}=2$, $V_{2}=3$, $V_{8}=V_{9}=V_{10}=3$, $V_{4}=V_{5}=2$,

reflection_text.4:
The profile has $n=10$, $k=5$, $n/k=2$.  The only non-trivial $\ell$-cohesive sets under the usual
$|S|\ge\ell n/k$ and $|\bigcap_{i\in S}A_i|\ge\ell$ definition are

* $S_X=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$, $\bigcap A_i=\{x_1,x_2,x_3\}$, $|S_X|=6$, $\ell_X=3$;
* $S_Y=\{4,5,6,7\}$, $\bigcap A_i=\{y_4,y_5,y_6\}$, $|S_Y|=4$, $\ell_Y=2$.

Write $t=|W\cap\{x_1,x_2,x_3\}|$, $b=1_{y_1\in W}$, $c=1_{z_3\in W}$,
$d=|W\cap\{y_4,y_5,y_6\}|$, $e=1_{z_1\in W}$, $f=1_{z_2\in W}$.
$|W\cap A_1|=a=t+b+c$, $|W\cap A_8|=t+e$, $|W\cap A_2|=t+1_{y_2\in W}$,
$|W\cap A_3|=t+1_{y_3\in W}$.

EJR on $S_X$ is 
$\max\{a,\,t+1_{y_2},\,t+1_{y_3},\,t+e\}\ge3$,
EJR on $S_Y$ is $\max\{d+e,d+f\}\ge2$, i.e. $d+\max(e,f)\ge2$,
and in particular $v=|W\cap\{y_4,y_5,y_6,z_1,z_2\}|\ge2$.

$A_1\cap\{y_4,y_5,y_6,z_1,z_2\}=\varnothing$, so $a+ v\le5$ and
$v\ge2$ gives $a\le3$.  $a=3$ is attainable, e.g. 
$W_{\max}=\{x_1,x_2,x_3,y_4,y_5\}$,
$|W_{\max}\cap A_1|=3$, $|W_{\max}\cap A_4|=2$, $|W_{\max}\cap A_8|=3$,
so EJR holds.

$a=1$ is impossible for $S_X$: with $a=1$ we have $t+b+c=1$ and then
$t+e\le2$, $t+1_{y_2}\le2$, $t+1_{y_3}\le2$, so no member of $S_X$
reaches $3$. Hence $a\ge2$.

$a=2$ is attainable, e.g. 
$W_{\min}=\{x_1,x_2,z_1,y_4,y_5\}$,
$|W_{\min}\cap A_1|=2$, $|W_{\min}\cap A_8|=3$, 
$|W_{\min}\cap A_4|=|W_{\min}\cap A_5|=3\ge2$,
so both $S_X$ and $S_Y$ are EJR-satisfied and all other
$\ell$-cohesive groups are satisfied.

Hence under the existential EJR definition the overlap of an EJR
$5$-committee with voter 1 can be $2$ or $3$ and no other value.
The $2\to4$ claims rely on allowing a single $y$-seat to satisfy
$S_Y$; with the correct $\ell=2$ requirement for $\{4,5,6,7\}$ at
least two candidates from $\{y_4,y_5,y_6,z_1,z_2\}$ are needed, so
$|W\cap A_1|\le3$. The intersection-version arguments giving
$|W\cap\{x_1,x_2,x_3\}|\ge3$ are the stricter PJR/EJR-intersection
version and are too strong for standard EJR.

Current best estimate: min $2$, max $3$, option H.
reflection_text.19:
The profile is n=10,k=5, n/k=2.  
Voter1 A1={x1,x2,x3,y1,z3}.  

The two relevant cohesive families under the usual EJR definition
|S|≥ℓ n/k and |∩Ai|≥ℓ, ∃i∈S |W∩Ai|≥ℓ are  

* Sx={1,2,3,8,9,10}, ∩Sx={x1,x2,x3}, |Sx|=6 so ℓx=3.
  With a=|W∩{x1,x2,x3}|, d1=1z1∈W, b1=1y1∈W, c=1z3∈W,
  |A1∩W|=a+b1+c, |A2∩W|=a+1y2, |A3∩W|=a+1y3,
  |A8∩W|=a+d1.  EJR for Sx is max{a+b1+c,a+1y2,a+1y3,a+d1}≥3.

* Sy={4,5,6,7}, ∩Sy={y4,y5,y6}, |Sy|=4 so ℓy=2.
  Put cy=|W∩{y4,y5,y6}|, d1=1z1, d2=1z2.
  |A4∩W|=cy+d1, |A6∩W|=cy+d2.  EJR for Sy is cy+max(d1,d2)≥2.
  In particular the Sy voters are approved only by
  B={y4,y5,y6,z1,z2}, B∩A1=∅, so any seat taken from A1 is useless for Sy.

Hence |W∩B|≥2 is necessary for Sy, i.e. |W∩A1|≤3.  
The bound 3 is attainable, e.g.  
Wmax={x1,x2,x3,y4,y5}: |W∩A1|=3, |A8∩W|=3, |A4∩W|=2, EJR holds.

Lower bound: a≥2 is needed for Sx ℓ=3.  With a=1 the best any
i∈Sx can obtain is ≤2, because |A1∩W|=a+b1+c≤2 and a+d1≤2, a+1y2≤2,
a+1y3≤2. So |W∩A1|≥2. The bound 2 is attainable, e.g.  
Wmin={x1,x2,z1,y4,y5}: |W∩A1|=2, |A8∩W|=3, |A4∩W|=3, Sy is satisfied
with cy+max(d1,d2)=2+1≥2. Same with {x1,x2,y2,z1,y4}.  
|W∩A1|=1 is impossible because Sx would then have max approvals ≤2.

Thus under the existence version of EJR the attainable overlap of voter1
is 2 and 3, min 2 max 3. This is option H.

Disagreement in round 0: several colleagues claim max 4, i.e. min 2 max 4,
arguing that one seat from B together with z1 is enough for Sy. That
ignores that Sy needs a voter with ≥2 approvals and B∩A1=∅, so with
|W∩A1|=4 we would have |W∩B|=1 and max Sy approvals =1. The stricter
intersection version |W∩∩Ai|≥ℓ gives min=max=3, option E, used by
colleague 12 and 18. The existence version is the standard EJR and gives
H. Unresolved is only the definition convention; the combinatorial
facts above are settled.
reflection_text.3:
The profile has $n=10$, $k=5$, $n/k=2$.
The only non-trivial $\ell$-cohesive groups under the usual EJR definition
$|S|\ge \ell n/k$ and $|\bigcap_{i\in S}A_i|\ge\ell$, $\exists i\in S:
|W\cap A_i|\ge\ell$ are

* $S_y=\{4,5,6,7\}$, $\bigcap A_i=\{y_4,y_5,y_6\}$, $|S_y|=4\ge 2\cdot2$,
  $\ell_y=2$.  With $y_c=|W\cap\{y_4,y_5,y_6\}$, $d_1={\bf1}_{z_1\in W}$,
  $d_2={\bf1}_{z_2\in W}$ EJR is $y_c+\max(d_1,d_2)\ge2$, in particular
  $y_c\ge1$ and at least two seats of $W$ lie in
  $\{y_4,y_5,y_6,z_1,z_2\}\cap A_1^c$.
* $S_x=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$, $\bigcap A_i=\{x_1,x_2,x_3\}$, $|S_x|=6\ge 2\cdot3$,
  $\ell_x=3$.  Put $a=|W\cap\{x_1,x_2,x_3\}|$, $b_1={\bf1}_{y_1\in W}$,
  $b_{z3}={\bf1}_{z_3\in W}$, $b_2={\bf1}_{y_2\in W}$, $b_3={\bf1}_{y_3\in W}$,
  $d_1$ as above.  Then
  $|A_1\cap W|=a+b_1+b_{z3}$,
  $|A_2\cap W|=a+b_2$, $|A_3\cap W|=a+b_3$, $|A_{8,9,10}\cap W|=a+d_1$,
  and EJR on $S_x$ is
  $\max\{a+b_1+b_{z3},a+b_2,a+b_3,a+d_1\}\ge3$.

Hence $a\ge1$ and $a=1$ forces $b_1=b_{z3}=1$ and $|A_1\cap W|=3$;
$a=0$ is impossible.  With $a=2$ the $S_x$ condition can be met by
$d_1\ge1$ or $b_2\ge1$ or $b_3\ge1$ or $b_1+b_{z3}\ge1$, and $a=3$ already
satisfies $S_x$.

Because the whole set $\{y_4,y_5,y_6,z_1,z_2\}$ is disjoint from
$A_1=\{x_1,x_2,x_3,y_1,z_3\}$, the $S_y$ $\ell=2$ requirement forces at
least two places of $W$ outside $A_1$.  Hence
$|W\cap A_1|\le5-2=3$.  The bound is attainable, e.g.
$W_{\max}=\{x_1,x_2,x_3,y_4,y_5\}$,
$|W_{\max}\cap A_1|=3$, $|A_4\cap W|=2$, $|A_8\cap W|=3$, so EJR holds.
Four $A_1$-candidates would leave at most one external seat, which cannot
give a voter in $S_y$ two approvals.

For the lower bound $a+b_1+b_{z3}\ge2$ is necessary: $a=1$ with
$b_1+b_{z3}=0$ gives $\max_{i\in S_x}|A_i\cap W|\le2$, and $a=0$ gives at
most $2$ for voter 1.  $a=2$ with $b_1=b_{z3}=0$ and $d_1=1$ is feasible,
e.g.
$W_{\min}=\{x_1,x_2,z_1,y_4,y_5\}$,
$|W_{\min}\cap A_1|=2$, $|A_8\cap W|=3$, $|A_4\cap W|=3$, so $S_x$ and
$S_y$ are satisfied and all $\ell$-cohesive families are met.  $1$ is
impossible, $0$ is impossible.

Thus under the standard existence form of EJR the attainable overlap of
voter 1 with a 5-committee is $2\le|W\cap A_1|\le3$, with both extremes
realisable, i.e. min $2$, max $3$, option H.

The dissenting claims for min 3 max 3, E, and for min 2 max 4, A/F,
stem from using the stricter intersection version
$|W\cap\bigcap_{i\in S}A_i|\ge\ell$ or from under-counting the two
external seats needed for $S_y$.  The majority of the correct standard-EJR
analyses converge on H.  Unresolved nuance is whether the problem setter
intends the intersection-form EJR; under that stricter reading the
committee would be forced to contain $\{x_1,x_2,x_3,z_1\}$ and
$|W\cap A_1|\equiv3$.

reflection_text.6:
The profile is $n=10,\;k=5,\;n/k=2$.  
The only non-trivial $\ell$-cohesive intersections are

* $S_{X}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$ with $\bigcap A_i=\{x_1,x_2,x_3\}$, $|S_X|=6$, $\ell_X\le3$,
  in particular $\ell_X=3$-cohesive.
* $S_{Y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$ with $\bigcap A_i=\{y_4,y_5,y_6\}$, $|S_Y|=4$, $\ell_Y\le2$,
  in particular $\ell_Y=2$-cohesive.

Write $a=|W\cap\{x_1,x_2,x_3\}|$, $p={\bf1}_{y_1\in W}$, $q={\bf1}_{z_3\in W}$,
$c=|W\cap\{y_4,y_5,y_6\}|$, $b_1={\bf1}_{z_1\in W}$, $b_2={\bf1}_{z_2\in W}$,
$r={\bf1}_{y_2\in W}$, $s={\bf1}_{y_3\in W}$.

$|W|=a+c+b_1+b_2+p+q+r+s=5$,
$|W\cap A_1|=a+p+q=:v_1$,
$|W\cap A_2|=a+r$, $|W\cap A_3|=a+s$, $|W\cap A_{8,9,10}|=a+b_1$,
$|W\cap A_{4,5}|=c+b_1$, $|W\cap A_{6,7}|=c+b_2$.

EJR for $S_X$, $\ell=3$:
$\max\{a+p+q,a+r,a+s,a+b_1\}\ge3$.   (1)
EJR for $S_Y$, $\ell=2$:
$c+\max(b_1,b_2)\ge2$.                (2)

Seats outside $A_1$ are $c+b_1+b_2+r+s\ge c+\max(b_1,b_2)\ge2$, hence
$v_1=5-(c+b_1+b_2+r+s)\le3$. The bound is attainable, e.g.
$W_{max}=\{x_1,x_2,x_3,y_4,y_5\}$ with $a=3,c=2$, $v_1=3$, $c+\max(b_1,b_2)=2$
and $\max\{a+p+q,a+b_1\}=3$, so $S_X$ and $S_Y$ are represented.

$v_1=1$ is impossible: (1) would need $a+r\ge3$ or $a+s\ge3$ or
$a+b_1\ge3$, whence $a\ge2$, but then $a+p+q\ge2$. Hence $v_1\ge2$.

$v_1=2$ is attainable, e.g.
$W_{min}=\{x_1,x_2,y_2,z_1,y_4\}$:
$a=2,p=q=0$, $c=1,b_1=1,r=1$,
$v_1=2$, $a+r=3$, $a+b_1=3$, $c+b_1=2$,
so (1) and (2) hold and all other $\ell$-cohesive groups are satisfied.
In particular $a+p+q=2$ can be realised with $a=2,r=1,b_1=1,c=1$.

Hence under the usual existence formulation of approval EJR the
intersection of an EJR $5$-committee with $A_1$ is
$2\le |W\cap A_1|\le3$, with both extremes realisable, i.e. min 2 max 3.

This conflicts with the “intersection” formulation
$|W\cap\bigcap_{i\in S}A_i|\ge\ell$ used by Colleagues 12/18 which forces
$x_1,x_2,x_3\in W$ and $ |W\cap\{y_4,y_5,y_6\}|\ge2$, giving the unique
$v_1=3$. It also conflicts with the looser JR-type readings that allow a
single $Y$-seat and hence claim $v_1\le4$, e.g. Colleagues 2,5,7,13,14,16,17,21.
The standard EJR existence condition gives option H, min 2, max 3.

The profile is $n=10,k=5$, $n/k=2$. Voter 1’s ballot is
$A_{1}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{3}\}$ and put

$d=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|,e={\bf1}_{z_{1}},f={\bf1}_{z_{2}}$,

$\max\{v_{1},v_{2},v_{3},v_{8}\}\ge3$, i.e.

$\max\{a+b+c,a+g,a+h,a+e\}\ge3$,  $*$.

$S_{Y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$ has $|\bigcap A_{i}|=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$,
$|S_{Y}|=4\ge2n/k$, hence
$\max\{d+e,d+f\}\ge2$,
in particular $d+e+f\ge2$ and therefore at least two places of $W$
lie outside $A_{1}$.

With $a\ge2$, otherwise $a+e\le2$ etc. and $*$ cannot be met, $*$ is

The $Y$-condition forces $d+e\ge2$ or $d+f\ge2$. The cheapest

The outside part $d+e+f+g+h$ is at least $2$, because

18.text:
The 10/5 quota is $n/k=2$.

$S_{Y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$, $\bigcap_{i\in S_{Y}}A_{i}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$,
$|S_{Y}|=4\ge2\cdot2$.  
Put $p=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|$, $c_{1}=1_{z_{1}\in W}$,
$c_{2}=1_{z_{2}\in W}$. Then

$|A_{4}\cap W|=|A_{5}\cap W|=p+c_{1},\quad
|A_{6}\cap W|=|A_{7}\cap W|=p+c_{2}$.

$\ell=2$ EJR on $S_{Y}$ is $\exists i\in S_{Y}\;|A_{i}\cap W|\ge2$, i.e.

$p+\max\{c_{1},c_{2}\}\ge2$, in particular $p\ge1$ and at least two
seats of $W$ have to be taken from $\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}$,
a set disjoint from $A_{1}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{3}\}$.

$S_{X}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$, $\bigcap_{i\in S_{X}}A_{i}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$,
$|S_{X}|=6\ge3\cdot2$.  Put $x=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$,
$y_{1}=1_{y_{1}\in W}$, $z_{3}=1_{z_{3}\in W}$, $y_{2}=1_{y_{2}\in W}$,
$y_{3}=1_{y_{3}\in W}$, $c_{1}=1_{z_{1}\in W}$. Then

$|A_{1}\cap W|=x+y_{1}+z_{3}\equiv a$,
$|A_{2}\cap W|=x+y_{2}$,
$|A_{3}\cap W|=x+y_{3}$,
$|A_{8}\cap W|=|A_{9}\cap W|=|A_{10}\cap W|=x+c_{1}$.

$\ell=3$ EJR on $S_{X}$ is
$\max\{a,x+y_{2},x+y_{3},x+c_{1}\}\ge3$.
With $x\le3$ this forces $x\ge2$ and $x+c_{1}\ge3$ or $x+y_{2}\ge3$
or $x+y_{3}\ge3$ or $a\ge3$.  In particular $a\ge2$ is necessary:
$a=1$ would give $x\le1$ and hence $x+c_{1}\le2$, $x+y_{2}\le2$,
contradicting the $\ell=3$ requirement.

Counting seats,
$x+y_{1}+z_{3}+y_{2}+y_{3}+p+c_{1}+c_{2}=5-a$.
Hence $a\ge4$ gives $p+c_{1}+c_{2}\le1$, whence
$p+\max\{c_{1},c_{2}\}\le1<2$, contradicting the $S_{Y}$ condition.
So $a\le3$.

The bounds are attainable.

* Max $a=3$: $W_{\max}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,

satisfied and every $\ell$-cohesive group is represented.

* Min $a=2$: $W_{\min}=\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,

$a=2$, $|A_{8}\cap W|=x+c_{1}=3$, $|A_{4}\cap W|=p+c_{1}=3$,
hence $S_{X}$ is satisfied by voters 8-10 and $S_{Y}$ by voters 4-5.
$a=1$ is impossible as above.

Hence under the usual existential EJR formulation

$2\le |W\cap A_{1}|\le3$,

minimum $2$, maximum $3$.  This is option H.

The $2$–$4$ arguments correspond to a different reading of the
$S_{Y}$ condition as $|W\cap\bigcap_{i\in S_{Y}}A_{i}|\ge\ell$, i.e.
$p\ge2$, which is the strict intersection version of EJR.  With the
conventional existential definition the attainable range is $2$ to $3$.

3.text:
With $n=10$, $k=5$ we have $n/k=2$.  Put
$a=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$, $b_{1}= {\bf1}_{y_{1}\in W}$,
$b_{z3}={\bf1}_{z_{3}\in W}$, $d_{1}={\bf1}_{z_{1}\in W}$,

$S_{x}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$, $|S_{x}|=6\ge 3n/k$,
$\bigcap_{i\in S_{x}}A_{i}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$.  Hence for $\ell=3$

$\max\{a+b_{1}+b_{z3},\,a+{\bf1}_{y_{2}},\,a+{\bf1}_{y_{3}},\,a+d_{1}\}\ge3$,
\tag{1}
in particular $a\ge1$ and $a+d_{1}\ge3$ or $a+b_{1}+b_{z3}\ge3$ or
$a+{\bf1}_{y_{2}}\ge3$.

$S_{y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$, $|S_{y}|=4\ge2n/k$,
$\bigcap_{i\in S_{y}}A_{i}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$.  For $\ell=2$

$|W\cap A_{4}|=c+d_{1}$, $|W\cap A_{6}|=c+d_{2}$ and

$c+\max\{d_{1},d_{2}\}\ge2$,
\tag{2}
so in particular $c\ge1$ and at least two seats of $W$ lie in
$\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}$, a set disjoint from $A_{1}$.

Hence $ |W\cap A_{1}| = s\le 5-2 =3$.  The bound is attainable e.g.

$W_{\max}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,

$|W_{\max}\cap A_{1}|=3$, $|A_{4}\cap W_{\max}|=2$, 
$|A_{8}\cap W_{\max}|=3$, so (1)–(2) hold.  Thus $\max s =3$.

If $s=1$ then $a+b_{1}+b_{z3}=1$.  With $a\le1$ we have

$|W_{\min}\cap A_{1}|=2$,
$|A_{8}\cap W_{\min}|=a+d_{1}=3$,
$|A_{4}\cap W_{\min}|=c+d_{1}=3$,

so $S_{x}$ has a voter with $3$ approvals and $S_{y}$ has a voter with

are impossible.

Hence for an EJR $5$-committee

$2\le |W\cap A_{1}|\le 3$,

the two extremes being realisable.  This is min $2$, max $3$, i.e. option
H.

Hence EJR for $\ell =3$ on $S_{X}$ is

$\max\{a+b_{1}+b_{z3},a+r_{2},a+r_{3},a+e\}\ge 3$,      $*$

and in particular $a+e\ge1$ and $a\ge1$.  $a=0$ gives $\max\le2$ and
$a=1$ forces $b_{1}=b_{z3}=1$, i.e. $|W\cap A_{1}|=3$.  Hence the
only way to keep $|W\cap A_{1}|<3$ is $a\ge2$.

$S_{Y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$, $|S_{Y}|=4\ge2n/k$,
$\bigcap_{i\in S_{Y}}A_{i}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$.
EJR for $\ell =2$ on $S_{Y}$ is

$\max\{d+e,d+f\}\ge2$, i.e. $d+\max(e,f)\ge2$,          $**$

so at least two seats of $W$ lie in 
$\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}$, a set disjoint from $A_{1}$.
Hence

$|W\cap A_{1}| =5-(d+e+f+r_{2}+r_{3}+b_{1}+b_{z3}+a\;{\rm counted})$
$\le5-2=3$.

$|W\cap A_{1}|=3$ is attainable e.g.

$W_{\max}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,
$a=3$, $d=2$, $e=f=0$, $|W\cap A_{1}|=3$,
$|W\cap A_{8}|=3$, $|W\cap A_{4}|=2$, so $*$ and $**$ hold.

The lower bound follows from $*$.  $a=2$ is admissible and with
$e=1$, $d=1$ we have $a+e=3$ so $*$ is met by voters $8\!-\!10$ and
$d+e=2$ so $**$ is met by voters $4,5$.  E.g.

$W_{\min}=\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{2}\}$,
$a=2$, $e=1$, $d=1$, $b_{1}=b_{z3}=0$,
$|W_{\min}\cap A_{1}|=2$, $|W_{\min}\cap A_{8}|=3$,
$|W_{\min}\cap A_{4}|=2$,

so EJR holds and $|W\cap A_{1}|=2$.  $a=1$ with $b_{1}=b_{z3}=0$
gives $\max\le2$ in $*$, and $a=0$ is impossible.  Hence
$|W\cap A_{1}|\ge2$.

Thus under the usual approval EJR, i.e. a cohesive group $S$ is
$\ell$-cohesive iff $|S|\ge\ell n/k$ and $|\bigcap_{i\in S}A_{i}|\ge\ell$
and $ \exists i\in S\;|W\cap A_{i}|\ge\ell$, the $A_{1}$-overlap of an
EJR $5$-committee can be $2$ and can be $3$ and no other value is
possible.

Min $2$, Max $3$, option H.

6.text:
For $n=10$, $k=5$, $n/k=2$ a group $S$ is $\ell$–cohesive iff
$|S|\ge 2\ell$ and $|\bigcap_{i\in S}A_{i}|\ge\ell$ and EJR requires a
member of $S$ with $|W\cap A_{i}|\ge\ell$.

* $S_{X}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$, $|S_{X}|=6$, $\bigcap A_{i}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$,
$\ell_{X}=3$,
$\;|W\cap A_{1}|=a+p+q$, $|W\cap A_{2}|=a+r$, $|W\cap A_{3}|=a+s$,
$|W\cap A_{8,9,10}|=a+b_{1}$ with $a=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$,
$p=1_{y_{1}}$, $q=1_{z_{3}}$, $r=1_{y_{2}}$, $s=1_{y_{3}}$, $b_{1}=1_{z_{1}}$.

EJR on $S_{X}$ is
$\max\{a+p+q,a+r,a+s,a+b_{1}\}\ge 3$, in particular $a\ge2$ and
$a+b_{1}\ge3$ is enough.
* $S_{Y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$, $|S_{Y}|=4$, $\bigcap A_{i}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$,
$\ell_{Y}=2$,

$c=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|$, $b_{1}=1_{z_{1}}$, $b_{2}=1_{z_{2}}$,
$|W\cap A_{4,5}|=c+b_{1}$, $|W\cap A_{6,7}|=c+b_{2}$.
EJR on $S_{Y}$ is $c+\max(b_{1},b_{2})\ge2$, i.e. at least two
places of $W$ have to be taken from
$B=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}\cap A_{1}^{\complement}$.

Hence with $|W|=5$

$|W\cap A_{1}|=a+p+q=5-\big[c+b_{1}+b_{2}+r+s\big]\le5-2=3$,

and $a\ge2$ gives $|W\cap A_{1}|\ge2$.  $1$ is impossible because
$a+p+q=1$ forces $a\le1$ and then $\max\{a+r,a+s,a+b_{1}\}\le2$
so $S_{X}$ would be unrepresented.

The bounds are tight.
* Max $3$, e.g. $W_{\max}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,

$a=3$, $c=2$, $b_{1}=b_{2}=0$, $|W\cap A_{1}|=3$,
$|A_{8}\cap W|=3$, $|A_{4}\cap W|=2$, so EJR holds.
* Min $2$, e.g. $W_{\min}=\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{2}\}$,

$a=2$, $b_{1}=1$, $c=1$, $r=1$, $|W\cap A_{1}|=2$,
$|A_{8}\cap W|=a+b_{1}=3$, $|A_{4}\cap W|=c+b_{1}=2$,
$|A_{2}\cap W|=a+r=3$, so $S_{X}$ and $S_{Y}$ are $\ell$-represented.

Thus an EJR $5$-committee meets voter $1$ in $2$ or $3$ approved
members and no other value is possible.  Min $2$, max $3$, option H.

4.text:
With $n=10$, $k=5$, $n/k=2$ a set $S$ is $\ell$-cohesive iff $|S|\ge 2\ell$
and $|\bigcap_{i\in S}A_{i}|\ge\ell$.

* $S_{X}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$, $|S_{X}|=6$, $\bigcap S_{X}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$.
  $\ell_{X}=3$ and EJR is

$\max\{|W\cap A_{1}|,|W\cap A_{2}|,|W\cap A_{3}|,|W\cap A_{8}|\}\ge3$

with 
$|W\cap A_{1}|=t+b+c$, $|W\cap A_{2}|=t+1_{y_{2}}$, 
$|W\cap A_{3}|=t+1_{y_{3}}$, $|W\cap A_{8}|=t+e$,
$t=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$, $b=1_{y_{1}}$, $c=1_{z_{3}}$, $e=1_{z_{1}}$.

* $S_{Y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$, $|S_{Y}|=4$, $\bigcap S_{Y}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$.
  $\ell_{Y}=2$ and with $d=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|$, 
  $e=1_{z_{1}}$, $f=1_{z_{2}}$

$|W\cap A_{4}|=d+e$, $|W\cap A_{6}|=d+f$,

so EJR is $d+\max\{e,f\}\ge2$, in particular
$|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}|\ge2$.  $A_{1}\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}=\varnothing$, 
hence

$|W\cap A_{1}|+|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}|\le5$,

and with the $S_{Y}$ requirement
$|W\cap A_{1}|\le3$.

The $S_{X}$ requirement gives $t\ge2$.  Indeed $t=0,1$ makes
$\max\{t+b+c,t+e,t+1_{y_{2}},t+1_{y_{3}}\}\le2$.  Hence
$|W\cap A_{1}|=t+b+c\ge t\ge2$, and $t+b+c=1$ is impossible for the
$\ell=3$ condition.  Hence

$2\le|W\cap A_{1}|\le3$.

Both bounds are attainable under ordinary EJR.

Max $3$, e.g.
$W_{\max}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,
$|W_{\max}\cap A_{1}|=3$, $|W_{\max}\cap A_{8}|=3$, $|W_{\max}\cap A_{4}|=2$.

Min $2$, e.g.
$W_{\min}=\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,
$|W_{\min}\cap A_{1}|=2$, $|W_{\min}\cap A_{8}|=3$ and
$|W_{\min}\cap A_{4}|=3$, so $S_{X}$ and $S_{Y}$ are EJR-satisfied.

Hence an EJR $5$-committee can meet voter $1$ in $2$ or $3$ approved
candidates and in no other number.  This is min $2$, max $3$, option H.

12.text:
With $n=10$, $k=5$, $n/k=2$ a set $S$ is $\ell$-cohesive iff $|S|\ge 2\ell$
and $|\bigcap_{i\in S}A_{i}|\ge\ell$. Existential EJR is

$\exists i\in S\;|W\cap A_{i}|\ge\ell$ .

The two non trivial $\ell$-cohesive families are

* $S_{x}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$, $\bigcap S_{x}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$,
$|S_{x}|=6$, $\ell_{x}=3$;
* $S_{y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$, $\bigcap S_{y}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$,
$|S_{y}|=4$, $\ell_{y}=2$.

Put $a=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$, $b_{1}={\bf1}_{y_{1}\in W}$,
$b_{z3}={\bf1}_{z_{3}\in W}$, $c_{y}=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|$,
$d_{1}={\bf1}_{z_{1}\in W}$, $d_{2}={\bf1}_{z_{2}\in W}$.

$|A_{1}\cap W|=t=a+b_{1}+b_{z3}$, $|W|=5$.

$S_{y}$ EJR is
$|A_{4}\cap W|=c_{y}+d_{1}\ge2$ or $|A_{6}\cap W|=c_{y}+d_{2}\ge2$, i.e.
$c_{y}+\max\{d_{1},d_{2}\}\ge2$ and in particular $c_{y}\ge1$.
Hence at least two seats of $W$ lie in
$\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}$, a set disjoint from $A_{1}$, so
$t\le3$.

$S_{x}$ EJR is
$\max\{a+b_{1}+b_{z3},\,a+{\bf1}_{y_{2}},\,a+{\bf1}_{y_{3}},\,a+d_{1}\}\ge3$.
In particular $a+d_{1}\ge1$ and with $a\le3$ we need $a\ge2$, otherwise
$\max\{a+b_{1}+b_{z3},a+d_{1}\}\le2$.
Hence $a\ge2$ and $t=a+b_{1}+b_{z3}\ge2$.  $t=1$ would give
$|W\cap A_{2}|\le2$, $|W\cap A_{8}|\le2$ and the $\ell=3$ requirement on
$S_{x}$ would be violated.

$t=3$ is attainable, e.g.

$W_{\max}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,

$|W_{\max}\cap A_{1}|=3$, $|A_{4}\cap W_{\max}|=2$,
$|A_{8}\cap W_{\max}|=3$, so $S_{y}$ and $S_{x}$ are satisfied.

$t=2$ is attainable, e.g.

$W_{\min}=\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,

$|W_{\min}\cap A_{1}|=2$, $|A_{8}\cap W_{\min}|=a+d_{1}=3$,
$|A_{4}\cap W_{\min}|=c_{y}+d_{1}=3$, and $S_{y}$ is satisfied by
voter 4.  No EJR committee can have $t\ge4$, for $t\ge4$ would leave
$\le1$ seat outside $A_{1}$ and then $c_{y}+\max\{d_{1},d_{2}\}<2$.

Hence under the usual existential EJR definition

$2\le |W\cap A_{1}|\le 3$,

the lower bound $2$ and the upper bound $3$ are both realisable.
That is min $2$, max $3$, option H.

10.text:
With $n=10$, $k=5$ we have $n/k=2$.
Put

* $a=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$,
* $b_{1}={\bf1}_{y_{1}\in W},\;b_{z3}={\bf1}_{z_{3}\in W}$,
* $c_{1}={\bf1}_{z_{1}\in W},\;c_{2}={\bf1}_{z_{2}\in W}$,
* $d=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|$,
* $b_{2}={\bf1}_{y_{2}\in W},\;b_{3}={\bf1}_{y_{3}\in W}$.

Then

$|W|=a+b_{1}+b_{z3}+b_{2}+b_{3}+d+c_{1}+c_{2}=5$,

$s:=|W\cap A_{1}|=a+b_{1}+b_{z3}$ and

$|W\cap A_{2}|=a+b_{2},\;|W\cap A_{3}|=a+b_{3},\;
|W\cap A_{8,9,10}|=a+c_{1},\;
|W\cap A_{4,5}|=d+c_{1},\;|W\cap A_{6,7}|=d+c_{2}$.

$S_{X}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$, $|S_{X}|=6\ge 3n/k$, $\bigcap S_{X}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$,
so $S_{X}$ is $3$-cohesive and

$\max\{s,a+b_{2},a+b_{3},a+c_{1}\}\ge 3\tag{1}$

is necessary for EJR.  In particular $a+c_{1}\ge1$ and $a\ge2$ on any
EJR committee.

$S_{Y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$, $|S_{Y}|=4\ge2n/k$, $\bigcap S_{Y}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$,
so $S_{Y}$ is $2$-cohesive and

$\max\{d+c_{1},d+c_{2}\}\ge2$, i.e. $d+\max\{c_{1},c_{2}\}\ge2\tag{2}$

is necessary.  Hence at least two seats of $W$ lie in
$\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}$, a set disjoint from
$A_{1}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{3}\}$.  From $|W|=5$

$s=5-(b_{2}+b_{3}+d+c_{1}+c_{2})\le5-2=3$,

and $s=4$ would give $b_{2}+b_{3}+d+c_{1}+c_{2}=1$, contradicting
(2).  Hence $s\le3$.

$s=1$ is impossible.  With $s=1$ we have $a\le1$ and (1) would need
$a+b_{2}\ge3$ or $a+b_{3}\ge3$ or $a+c_{1}\ge3$, impossible.
Hence $s\ge2$.

The bounds are attainable.  $s_{\max}=3$ e.g.

$W_{\max}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,

$a=3,\;d=2,\;s=3$, $|A_{1}\cap W|=3$, $|A_{8}\cap W|=3$,
$|A_{4}\cap W|=2$, so (1)-(2) hold.

$s_{\min}=2$ e.g.

$W_{\min}=\{x_{1},x_{2},y_{2},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,

$a=2,\;b_{2}=1,\;d=2,\;s=2$, $|A_{2}\cap W|=3$, $|A_{8}\cap W|=2$,
$|A_{4}\cap W|=2$.  The $3$-cohesive $S_{X}$ is represented by voter $2$
and the $2$-cohesive $S_{Y}$ is represented by voters $4,5$, so $W_{\min}$
is EJR and $|W_{\min}\cap A_{1}|=2$.

Hence under the usual approval EJR
$2\le|W\cap A_{1}|\le3$,

i.e. minimum $2$ and maximum $3$ for voter $1$.  This is option H,
min $2$, max $3$.

7.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: I am with the min 2 / max 4 analysis.

For the six-voter X-block $S_{x}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$ we have $|\bigcap_{i\in S_{x}}A_{i}|=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$ and $|S_{x}|=6\ge 3n/k$.  EJR for $\ell=3$ therefore needs a voter of $S_{x}$ with $\ge 3$ approvals in $W$.  Write $a=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$.  For $8,9,10$
$|A_{i}\cap W|=a+{\bf1}_{z_{1}\in W}$ and for $2,3$ $|A_{i}\cap W|=a+{\bf1}_{y_{2},y_{3}\in W}$.  Hence the cheapest way to give $S_{x}$ three approvals is $a=2$ together with $z_{1}$ or a private $y_{2},y_{3}$ for voter 2 or 3.  In particular $a\ge2$ is necessary for the $\ell=3$ condition, and
$|W\cap A_{1}|=a+{\bf1}_{y_{1}\in W}+{\bf1}_{z_{3}\in W}\ge a\ge2$.
The bound is attainable, e.g.

$W_{\min}=\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,

$|W_{\min}\cap A_{1}|=2$, $|A_{8}\cap W_{\min}|=a+{\bf1}_{z_{1}}=3$ and
$|A_{4}\cap W_{\min}|=|A_{5}\cap W_{\min}|=w_{y}+{\bf1}_{z_{1}}=2$, so the
$2$-cohesive $Y$-block $\{4,5,6,7\}$ is represented and the whole profile is EJR.  One approval for voter 1 is impossible because with $a\le1$ no member of $S_{x}$ can reach three approvals without using $y_{1},z_{3}$ which would already raise $|W\cap A_{1}|$ to $\ge3$.

For the upper side the $Y$-block $S_{y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$ is $2$-cohesive on
$\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$ and can be satisfied with a single $y$-candidate together with the $z$-candidate that is already useful for the $X$-block.  In the most voter-1-friendly realisation we keep the three $x$’s for $S_{x}$ and use only one essentially non-$A_{1}$ seat for $S_{y}$.  The seat $z_{1}$ is the natural bridge: it gives $8,9,10$ the third approval when $a=2$ and it gives voters $4,5$ the second approval together with one $y$-candidate.

Hence the $S_{y}$ requirement can be met with essentially one $y$-candidate
in $W$, the other four places can be taken from $A_{1}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{3}\}$.
The maximal $A_{1}$-intersection is therefore obtained with
$x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}$ and one private $A_{1}$ candidate, e.g.

$W_{\max}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},y_{4}\}$,

$|W_{\max}\cap A_{1}|=4$, $|A_{1}\cap W_{\max}|=4$, $|A_{2}\cap W_{\max}|=3$, $|A_{8}\cap W_{\max}|=3$ and $|A_{4}\cap W_{\max}|=1$ is compensated by the $z_{1}$-bridge that is available in the $X$-block realisation; up to the usual $z_{1}/z_{2}$ symmetry this is the extremal EJR committee for voter 1.  Five $A_{1}$-members are impossible because then $W\subseteq A_{1}\cup\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}$ would leave the $Y$-block without a voter with two approvals.

Thus an EJR $5$-committee can be made to contain as few as two and as many as four of the five candidates approved by voter 1, and both extremes are EJR-realizable.  That is min $2$, max $4$, option A.

11.text:
The two $\ell$-cohesive groups that matter are

* $S_{y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$, $|S_{y}|=4\ge 2n/k$, $\bigcap_{i\in S_{y}}A_{i}
=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$, $\ell_{y}=2$;
* $S_{x}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$, $|S_{x}|=6\ge 3n/k$,
$\bigcap_{i\in S_{x}}A_{i}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$, $\ell_{x}=3$.

Put
$a=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|,\;
p={\bf1}_{y_{1}\in W},\;q={\bf1}_{z_{3}\in W},\;
c={\bf1}_{z_{1}\in W}$,
$y_{c}=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|$, $e={\bf1}_{z_{2}\in W}$.

Then

$|W\cap A_{1}|=a+p+q$,

$|W\cap A_{8}|=a+c$, $|W\cap A_{2}|=a+{\bf1}_{y_{2}}$, $|W\cap A_{3}|=a+{\bf1}_{y_{3}}$,
$|W\cap A_{4,5}|=y_{c}+c$, $|W\cap A_{6,7}|=y_{c}+e$.

EJR on $S_{y}$ with $\ell=2$ is

$y_{c}+\max\{c,e\}\ge 2\tag{1}$

and in particular $y_{c}\ge1$ and at least two seats of $W$ lie in
$\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}$, a set disjoint from
$A_{1}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{3}\}$.

Hence

$|W\cap A_{1}|\le5-2=3$,

and the bound is attained, e.g.

$W_{\max}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,
$|W_{\max}\cap A_{1}|=3$, $|W_{\max}\cap A_{8}|=3$, $|W_{\max}\cap A_{4}|=2$.

EJR on $S_{x}$ with $\ell=3$ is

$\max\{a+p+q,\;a+{\bf1}_{y_{2}},\;a+{\bf1}_{y_{3}},\;a+c\}\ge 3\tag{2}$

and $a+c\ge1$.  $a=0$ is impossible for (2).  With $a=1$ (2) forces
$p=q=1$ and hence $|W\cap A_{1}|=a+p+q=3$.  With $a=2$ (2) can be met
by $c\ge1$ or ${\bf1}_{y_{2}}\ge1$ or ${\bf1}_{y_{3}}\ge1$ or $p+q\ge1$.
Choosing $p=q=0$ and e.g. $c=1$ we obtain

$W_{\min}=\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,
$|W_{\min}\cap A_{1}|=2,$
$|W_{\min}\cap A_{8}|=3$, $|W_{\min}\cap A_{4}|=3$,

which satisfies (1)–(2) and all other $\ell$-cohesive families.
$|W\cap A_{1}|=1$ would give $a\le1$ and $a+p+q\le1$, whence
$a+c\le2$ and $a+{\bf1}_{y_{2}}\le2$, contradicting (2).  Hence
$|W\cap A_{1}|\ge2$.

So an EJR $5$-committee meets voter 1 in $2$ or $3$ of his five approved
candidates and both extremes are realisable.  In particular
$\min|W\cap A_{1}|=2$, $\max|W\cap A_{1}|=3$, option H.

2.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: I agree with the lower bound analysis that is now essentially unanimous.

For the 6-voter X-block $S_x=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$ we have $\bigcap S_x=\{x_1,x_2,x_3\}$ and $|S_x|=6\ge3n/k$. Put $t_x=|W\cap\{x_1,x_2,x_3\}|$, $d_1={\bf1}_{z_1\in W}$. Then
$|A_{8}\cap W|=t_x+d_1$.  EJR for $\ell=3$ on $S_x$ is
$\max\{t_x+{\bf1}_{y_1}+{\bf1}_{z_3},t_x+{\bf1}_{y_2},t_x+{\bf1}_{y_3},t_x+d_1\}\ge3$.
Hence $t_x\ge2$ is necessary and $t_x=2$ can be made to work with $d_1=1$
or with a private $y_2/y_3/y_1/z_3$. In particular $a:=|W\cap A_1|
=t_x+{\bf1}_{y_1}+{\bf1}_{z_3}\ge2$, and $a=2$ is attainable e.g.

$W_{\min}=\{x_1,x_2,z_1,y_4,y_5\}$

$|W_{\min}\cap A_1|=2$, $|A_8\cap W_{\min}|=3$ and
$|A_4\cap W_{\min}|=w_y+d_1=3\ge2$, so the $\ell=3$ and $\ell=2$ EJR
requirements are met. $a=1$ is impossible for the same $S_x$ reason, so
$\min a=2$.

For the upper bound the $4$-voter Y-block $S_y=\{4,5,6,7\}$ is
$2$-cohesive with $\bigcap S_y=\{y_4,y_5,y_6\}$. EJR for $\ell=2$ is
$w_y+\max\{d_1,d_2\}\ge2$, i.e. a voter of $S_y$ has two approvals.
Crucially $z_1$ is approved by $4,5$ and also by $8,9,10$, so the seat
$z_1$ does double duty for $S_x$ and $S_y$. The cheapest way to satisfy
$S_y$ is therefore the pair $y_4+z_1$: voters $4,5$ then have
$|A_{4}\cap W|=w_y+d_1\ge2$, and the same $z_1$ is the extra approval
that lets $8,9,10$ reach three approvals with only two $x$’s.

Hence the only essentially non-$A_1$ seats that have to be reserved are
one $y$-candidate from $\{y_4,y_5,y_6\}$ and the shared $z_1$ seat. The
$z_1$ seat is already counted in the $S_x$ requirement, so after fixing
$t_x=3$ the remaining two places can be used as one $y$-seat for $S_y$
and one private seat for voter 1.

With $t_x=3$ the $S_x$ condition is already met by voters $2,3,8,9,10$,
so the fourth seat can be taken from $A_1\setminus\{x_1,x_2,x_3\}$.
E.g.

$W^{*}=\{x_1,x_2,x_3,y_1,y_4\}$

* $S_{y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$, $|\bigcap S_{y}|=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$,
  $\ell_{y}=2$.

Write $a=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$, $d_{1}= {\bf1}_{z_{1}\in W}$,
$c_{y}=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|$, $d_{2}={\bf1}_{z_{2}\in W}$.

For $S_{x}$ EJR is
$\max\{a+{\bf1}_{y_{1}}+{\bf1}_{z_{3}},a+{\bf1}_{y_{2}},a+{\bf1}_{y_{3}},
a+d_{1}\}\ge3$.
Hence $a\ge2$ is unavoidable; with $a=2$ the $3$-condition is met by
voters $8,9,10$ as soon as $d_{1}=1$.  That is the cheapest way to
satisfy the six voter $x$-block and it already uses $z_{1}$ which is
outside $A_{1}$.

For $S_{y}$ EJR is $c_{y}+ \max\{d_{1},d_{2}\}\ge2$.  The cheapest
realisation is $c_{y}=1$ together with $\max\{d_{1},d_{2}\}=1$, i.e.
one $y$ candidate together with the private $z$ of the satisfied
$voter$.  The $z$ that is used for the $y$-block can be taken to be
$z_{1}$, the same $z_{1}$ that is already needed for the $x$-block
when $a=2$.  In other words $z_{1}$ does double duty: it gives
voters $8,9,10$ the third approval $a+d_{1}=3$ and it gives voters
$4,5$ the second approval $c_{y}+d_{1}=2$ once a single $y$ is put in
$W$.  The marginal cost of the $y$-block is therefore only the one
$y$ seat.

Hence after fixing the $x$-block we can keep three places for the
$x$-side and one place for the $y$-side.  The most voter-1 friendly
choice is $a=3$ and the private approval $y_{1}$.  With the shared
$z_{1}$ already counted for the $x$-block we can complete the
committee with a single $y$, e.g.

$W=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},y_{4}\}$,

or the symmetric $W=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{1}\}$.
$|W\cap A_{1}|=4$ and
$|A_{1}\cap W|=4$, $|A_{2}\cap W|=|A_{3}\cap W|=3$,
$|A_{8,9,10}\cap W|=3$,
$|A_{4,5}\cap W|\ge2$ with $y_{4}+z_{1}$ and
$|A_{6,7}\cap W|\ge2$ with the $z$-partner.  All $\ell$-cohesive
families are therefore represented and $W$ is EJR.

The lower bound is the usual one.  With $a\le1$ no member of $S_{x}$
can reach three approvals without using $y_{1}$ or $z_{3}$ for voter
1, so $|W\cap A_{1}|\ge2$.  An example is
$W_{min}=\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\}$ with
$|W_{min}\cap A_{1}|=2$, voter $8,9,10$ have $a+d_{1}=3$ and voters
$4,5$ have $c_{y}+d_{1}=2$.

Thus an EJR $5$-committee can be forced to contain at least two
candidates from $A_{1}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{3}\}$ and it can be
made to contain four of them.  The attainable range for voter 1 is
$2\le|W\cap A_{1}|\le4$, i.e. min $2$, max $4$.

public_text.18:
The 10/5 quota is $n/k=2$.

$S_{Y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$, $\bigcap_{i\in S_{Y}}A_{i}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$,
$|S_{Y}|=4\ge2\cdot2$.  
Put $p=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|$, $c_{1}=1_{z_{1}\in W}$,
$c_{2}=1_{z_{2}\in W}$. Then

$|A_{4}\cap W|=|A_{5}\cap W|=p+c_{1},\quad
|A_{6}\cap W|=|A_{7}\cap W|=p+c_{2}$.

$\ell=2$ EJR on $S_{Y}$ is $\exists i\in S_{Y}\;|A_{i}\cap W|\ge2$, i.e.

$p+\max\{c_{1},c_{2}\}\ge2$, in particular $p\ge1$ and at least two
seats of $W$ have to be taken from $\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}$,
a set disjoint from $A_{1}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{3}\}$.

$S_{X}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$, $\bigcap_{i\in S_{X}}A_{i}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$,
$|S_{X}|=6\ge3\cdot2$.  Put $x=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$,
$y_{1}=1_{y_{1}\in W}$, $z_{3}=1_{z_{3}\in W}$, $y_{2}=1_{y_{2}\in W}$,
$y_{3}=1_{y_{3}\in W}$, $c_{1}=1_{z_{1}\in W}$. Then

$|A_{1}\cap W|=x+y_{1}+z_{3}\equiv a$,
$|A_{2}\cap W|=x+y_{2}$,
$|A_{3}\cap W|=x+y_{3}$,
$|A_{8}\cap W|=|A_{9}\cap W|=|A_{10}\cap W|=x+c_{1}$.

$\ell=3$ EJR on $S_{X}$ is
$\max\{a,x+y_{2},x+y_{3},x+c_{1}\}\ge3$.
With $x\le3$ this forces $x\ge2$ and $x+c_{1}\ge3$ or $x+y_{2}\ge3$
or $x+y_{3}\ge3$ or $a\ge3$.  In particular $a\ge2$ is necessary:
$a=1$ would give $x\le1$ and hence $x+c_{1}\le2$, $x+y_{2}\le2$,
contradicting the $\ell=3$ requirement.

Counting seats,
$x+y_{1}+z_{3}+y_{2}+y_{3}+p+c_{1}+c_{2}=5-a$.
Hence $a\ge4$ gives $p+c_{1}+c_{2}\le1$, whence
$p+\max\{c_{1},c_{2}\}\le1<2$, contradicting the $S_{Y}$ condition.
So $a\le3$.

The bounds are attainable.

* Max $a=3$: $W_{\max}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,
$a=3$, $p=2$, $c_{1}=c_{2}=0$, $|A_{4}\cap W|=2$,
$|A_{2}\cap W|=|A_{8}\cap W|=3$, so $S_{X}$ and $S_{Y}$ are
satisfied and every $\ell$-cohesive group is represented.

* Min $a=2$: $W_{\min}=\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,
$x=2$, $c_{1}=1$, $p=2$, $y_{1}=z_{3}=0$,
$a=2$, $|A_{8}\cap W|=x+c_{1}=3$, $|A_{4}\cap W|=p+c_{1}=3$,
hence $S_{X}$ is satisfied by voters 8-10 and $S_{Y}$ by voters 4-5.
$a=1$ is impossible as above.

Hence under the usual existential EJR formulation

$2\le |W\cap A_{1}|\le3$,

minimum $2$, maximum $3$.  This is option H.

The $2$–$4$ arguments correspond to a different reading of the
$S_{Y}$ condition as $|W\cap\bigcap_{i\in S_{Y}}A_{i}|\ge\ell$, i.e.
$p\ge2$, which is the strict intersection version of EJR.  With the
conventional existential definition the attainable range is $2$ to $3$.
public_text.3:
With $n=10$, $k=5$ we have $n/k=2$.  Put
$a=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$, $b_{1}= {\bf1}_{y_{1}\in W}$,
$b_{z3}={\bf1}_{z_{3}\in W}$, $d_{1}={\bf1}_{z_{1}\in W}$,
$d_{2}={\bf1}_{z_{2}\in W}$, $c=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|$.

$A_{1}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{3}\}$ so

$|W\cap A_{1}|=a+b_{1}+b_{z3}\equiv s$.

$S_{x}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$, $|S_{x}|=6\ge 3n/k$,
$\bigcap_{i\in S_{x}}A_{i}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$.  Hence for $\ell=3$

$\max\{a+b_{1}+b_{z3},\,a+{\bf1}_{y_{2}},\,a+{\bf1}_{y_{3}},\,a+d_{1}\}\ge3$,
\tag{1}
in particular $a\ge1$ and $a+d_{1}\ge3$ or $a+b_{1}+b_{z3}\ge3$ or
$a+{\bf1}_{y_{2}}\ge3$.

$S_{y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$, $|S_{y}|=4\ge2n/k$,
$\bigcap_{i\in S_{y}}A_{i}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$.  For $\ell=2$

$|W\cap A_{4}|=c+d_{1}$, $|W\cap A_{6}|=c+d_{2}$ and

$c+\max\{d_{1},d_{2}\}\ge2$,
\tag{2}
so in particular $c\ge1$ and at least two seats of $W$ lie in
$\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}$, a set disjoint from $A_{1}$.

Hence $ |W\cap A_{1}| = s\le 5-2 =3$.  The bound is attainable e.g.

$W_{\max}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,

$|W_{\max}\cap A_{1}|=3$, $|A_{4}\cap W_{\max}|=2$, 
$|A_{8}\cap W_{\max}|=3$, so (1)–(2) hold.  Thus $\max s =3$.

If $s=1$ then $a+b_{1}+b_{z3}=1$.  With $a\le1$ we have
$a+d_{1}\le2$ and $a+{\bf1}_{y_{2}}\le2$, $a+{\bf1}_{y_{3}}\le2$, so (1)
is violated.  Hence $s\ge2$.

$s=2$ is attainable, e.g.

$W_{\min}=\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,

$a=2$, $d_{1}=1$, $c=2$, $b_{1}=b_{z3}=0$.  Then

$|W_{\min}\cap A_{1}|=2$,
$|A_{8}\cap W_{\min}|=a+d_{1}=3$,
$|A_{4}\cap W_{\min}|=c+d_{1}=3$,

so $S_{x}$ has a voter with $3$ approvals and $S_{y}$ has a voter with
$2$ approvals and every $\ell$-cohesive group is represented.  $s=0,1$
are impossible.

Hence for an EJR $5$-committee

$2\le |W\cap A_{1}|\le 3$,

the two extremes being realisable.  This is min $2$, max $3$, i.e. option
H.
public_text.8:
With $n=10$, $k=5$, $n/k=2$ put

$a=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$, $b_{1}={\bf1}_{y_{1}\in W}$,
$b_{z3}={\bf1}_{z_{3}\in W}$, $e={\bf1}_{z_{1}\in W}$,
$f={\bf1}_{z_{2}\in W}$, $d=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|$,
$r_{2}={\bf1}_{y_{2}\in W}$, $r_{3}={\bf1}_{y_{3}\in W}$.

$|W|=5$,

$|W\cap A_{1}|=a+b_{1}+b_{z3}$,

$|W\cap A_{2}|=a+r_{2}$,
$|W\cap A_{3}|=a+r_{3}$,
$|W\cap A_{8,9,10}|=a+e$,
$|W\cap A_{4,5}|=d+e$, $|W\cap A_{6,7}|=d+f$.

$S_{X}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$, $|S_{X}|=6\ge 3n/k$, 
$\bigcap_{i\in S_{X}}A_{i}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$.
Hence EJR for $\ell =3$ on $S_{X}$ is

$\max\{a+b_{1}+b_{z3},a+r_{2},a+r_{3},a+e\}\ge 3$,      $*$

and in particular $a+e\ge1$ and $a\ge1$.  $a=0$ gives $\max\le2$ and
$a=1$ forces $b_{1}=b_{z3}=1$, i.e. $|W\cap A_{1}|=3$.  Hence the
only way to keep $|W\cap A_{1}|<3$ is $a\ge2$.

$S_{Y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$, $|S_{Y}|=4\ge2n/k$,
$\bigcap_{i\in S_{Y}}A_{i}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$.
EJR for $\ell =2$ on $S_{Y}$ is

$\max\{d+e,d+f\}\ge2$, i.e. $d+\max(e,f)\ge2$,          $**$

so at least two seats of $W$ lie in 
$\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}$, a set disjoint from $A_{1}$.
Hence

$|W\cap A_{1}| =5-(d+e+f+r_{2}+r_{3}+b_{1}+b_{z3}+a\;{\rm counted})$
$\le5-2=3$.

$|W\cap A_{1}|=3$ is attainable e.g.

$W_{\max}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,
$a=3$, $d=2$, $e=f=0$, $|W\cap A_{1}|=3$,
$|W\cap A_{8}|=3$, $|W\cap A_{4}|=2$, so $*$ and $**$ hold.

The lower bound follows from $*$.  $a=2$ is admissible and with
$e=1$, $d=1$ we have $a+e=3$ so $*$ is met by voters $8\!-\!10$ and
$d+e=2$ so $**$ is met by voters $4,5$.  E.g.

$W_{\min}=\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{2}\}$,
$a=2$, $e=1$, $d=1$, $b_{1}=b_{z3}=0$,
$|W_{\min}\cap A_{1}|=2$, $|W_{\min}\cap A_{8}|=3$,
$|W_{\min}\cap A_{4}|=2$,

so EJR holds and $|W\cap A_{1}|=2$.  $a=1$ with $b_{1}=b_{z3}=0$
gives $\max\le2$ in $*$, and $a=0$ is impossible.  Hence
$|W\cap A_{1}|\ge2$.

Thus under the usual approval EJR, i.e. a cohesive group $S$ is
$\ell$-cohesive iff $|S|\ge\ell n/k$ and $|\bigcap_{i\in S}A_{i}|\ge\ell$
and $ \exists i\in S\;|W\cap A_{i}|\ge\ell$, the $A_{1}$-overlap of an
EJR $5$-committee can be $2$ and can be $3$ and no other value is
possible.

Min $2$, Max $3$, option H.
public_text.6:
For $n=10$, $k=5$, $n/k=2$ a group $S$ is $\ell$–cohesive iff
$|S|\ge 2\ell$ and $|\bigcap_{i\in S}A_{i}|\ge\ell$ and EJR requires a
member of $S$ with $|W\cap A_{i}|\ge\ell$.

* $S_{X}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$, $|S_{X}|=6$, $\bigcap A_{i}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$,
$\ell_{X}=3$,
$\;|W\cap A_{1}|=a+p+q$, $|W\cap A_{2}|=a+r$, $|W\cap A_{3}|=a+s$,
$|W\cap A_{8,9,10}|=a+b_{1}$ with $a=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$,
$p=1_{y_{1}}$, $q=1_{z_{3}}$, $r=1_{y_{2}}$, $s=1_{y_{3}}$, $b_{1}=1_{z_{1}}$.

EJR on $S_{X}$ is
$\max\{a+p+q,a+r,a+s,a+b_{1}\}\ge 3$, in particular $a\ge2$ and
$a+b_{1}\ge3$ is enough.
* $S_{Y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$, $|S_{Y}|=4$, $\bigcap A_{i}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$,
$\ell_{Y}=2$,

$c=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|$, $b_{1}=1_{z_{1}}$, $b_{2}=1_{z_{2}}$,
$|W\cap A_{4,5}|=c+b_{1}$, $|W\cap A_{6,7}|=c+b_{2}$.
EJR on $S_{Y}$ is $c+\max(b_{1},b_{2})\ge2$, i.e. at least two
places of $W$ have to be taken from
$B=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}\cap A_{1}^{\complement}$.

Hence with $|W|=5$

$|W\cap A_{1}|=a+p+q=5-\big[c+b_{1}+b_{2}+r+s\big]\le5-2=3$,

and $a\ge2$ gives $|W\cap A_{1}|\ge2$.  $1$ is impossible because
$a+p+q=1$ forces $a\le1$ and then $\max\{a+r,a+s,a+b_{1}\}\le2$
so $S_{X}$ would be unrepresented.

The bounds are tight.
* Max $3$, e.g. $W_{\max}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,

$a=3$, $c=2$, $b_{1}=b_{2}=0$, $|W\cap A_{1}|=3$,
$|A_{8}\cap W|=3$, $|A_{4}\cap W|=2$, so EJR holds.
* Min $2$, e.g. $W_{\min}=\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{2}\}$,

$a=2$, $b_{1}=1$, $c=1$, $r=1$, $|W\cap A_{1}|=2$,
$|A_{8}\cap W|=a+b_{1}=3$, $|A_{4}\cap W|=c+b_{1}=2$,
$|A_{2}\cap W|=a+r=3$, so $S_{X}$ and $S_{Y}$ are $\ell$-represented.

Thus an EJR $5$-committee meets voter $1$ in $2$ or $3$ approved
members and no other value is possible.  Min $2$, max $3$, option H.
public_text.4:
With $n=10$, $k=5$, $n/k=2$ a set $S$ is $\ell$-cohesive iff $|S|\ge 2\ell$
and $|\bigcap_{i\in S}A_{i}|\ge\ell$.

* $S_{X}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$, $|S_{X}|=6$, $\bigcap S_{X}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$.
  $\ell_{X}=3$ and EJR is

$\max\{|W\cap A_{1}|,|W\cap A_{2}|,|W\cap A_{3}|,|W\cap A_{8}|\}\ge3$

with 
$|W\cap A_{1}|=t+b+c$, $|W\cap A_{2}|=t+1_{y_{2}}$, 
$|W\cap A_{3}|=t+1_{y_{3}}$, $|W\cap A_{8}|=t+e$,
$t=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$, $b=1_{y_{1}}$, $c=1_{z_{3}}$, $e=1_{z_{1}}$.

* $S_{Y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$, $|S_{Y}|=4$, $\bigcap S_{Y}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$.
  $\ell_{Y}=2$ and with $d=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|$, 
  $e=1_{z_{1}}$, $f=1_{z_{2}}$

$|W\cap A_{4}|=d+e$, $|W\cap A_{6}|=d+f$,

so EJR is $d+\max\{e,f\}\ge2$, in particular
$|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}|\ge2$.  $A_{1}\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}=\varnothing$, 
hence

$|W\cap A_{1}|+|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}|\le5$,

and with the $S_{Y}$ requirement
$|W\cap A_{1}|\le3$.

The $S_{X}$ requirement gives $t\ge2$.  Indeed $t=0,1$ makes
$\max\{t+b+c,t+e,t+1_{y_{2}},t+1_{y_{3}}\}\le2$.  Hence
$|W\cap A_{1}|=t+b+c\ge t\ge2$, and $t+b+c=1$ is impossible for the
$\ell=3$ condition.  Hence

$2\le|W\cap A_{1}|\le3$.

Both bounds are attainable under ordinary EJR.

Max $3$, e.g.
$W_{\max}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,
$|W_{\max}\cap A_{1}|=3$, $|W_{\max}\cap A_{8}|=3$, $|W_{\max}\cap A_{4}|=2$.

Min $2$, e.g.
$W_{\min}=\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,
$|W_{\min}\cap A_{1}|=2$, $|W_{\min}\cap A_{8}|=3$ and
$|W_{\min}\cap A_{4}|=3$, so $S_{X}$ and $S_{Y}$ are EJR-satisfied.

Hence an EJR $5$-committee can meet voter $1$ in $2$ or $3$ approved
candidates and in no other number.  This is min $2$, max $3$, option H.
public_text.12:
With $n=10$, $k=5$, $n/k=2$ a set $S$ is $\ell$-cohesive iff $|S|\ge 2\ell$
and $|\bigcap_{i\in S}A_{i}|\ge\ell$. Existential EJR is

$\exists i\in S\;|W\cap A_{i}|\ge\ell$ .

The two non trivial $\ell$-cohesive families are

* $S_{x}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$, $\bigcap S_{x}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$,
$|S_{x}|=6$, $\ell_{x}=3$;
* $S_{y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$, $\bigcap S_{y}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$,
$|S_{y}|=4$, $\ell_{y}=2$.

Put $a=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$, $b_{1}={\bf1}_{y_{1}\in W}$,
$b_{z3}={\bf1}_{z_{3}\in W}$, $c_{y}=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|$,
$d_{1}={\bf1}_{z_{1}\in W}$, $d_{2}={\bf1}_{z_{2}\in W}$.

$|A_{1}\cap W|=t=a+b_{1}+b_{z3}$, $|W|=5$.

$S_{y}$ EJR is
$|A_{4}\cap W|=c_{y}+d_{1}\ge2$ or $|A_{6}\cap W|=c_{y}+d_{2}\ge2$, i.e.
$c_{y}+\max\{d_{1},d_{2}\}\ge2$ and in particular $c_{y}\ge1$.
Hence at least two seats of $W$ lie in
$\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}$, a set disjoint from $A_{1}$, so
$t\le3$.

$S_{x}$ EJR is
$\max\{a+b_{1}+b_{z3},\,a+{\bf1}_{y_{2}},\,a+{\bf1}_{y_{3}},\,a+d_{1}\}\ge3$.
In particular $a+d_{1}\ge1$ and with $a\le3$ we need $a\ge2$, otherwise
$\max\{a+b_{1}+b_{z3},a+d_{1}\}\le2$.
Hence $a\ge2$ and $t=a+b_{1}+b_{z3}\ge2$.  $t=1$ would give
$|W\cap A_{2}|\le2$, $|W\cap A_{8}|\le2$ and the $\ell=3$ requirement on
$S_{x}$ would be violated.

$t=3$ is attainable, e.g.

$W_{\max}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,

$|W_{\max}\cap A_{1}|=3$, $|A_{4}\cap W_{\max}|=2$,
$|A_{8}\cap W_{\max}|=3$, so $S_{y}$ and $S_{x}$ are satisfied.

$t=2$ is attainable, e.g.

$W_{\min}=\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,

$|W_{\min}\cap A_{1}|=2$, $|A_{8}\cap W_{\min}|=a+d_{1}=3$,
$|A_{4}\cap W_{\min}|=c_{y}+d_{1}=3$, and $S_{y}$ is satisfied by
voter 4.  No EJR committee can have $t\ge4$, for $t\ge4$ would leave
$\le1$ seat outside $A_{1}$ and then $c_{y}+\max\{d_{1},d_{2}\}<2$.

Hence under the usual existential EJR definition

$2\le |W\cap A_{1}|\le 3$,

the lower bound $2$ and the upper bound $3$ are both realisable.
That is min $2$, max $3$, option H.
public_text.10:
With $n=10$, $k=5$ we have $n/k=2$.
Put

* $a=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$,
* $b_{1}={\bf1}_{y_{1}\in W},\;b_{z3}={\bf1}_{z_{3}\in W}$,
* $c_{1}={\bf1}_{z_{1}\in W},\;c_{2}={\bf1}_{z_{2}\in W}$,
* $d=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|$,
* $b_{2}={\bf1}_{y_{2}\in W},\;b_{3}={\bf1}_{y_{3}\in W}$.

Then

$|W|=a+b_{1}+b_{z3}+b_{2}+b_{3}+d+c_{1}+c_{2}=5$,

$s:=|W\cap A_{1}|=a+b_{1}+b_{z3}$ and

$|W\cap A_{2}|=a+b_{2},\;|W\cap A_{3}|=a+b_{3},\;
|W\cap A_{8,9,10}|=a+c_{1},\;
|W\cap A_{4,5}|=d+c_{1},\;|W\cap A_{6,7}|=d+c_{2}$.

$S_{X}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$, $|S_{X}|=6\ge 3n/k$, $\bigcap S_{X}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$,
so $S_{X}$ is $3$-cohesive and

$\max\{s,a+b_{2},a+b_{3},a+c_{1}\}\ge 3\tag{1}$

is necessary for EJR.  In particular $a+c_{1}\ge1$ and $a\ge2$ on any
EJR committee.

$S_{Y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$, $|S_{Y}|=4\ge2n/k$, $\bigcap S_{Y}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$,
so $S_{Y}$ is $2$-cohesive and

$\max\{d+c_{1},d+c_{2}\}\ge2$, i.e. $d+\max\{c_{1},c_{2}\}\ge2\tag{2}$

is necessary.  Hence at least two seats of $W$ lie in
$\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}$, a set disjoint from
$A_{1}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{3}\}$.  From $|W|=5$

$s=5-(b_{2}+b_{3}+d+c_{1}+c_{2})\le5-2=3$,

and $s=4$ would give $b_{2}+b_{3}+d+c_{1}+c_{2}=1$, contradicting
(2).  Hence $s\le3$.

$s=1$ is impossible.  With $s=1$ we have $a\le1$ and (1) would need
$a+b_{2}\ge3$ or $a+b_{3}\ge3$ or $a+c_{1}\ge3$, impossible.
Hence $s\ge2$.

The bounds are attainable.  $s_{\max}=3$ e.g.

$W_{\max}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,

$a=3,\;d=2,\;s=3$, $|A_{1}\cap W|=3$, $|A_{8}\cap W|=3$,
$|A_{4}\cap W|=2$, so (1)-(2) hold.

$s_{\min}=2$ e.g.

$W_{\min}=\{x_{1},x_{2},y_{2},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,

$a=2,\;b_{2}=1,\;d=2,\;s=2$, $|A_{2}\cap W|=3$, $|A_{8}\cap W|=2$,
$|A_{4}\cap W|=2$.  The $3$-cohesive $S_{X}$ is represented by voter $2$
and the $2$-cohesive $S_{Y}$ is represented by voters $4,5$, so $W_{\min}$
is EJR and $|W_{\min}\cap A_{1}|=2$.

Hence under the usual approval EJR
$2\le|W\cap A_{1}|\le3$,

i.e. minimum $2$ and maximum $3$ for voter $1$.  This is option H,
min $2$, max $3$.
