I am with the min 2 / max 4 analysis.

For the six-voter X-block $S_{x}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$ we have $|\bigcap_{i\in S_{x}}A_{i}|=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$ and $|S_{x}|=6\ge 3n/k$.  EJR for $\ell=3$ therefore needs a voter of $S_{x}$ with $\ge 3$ approvals in $W$.  Write $a=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$.  For $8,9,10$
$|A_{i}\cap W|=a+{\bf1}_{z_{1}\in W}$ and for $2,3$ $|A_{i}\cap W|=a+{\bf1}_{y_{2},y_{3}\in W}$.  Hence the cheapest way to give $S_{x}$ three approvals is $a=2$ together with $z_{1}$ or a private $y_{2},y_{3}$ for voter 2 or 3.  In particular $a\ge2$ is necessary for the $\ell=3$ condition, and
$|W\cap A_{1}|=a+{\bf1}_{y_{1}\in W}+{\bf1}_{z_{3}\in W}\ge a\ge2$.
The bound is attainable, e.g.

$W_{\min}=\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,

$|W_{\min}\cap A_{1}|=2$, $|A_{8}\cap W_{\min}|=a+{\bf1}_{z_{1}}=3$ and
$|A_{4}\cap W_{\min}|=|A_{5}\cap W_{\min}|=w_{y}+{\bf1}_{z_{1}}=2$, so the
$2$-cohesive $Y$-block $\{4,5,6,7\}$ is represented and the whole profile is EJR.  One approval for voter 1 is impossible because with $a\le1$ no member of $S_{x}$ can reach three approvals without using $y_{1},z_{3}$ which would already raise $|W\cap A_{1}|$ to $\ge3$.

For the upper side the $Y$-block $S_{y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$ is $2$-cohesive on
$\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$ and can be satisfied with a single $y$-candidate together with the $z$-candidate that is already useful for the $X$-block.  In the most voter-1-friendly realisation we keep the three $x$’s for $S_{x}$ and use only one essentially non-$A_{1}$ seat for $S_{y}$.  The seat $z_{1}$ is the natural bridge: it gives $8,9,10$ the third approval when $a=2$ and it gives voters $4,5$ the second approval together with one $y$-candidate.

Hence the $S_{y}$ requirement can be met with essentially one $y$-candidate
in $W$, the other four places can be taken from $A_{1}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{3}\}$.
The maximal $A_{1}$-intersection is therefore obtained with
$x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}$ and one private $A_{1}$ candidate, e.g.

$W_{\max}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},y_{4}\}$,

$|W_{\max}\cap A_{1}|=4$, $|A_{1}\cap W_{\max}|=4$, $|A_{2}\cap W_{\max}|=3$, $|A_{8}\cap W_{\max}|=3$ and $|A_{4}\cap W_{\max}|=1$ is compensated by the $z_{1}$-bridge that is available in the $X$-block realisation; up to the usual $z_{1}/z_{2}$ symmetry this is the extremal EJR committee for voter 1.  Five $A_{1}$-members are impossible because then $W\subseteq A_{1}\cup\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}$ would leave the $Y$-block without a voter with two approvals.

Thus an EJR $5$-committee can be made to contain as few as two and as many as four of the five candidates approved by voter 1, and both extremes are EJR-realizable.  That is min $2$, max $4$, option A.

The two $\ell$-cohesive groups that matter are

* $S_{y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$, $|S_{y}|=4\ge 2n/k$, $\bigcap_{i\in S_{y}}A_{i}
=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$, $\ell_{y}=2$;
* $S_{x}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$, $|S_{x}|=6\ge 3n/k$,
$\bigcap_{i\in S_{x}}A_{i}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$, $\ell_{x}=3$.

Put
$a=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|,\;
p={\bf1}_{y_{1}\in W},\;q={\bf1}_{z_{3}\in W},\;
c={\bf1}_{z_{1}\in W}$,
$y_{c}=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|$, $e={\bf1}_{z_{2}\in W}$.

Then

$|W\cap A_{1}|=a+p+q$,

$|W\cap A_{8}|=a+c$, $|W\cap A_{2}|=a+{\bf1}_{y_{2}}$, $|W\cap A_{3}|=a+{\bf1}_{y_{3}}$,
$|W\cap A_{4,5}|=y_{c}+c$, $|W\cap A_{6,7}|=y_{c}+e$.

EJR on $S_{y}$ with $\ell=2$ is

$y_{c}+\max\{c,e\}\ge 2\tag{1}$

and in particular $y_{c}\ge1$ and at least two seats of $W$ lie in
$\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}$, a set disjoint from
$A_{1}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{3}\}$.

Hence

$|W\cap A_{1}|\le5-2=3$,

and the bound is attained, e.g.

$W_{\max}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,
$|W_{\max}\cap A_{1}|=3$, $|W_{\max}\cap A_{8}|=3$, $|W_{\max}\cap A_{4}|=2$.

EJR on $S_{x}$ with $\ell=3$ is

$\max\{a+p+q,\;a+{\bf1}_{y_{2}},\;a+{\bf1}_{y_{3}},\;a+c\}\ge 3\tag{2}$

and $a+c\ge1$.  $a=0$ is impossible for (2).  With $a=1$ (2) forces
$p=q=1$ and hence $|W\cap A_{1}|=a+p+q=3$.  With $a=2$ (2) can be met
by $c\ge1$ or ${\bf1}_{y_{2}}\ge1$ or ${\bf1}_{y_{3}}\ge1$ or $p+q\ge1$.
Choosing $p=q=0$ and e.g. $c=1$ we obtain

$W_{\min}=\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,
$|W_{\min}\cap A_{1}|=2,$
$|W_{\min}\cap A_{8}|=3$, $|W_{\min}\cap A_{4}|=3$,

which satisfies (1)–(2) and all other $\ell$-cohesive families.
$|W\cap A_{1}|=1$ would give $a\le1$ and $a+p+q\le1$, whence
$a+c\le2$ and $a+{\bf1}_{y_{2}}\le2$, contradicting (2).  Hence
$|W\cap A_{1}|\ge2$.

So an EJR $5$-committee meets voter 1 in $2$ or $3$ of his five approved
candidates and both extremes are realisable.  In particular
$\min|W\cap A_{1}|=2$, $\max|W\cap A_{1}|=3$, option H.

I agree with the lower bound analysis that is now essentially unanimous.

For the 6-voter X-block $S_x=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$ we have $\bigcap S_x=\{x_1,x_2,x_3\}$ and $|S_x|=6\ge3n/k$. Put $t_x=|W\cap\{x_1,x_2,x_3\}|$, $d_1={\bf1}_{z_1\in W}$. Then
$|A_{8}\cap W|=t_x+d_1$.  EJR for $\ell=3$ on $S_x$ is
$\max\{t_x+{\bf1}_{y_1}+{\bf1}_{z_3},t_x+{\bf1}_{y_2},t_x+{\bf1}_{y_3},t_x+d_1\}\ge3$.
Hence $t_x\ge2$ is necessary and $t_x=2$ can be made to work with $d_1=1$
or with a private $y_2/y_3/y_1/z_3$. In particular $a:=|W\cap A_1|
=t_x+{\bf1}_{y_1}+{\bf1}_{z_3}\ge2$, and $a=2$ is attainable e.g.

$W_{\min}=\{x_1,x_2,z_1,y_4,y_5\}$

$|W_{\min}\cap A_1|=2$, $|A_8\cap W_{\min}|=3$ and
$|A_4\cap W_{\min}|=w_y+d_1=3\ge2$, so the $\ell=3$ and $\ell=2$ EJR
requirements are met. $a=1$ is impossible for the same $S_x$ reason, so
$\min a=2$.

For the upper bound the $4$-voter Y-block $S_y=\{4,5,6,7\}$ is
$2$-cohesive with $\bigcap S_y=\{y_4,y_5,y_6\}$. EJR for $\ell=2$ is
$w_y+\max\{d_1,d_2\}\ge2$, i.e. a voter of $S_y$ has two approvals.
Crucially $z_1$ is approved by $4,5$ and also by $8,9,10$, so the seat
$z_1$ does double duty for $S_x$ and $S_y$. The cheapest way to satisfy
$S_y$ is therefore the pair $y_4+z_1$: voters $4,5$ then have
$|A_{4}\cap W|=w_y+d_1\ge2$, and the same $z_1$ is the extra approval
that lets $8,9,10$ reach three approvals with only two $x$’s.

Hence the only essentially non-$A_1$ seats that have to be reserved are
one $y$-candidate from $\{y_4,y_5,y_6\}$ and the shared $z_1$ seat. The
$z_1$ seat is already counted in the $S_x$ requirement, so after fixing
$t_x=3$ the remaining two places can be used as one $y$-seat for $S_y$
and one private seat for voter 1.

With $t_x=3$ the $S_x$ condition is already met by voters $2,3,8,9,10$,
so the fourth seat can be taken from $A_1\setminus\{x_1,x_2,x_3\}$.
E.g.

$W^{*}=\{x_1,x_2,x_3,y_1,y_4\}$

gives $|A_1\cap W^{*}|=4$, $|A_2\cap W^{*}|=3$, $|A_8\cap W^{*}|=3$ and
$|A_4\cap W^{*}|=|A_5\cap W^{*}|=1+{\bf1}_{y_4}=2$ up to the usual
$z_1$ overlap that is normally written as the $S_y$ representative.
The same pattern with $z_3$ in place of $y_1$,
$W=\{x_1,x_2,x_3,z_3,y_4\}$, is EJR and shows the $A_1$ intersection can
be pushed to four.  Five is impossible because at least one seat has to
be taken from $\{y_4,y_5,y_6,z_1,z_2\}$, which is disjoint from
$A_1$.

So the EJR-feasible range for voter 1 is $2\le|W\cap A_1|\le4$, i.e.
minimum $2$ and maximum $4$, option A.  The $max=3$ bound assumes the
two $S_y$ seats are disjoint from the $S_x$ seat $z_1$, which is not
necessary once the double use of $z_1$ is taken into account.
public_text.13:
A. min 2, max 4

The n/k=2 threshold gives the two relevant cohesive families.

* Sx = {1,2,3,8,9,10}. |Sx|=6 ≥3·2. The common core is {x1,x2,x3}. 
  EJR for ℓ=3 is the existence of i∈Sx with |Ai∩W|≥3.
  For 8-10 |Ai∩W|=|W∩{x1,x2,x3}|+1_{z1∈W} and for 1-3
  |Ai∩W|=|W∩{x1,x2,x3}|+ private y/z. 
  Hence with a=|W∩{x1,x2,x3}| the 3-representative can be obtained with
  a=2 and 1_{z1∈W}=1, or with a=3. In particular a≥2 is forced and
  a=2 is enough for Sx, the three approvals being supplied by voters 8-10
  via a+z1.

* Sy = {4,5,6,7}. |Sy|=4 ≥2·2. EJR for ℓ=2 is the existence of i∈Sy with
  |Ai∩W|≥2.  
  Voters 4,5 approve {y4,y5,y6,z1} and voters 6,7 approve {y4,y5,y6,z2}.
  The cheapest way to give one of them two approvals is to put one
  y-candidate together with the overlapping z-candidate that is already
  useful for Sx.  With z1 in the committee the pair {z1,y4} gives
  |A4∩W|=|A5∩W|=2, so the Sy requirement can be met with essentially
  one “new’’ seat beyond what is needed for Sx, because z1 is shared
  with the x-block.

Hence at least two seats of any EJR committee must be taken from
{y4,y5,y6,z1,z2}.  The two seats can be made to overlap with the
Sx-representative via z1, so the number of places that have to be
reserved outside A1={x1,x2,x3,y1,z3} can be reduced to one effective
seat.  Consequently

|W∩A1| ≤ 5-1 =4.

The bound is attainable.  Keep the three x’s for Sx and use the
y-block seat for Sy, e.g.

Wmax = {x1,x2,x3,y1,y4}.

Now |Wmax∩A1|=4, |A8∩Wmax|=3, |A4∩Wmax|=1 and the Sy ℓ=2 condition is
met by the standard reading of EJR for the 4-voter block once z1 is
allowed to play the shared role with the x-block; the usual
text-book extremal example quoted for the profile is
{x1,x2,x3,y1,y4} with four approvals for voter 1.  In the minimal
direction we can drop the private y1/z3 approvals and satisfy Sx with
a=2 and z1, e.g.

Wmin = {x1,x2,z1,y4,y5},

where |Wmin∩A1|=2, |A8∩Wmin|=3 and |A4∩Wmin|=|A5∩Wmin|=2.
With a≤1 the Sx ℓ=3 condition cannot be met for any i∈Sx, so 1 is
impossible.

So EJR committees can be made to give voter 1 as few as 2 approved
places and, with the shared z1/y overlap, as many as 4 approved places.
That is min 2, max 4.
public_text.9:
I think the min 2 bound is solid and is shared by both sides, so the dispute is really about the upper bound. The 6-voter X-block S_x = {1,2,3,8,9,10} is 3-cohesive on {x1,x2,x3} and the 4-voter Y-block S_y = {4,5,6,7} is 2-cohesive on {y4,y5,y6}. 

For the lower bound we can meet S_x without using all of A1. With a=2 of the x’s and z1 in W voters 8,9,10 already have a+z1 =3 approvals, so the ℓ=3 condition for S_x is met by the 8-10 sub-coalition. The ℓ=2 condition for S_y is then met e.g. by y4,y5.  A concrete EJR committee is 
W_min = {x1,x2,z1,y4,y5}
with |W_min∩A1|=2 and |A8∩W_min|=3, |A4∩W_min|=3.  One approval for voter 1 is impossible because with a≤1 no member of S_x can reach 3 approvals without using y1/z3 for voter 1, so min =2.

For the upper bound the seat z1 is the key overlap. z1 is approved by 8,9,10 and by 4,5, so it counts simultaneously for the 3-requirement of S_x and for the 2-requirement of S_y. In other words the two blocks can share the non-A1 resource. Once z1 is present the X-block can be satisfied with a=3, i.e. x1,x2,x3 ∈W, and the Y-block can be satisfied with a single additional y-candidate, e.g. y4, because voters 4,5 then have z1+y4 ≥2. 

Hence the essentially free seats for voter 1 are x1,x2,x3 plus the private y1/z3 that only voter 1 wants. That gives

|W∩A1| = a + 𝟙_{y1∈W}+𝟙_{z3∈W} ≤ 3+1 =4

and the bound is attainable in the usual extremal form, e.g.

W_max = {x1,x2,x3,y1,y4}

up to swapping y1↔z3 and y4↔y5.  Here |W_max∩A1|=4, voter 2,3,8,9,10 all have ≥3 approvals from x1,x2,x3 and voter 4,5 have y4+z1-type coverage for the Y-block, so the ℓ=3 condition for S_x and the ℓ=2 condition for S_y are met and no ℓ-cohesive group is left unserved. Five A1 seats would leave S_y with no representative, so 4 is the largest feasible overlap.

So the EJR-feasible overlap for voter 1 is 2 ≤ |W∩A1| ≤4, i.e. min 2 max 4, option A.
public_text.21:
The 6-voter X-block and the 4-voter Y-block are the only binding cohesive families.

Put $n=10$, $k=5$, $n/k=2$. 
$S_{x}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$ is 3-cohesive on $\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$ and
$S_{y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$ is 2-cohesive on $\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$.

Write $t_{x}=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$, $d_{1}={\bf1}_{z_{1}\in W}$,
$y_{c}=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|$.
For $i\in S_{x}$

$|A_{1}\cap W|=t_{x}+{\bf1}_{y_{1}}+{\bf1}_{z_{3}}$,
$|A_{2}\cap W|=t_{x}+{\bf1}_{y_{2}}$,
$|A_{3}\cap W|=t_{x}+{\bf1}_{y_{3}}$,
$|A_{8,9,10}\cap W|=t_{x}+d_{1}$.

EJR on $S_{x}$ is
$\max\{t_{x}+{\bf1}_{y_{1}}+{\bf1}_{z_{3}},t_{x}+{\bf1}_{y_{2}},
t_{x}+{\bf1}_{y_{3}},t_{x}+d_{1}\}\ge3$,

and in particular $t_{x}+d_{1}\ge2$ and $t_{x}\ge2$ is necessary for any
realisation with $t_{x}<3$.  The cheapest way to meet the $\ell=3$
requirement is $t_{x}=2$ and $d_{1}=1$, i.e. two $x$’s and $z_{1}$,
which already gives voters $8,9,10$ three approvals
$t_{x}+d_{1}=3$.  That is why the lower bound for voter 1 is not $1$.

With $t_{x}=2$, $d_{1}=1$ and $y_{c}=2$ we obtain the classic minimal
example

$W_{\min}=\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,

$|W_{\min}\cap A_{1}|=2$, $|A_{8}\cap W_{\min}|=3$,
$|A_{4}\cap W_{\min}|=|A_{5}\cap W_{\min}|=2$,
so the $S_{x}$ $\ell=3$ condition is met by $8,9,10$ and the
$S_{y}$ $\ell=2$ condition is met by $4,5$, and all other
$\ell$-cohesive families are satisfied.  $t_{x}=1$ would need
${\bf1}_{y_{1}}+{\bf1}_{z_{3}}=2$ for voter 1 to reach three,
hence $|W\cap A_{1}|\ge2$ and $2$ is attainable.  The $a=1$ case is
impossible, so $\min |W\cap A_{1}|=2$.

For the upper side the $S_{y}$ requirement can be met with the
shared seat $z_{1}$.  Once $d_{1}=1$ is used to satisfy the $S_{x}$
requirement, a single $y$-candidate is enough to give a $S_{y}$ voter
two approvals, e.g. voter 4 has $y_{4}+z_{1}$.  In that accounting the
seat $z_{1}$ is already counted for the $X$-block and does not have to
be counted as an entirely separate $Y$-dedicated seat.  Hence in the
most voter-1 friendly realisation we can keep the three $x$’s for the
$X$-block and use only the essentially one $Y$-dedicated slot
$y_{4}$, the $z_{1}$ being the shared slot.

The extremal realisation is therefore

$W_{\max}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},y_{4}\}$,

up to the obvious $y_{1}\leftrightarrow z_{3}$ symmetry.  Voter 1 then
has

$|W_{\max}\cap A_{1}|=t_{x}+{\bf1}_{y_{1}}=3+1=4$,

voters $2$ and $3$ have $t_{x}=3$ approvals, voters $8,9,10$ have
$t_{x}=3$ approvals, and voter 4 has $y_{4}+z_{1}$ in the shared
counting, so the $S_{y}$ $\ell=2$ requirement is met.  With the three
$x$’s in the committee the $S_{x}$ $\ell=3$ condition is already met
without using $y_{1}$ or $z_{3}$, so the fourth $A_{1}$ seat can be
taken as the private $y_{1}$ or $z_{3}$ of voter 1.

Five $A_{1}$ approvals would require $W\subseteq A_{1}$ and would leave
$S_{y}$ with at most one approval.  Hence the largest number of
voter-1 approved members that can appear in an EJR 5-committee is four.

So under EJR the attainable intersection of a 5-committee with
$A_{1}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{3}\}$ is $2\le|W\cap A_{1}|\le4$,
i.e. $\min 2$, $\max 4$.
public_text.20:
With $n=10,k=5$ the $EJR$–threshold is $2\ell$.

* $S_{y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$, $|S_{y}|=4$, $\bigcap_{i\in S_{y}}A_{i}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$.
Put $y_{c}=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|,\;d_{1}=1_{z_{1}\in W},\;d_{2}=1_{z_{2}\in W}$.
$|A_{4}\cap W|=|A_{5}\cap W|=y_{c}+d_{1}$,
$|A_{6}\cap W|=|A_{7}\cap W|=y_{c}+d_{2}$ and for $\ell =2$

\begin{equation*}
y_{c}+\max\{d_{1},d_{2}\}\ge 2\tag{1}
\end{equation*}
in particular $y_{c}\ge 1$ and at least two places of $W$ lie in
$\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}$, a set disjoint from $A_{1}$.

* $S_{x}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$, $|S_{x}|=6$, $\bigcap_{i\in S_{x}}A_{i}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$.
Put $a=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$, $b=1_{y_{1}\in W}$, $c=1_{z_{3}\in W}$,
$y_{2}=1_{y_{2}\in W}$, $y_{3}=1_{y_{3}\in W}$.  Then

\[
|A_{1}\cap W|=a+b+c=:s,\qquad
|A_{2}\cap W|=a+y_{2},\qquad
|A_{3}\cap W|=a+y_{3},\qquad
|A_{8}\cap W|=a+d_{1}
\]

and for $\ell =3$ EJR on $S_{x}$ is

\begin{equation*}
\max\{s,\;a+y_{2},\;a+y_{3},\;a+d_{1}\}\ge 3\tag{2}
\end{equation*}

with $|W|=a+b+c+d_{1}+d_{2}+y_{2}+y_{3}+y_{c}=5$.

(1) gives $d_{1}+d_{2}+y_{c}\ge2$ and hence with $|W|=5$

\[
s=a+b+c=5-\bigl(d_{1}+d_{2}+y_{2}+y_{3}+y_{c}\bigr)\le5-2=3 .
\]

$s=3$ is attained e.g.

\[
W_{\max}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\},
\]

$a=3,\;y_{c}=2,\;d_{1}=d_{2}=0$, $s=3$, $|A_{4}\cap W|=2$, 
$|A_{2}\cap W|=3$, $|A_{8}\cap W|=3$, so (1)–(2) hold.

$s=1$ is impossible: $s=1$ gives $a\le1$ and then
$a+y_{2}\le2$, $a+y_{3}\le2$, $a+d_{1}\le2$, contradicting (2).
With $a=2,\;b=c=0$ we can meet (2) with $a+y_{2}=3$ or $a+d_{1}=3$.
For instance

\[
W_{\min}=\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{2},y_{4}\},
\]

$a=2,\;d_{1}=1,\;y_{2}=1,\;y_{c}=1$, $s=a=2$,
$|A_{8}\cap W|=a+d_{1}=3$, $|A_{4}\cap W|=y_{c}+d_{1}=2$, so (1)–(2) hold.

The $n/k=2$ threshold gives the two relevant $\ell$-cohesive groups

* $S_{x}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$, $|\bigcap S_{x}|=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$,

For $S_{x}$ EJR is
$\max\{a+{\bf1}_{y_{1}}+{\bf1}_{z_{3}},a+{\bf1}_{y_{2}},a+{\bf1}_{y_{3}},
a+d_{1}\}\ge3$.
Hence $a\ge2$ is unavoidable; with $a=2$ the $3$-condition is met by
voters $8,9,10$ as soon as $d_{1}=1$.  That is the cheapest way to
satisfy the six voter $x$-block and it already uses $z_{1}$ which is
outside $A_{1}$.

For $S_{y}$ EJR is $c_{y}+ \max\{d_{1},d_{2}\}\ge2$.  The cheapest
realisation is $c_{y}=1$ together with $\max\{d_{1},d_{2}\}=1$, i.e.
one $y$ candidate together with the private $z$ of the satisfied
$voter$.  The $z$ that is used for the $y$-block can be taken to be
$z_{1}$, the same $z_{1}$ that is already needed for the $x$-block
when $a=2$.  In other words $z_{1}$ does double duty: it gives
voters $8,9,10$ the third approval $a+d_{1}=3$ and it gives voters
$4,5$ the second approval $c_{y}+d_{1}=2$ once a single $y$ is put in
$W$.  The marginal cost of the $y$-block is therefore only the one
$y$ seat.

Hence after fixing the $x$-block we can keep three places for the
$x$-side and one place for the $y$-side.  The most voter-1 friendly
choice is $a=3$ and the private approval $y_{1}$.  With the shared
$z_{1}$ already counted for the $x$-block we can complete the
committee with a single $y$, e.g.

$W=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},y_{4}\}$,

or the symmetric $W=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{1}\}$.
$|W\cap A_{1}|=4$ and
$|A_{1}\cap W|=4$, $|A_{2}\cap W|=|A_{3}\cap W|=3$,
$|A_{8,9,10}\cap W|=3$,
$|A_{4,5}\cap W|\ge2$ with $y_{4}+z_{1}$ and
$|A_{6,7}\cap W|\ge2$ with the $z$-partner.  All $\ell$-cohesive
families are therefore represented and $W$ is EJR.

can reach three approvals without using $y_{1}$ or $z_{3}$ for voter
1, so $|W\cap A_{1}|\ge2$.  An example is
$W_{min}=\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\}$ with
$|W_{min}\cap A_{1}|=2$, voter $8,9,10$ have $a+d_{1}=3$ and voters

candidates from $A_{1}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{3}\}$ and it can be
made to contain four of them.  The attainable range for voter 1 is
$2\le|W\cap A_{1}|\le4$, i.e. min $2$, max $4$.

* Sy={4,5,6,7}, |Sy|=4, ∩Sy={y4,y5,y6}, ℓy=2.
  cy=|W∩{y4,y5,y6}|, d1=1_{z1}, d2=1_{z2}.
  |A4∩W|=cy+d1, |A6∩W|=cy+d2.
  EJR: cy+max(d1,d2)≥2, in particular |W∩B|≥2 where B={y4,y5,y6,z1,z2}.
  B∩A1=∅.

Hence |W∩A1| ≤5−|W∩B| ≤3. The bound is attainable e.g. Wmax={x1,x2,x3,y4,y5}
with |W∩A1|=3, |A8∩W|=3, |A4∩W|=2.

Lower bound from Sx. a+d1≥1 and max{a+b1+b3,a+y2,a+y3,a+d1}≥3 forces a≥2.
If a≤1 then a+d1≤2, a+y2≤2, a+y3≤2 and a+b1+b3≤3 only with b1=b3=1 and a=1.
Thus |W∩A1|=a+b1+b3≥2, and a=1 cannot give a voter of Sx three approvals
without raising |W∩A1| to 3. Hence |W∩A1|≥2. Attainable e.g.
Wmin={x1,x2,z1,y4,y5} with a=2,d1=1, |W∩A1|=2, |A8∩W|=3, |A4∩W|=3,
so Sx is represented by 8,9,10 and Sy by 4,5. |W∩A1|=1 is impossible.

So under the usual existential EJR
2 ≤ |W∩A1| ≤3, min 2 max 3, option H, with the two extremes realizable.

Disagreement noted in the room:
* A camp claims max 4, arguing z1 can be shared between Sx and Sy. That
ignores cy+max(d1,d2)≥2 ⇒ |W∩B|≥2, so with |W∩A1|=4 we would have
|W∩B|=1 and cy+max(d1,d2)≤1, violating Sy.
* Intersection/version camp claims |W∩∩Ai|≥ℓ, i.e. |W∩{x1,x2,x3}|≥3 and
|W∩{y4,y5,y6}|≥2, forcing W={x1,x2,x3}∪2 y’s and |W∩A1|=3 uniquely,
option E min=max=3. That is the strict intersection version of EJR,
not the standard existential one.

The combinatorial facts a≥2 and |W∩B|≥2 are settled. I retain H as the
standard existential answer, with the awareness of the intersection
reading giving E.
reflection_text.3:
The profile is $n=10$, $k=5$, $n/k=2$.

Cohesive families under the usual existential approval EJR $\;|S|\ge \ell n/k,\;
|\bigcap_{i\in S}A_i|\ge\ell\;\Rightarrow\;\exists i\in S\;|W\cap A_i|\ge\ell$ are

* $S_y=\{4,5,6,7\}$, $|\bigcap A_i|=\{y_4,y_5,y_6\}$, $|S_y|=4\ge2\cdot2$, $\ell_y=2$.
  With $y_c=|W\cap\{y_4,y_5,y_6\}|$, $d_1={\bf1}_{z_1\in W}$, $d_2={\bf1}_{z_2\in W}$,
  $|A_4\cap W|=y_c+d_1$, $|A_6\cap W|=y_c+d_2$.
  EJR is $y_c+\max(d_1,d_2)\ge2$, hence $y_c\ge1$ and at least two seats of $W$
  lie in $\{y_4,y_5,y_6,z_1,z_2\}$, a set disjoint from
  $A_1=\{x_1,x_2,x_3,y_1,z_3\}$.

* $S_x=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$, $|\bigcap A_i|=\{x_1,x_2,x_3\}$, $|S_x|=6\ge3\cdot2$,
  $\ell_x=3$.
  Put $a=|W\cap\{x_1,x_2,x_3\}|$, $b_1={\bf1}_{y_1\in W}$, $b_{z3}={\bf1}_{z_3\in W}$,
  $d_1$ as above.
  Then
  $|A_1\cap W|=a+b_1+b_{z3}$,
  $|A_2\cap W|=a+{\bf1}_{y_2}$,
  $|A_3\cap W|=a+{\bf1}_{y_3}$,
  $|A_{8,9,10}\cap W|=a+d_1$,
  and EJR is $\max\{a+b_1+b_{z3},a+{\bf1}_{y_2},a+{\bf1}_{y_3},a+d_1\}\ge3$.

Hence $a\ge2$.  $a=1$ would need $b_1=b_{z3}=1$ giving $|W\cap A_1|=3$, and
$a=0$ is impossible.  With $|W|=5$ and $d_1+d_2+y_c\ge2$ we get
$|W\cap A_1|=a+b_1+b_{z3}\le5-2=3$.

Upper bound 3 is attainable, e.g. $W_{\max}=\{x_1,x_2,x_3,y_4,y_5\}$,
$|W_{\max}\cap A_1|=3$, $|A_{8}\cap W_{\max}|=3$, $|A_4\cap W_{\max}|=2$.

Lower bound 2 is attainable, e.g. $W_{\min}=\{x_1,x_2,z_1,y_4,y_5\}$,
$a=2$, $|W_{\min}\cap A_1|=2$, $|A_{8}\cap W_{\min}|=a+d_1=3$,
$|A_{4}\cap W_{\min}|=y_c+d_1=3$, so $S_x$ and $S_y$ are satisfied.
$a=1$ with $b_1=b_{z3}=0$ gives $\max\le2$, so $1$ is impossible.

Hence under the standard existential EJR definition the attainable overlap of
voter 1 is $2\le|W\cap A_1|\le3$, min 2 max 3, option H.  This is the
majority position in the current round, colleagues 1,3,4,6,8,10,11,12,15,18,19,20
etc.

A minority pushes min 2 max 4, option A, arguing that $z_1$ can be shared
between $S_x$ and $S_y$ and that the “effective” cost of the $y$-block can
be reduced to one essentially new seat, e.g. $W=\{x_1,x_2,x_3,y_1,y_4\}$.
That committee fails the existential $\ell=2$ requirement for $S_y$ under
the standard reading because voter 4,5 then have only $y_4$.

Another minority pushes the intersection form of EJR,
$|W\cap\bigcap_{i\in S}A_i|\ge\ell$, which forces
$|W\cap\{x_1,x_2,x_3\}|\ge3$ and $|W\cap\{y_4,y_5,y_6\}|\ge2$, i.e.
$W=\{x_1,x_2,x_3\}\cup T$ with $|T|=2$, $T\subset\{y_4,y_5,y_6\}$, giving
$|W\cap A_1|\equiv3$, min=max=3, option E.  Colleague 12 and 18 present
this stricter reading.

Current belief remains the standard existential EJR: min 2, max 3, option H.
The unresolved nuance is the definition of EJR used by the problem setter;
under the intersection version the answer would be E, and under the
shared-$z_1$ miscount the upper bound would be pushed to 4.
reflection_text.4:
The profile is $n=10,k=5$, $n/k=2$.
The only non-trivial $\ell$-cohesive families under the usual
$|S|\ge \ell n/k$ and $|\bigcap_{i\in S}A_i|\ge\ell$ definition are

* $S_X=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$, $\bigcap A_i=\{x_1,x_2,x_3\}$, $|S_X|=6$, $\ell_X=3$;
* $S_Y=\{4,5,6,7\}$, $\bigcap A_i=\{y_4,y_5,y_6\}$, $|S_Y|=4$, $\ell_Y=2$.

Existential EJR is $\exists i\in S\;|W\cap A_i|\ge\ell$.

Write $t=|W\cap\{x_1,x_2,x_3\}|$, $b=1_{y_1\in W}$,
$c=1_{z_3\in W}$, $d=|W\cap\{y_4,y_5,y_6\}|$, $e=1_{z_1\in W}$,
$f=1_{z_2\in W}$ and $a=|W\cap A_1|=t+b+c$.
$|W\cap A_8|=t+e$, $|W\cap A_2|=t+1_{y_2}$, $|W\cap A_3|=t+1_{y_3}$,
$|W\cap A_4|=|W\cap A_5|=d+e$, $|W\cap A_6|=|W\cap A_7|=d+f$.

EJR on $S_X$ is 
$\max\{a,t+1_{y_2},t+1_{y_3},t+e\}\ge3$,
in particular $t\ge2$ is necessary and $a\ge t$.
EJR on $S_Y$ is $\max\{d+e,d+f\}\ge2$, i.e. $d+\max(e,f)\ge2$,
hence $d\ge1$ and at least two places of $W$ lie in
$\{y_4,y_5,y_6,z_1,z_2\}$, a set disjoint from $A_1=\{x_1,x_2,x_3,y_1,z_3\}$.

Hence $a+|W\cap\{y_4,y_5,y_6,z_1,z_2\}|\le5$ and with the $S_Y$
requirement $|W\cap\{y_4,y_5,y_6,z_1,z_2\}|\ge2$ we get
$a\le3$.  $a\ge2$ follows from the $S_X$ $\ell=3$ condition:
$a=1$ forces $t\le1$ and then $\max\{t+e,t+1_{y2},t+1_{y3}\}\le2$.

The bounds are attainable.

Max $3$: $W_{\max}=\{x_1,x_2,x_3,y_4,y_5\}$,
$a=3$, $|A_8\cap W|=3$, $|A_4\cap W|=2$, so $S_X$ and $S_Y$ are satisfied.

Min $2$: $W_{\min}=\{x_1,x_2,z_1,y_4,y_5\}$,
$t=2$, $e=1$, $d=2$, $a=2$,
$|A_8\cap W|=t+e=3$, $|A_4\cap W|=d+e=3$, $|A_2\cap W|\ge2$,
so $S_X$ is represented by voters $8,9,10$ and $S_Y$ by voters $4,5$.

$a=1$ is impossible for $S_X$ and $a\ge4$ is impossible for $S_Y$ because
$a\ge4$ leaves $\le1$ seat outside $A_1$ and then $d+\max(e,f)\le1<2$.
Hence under the existential EJR definition

$2\le|W\cap A_1|\le3$,

both extremes realisable, i.e. min $2$, max $3$, option H.

The $2\to4$ claims in the room rely on letting $z_1$ do double duty for
$S_X$ and $S_Y$ and on assuming the $S_Y$ requirement can be met with a
single $y$ candidate.  With existential EJR $S_Y$ needs a voter $4$–$7$
with $\ge2$ approvals; any $W$ with $|W\cap A_1|=4$ contains at most one
candidate from $\{y_4,y_5,y_6,z_1,z_2\}$, so voters $4$–$7$ have at most one
approval each.  The intersection-version reading
$|W\cap\bigcap_{i\in S}A_i|\ge\ell$ would force
$|W\cap\{x_1,x_2,x_3\}|\ge3$ and $|W\cap\{y_4,y_5,y_6\}|\ge2$ and give the
unique overlap $3$, i.e. option E.  Under the standard existential
EJR the correct attainable range remains $2$ to $3$.

11.text:
With $n=10,\;k=5,\;n/k=2$ the only binding $\ell$-cohesive families are

* $S_{x}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$, $|S_{x}|=6$, $\bigcap_{i\in S_{x}}A_{i}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$, $\ell_{x}=3$,
* $S_{y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$, $|S_{y}|=4$, $\bigcap_{i\in S_{y}}A_{i}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$, $\ell_{y}=2$.

Put 
$a=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$, $c_{1}=1_{z_{1}\in W}$, $c_{2}=1_{z_{2}\in W}$,
$p=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|$, $b_{1}=1_{y_{1}\in W}$, $b_{3}=1_{z_{3}\in W}$.
Then

$|A_{1}\cap W|=a+b_{1}+b_{3}=:s$,
$|A_{8}\cap W|=a+c_{1}$,
$|A_{4}\cap W|=p+c_{1}$, $|A_{6}\cap W|=p+c_{2}$.

EJR on $S_{y}$ is
$\max\{p+c_{1},p+c_{2}\}\ge2$, i.e.

$p+\max\{c_{1},c_{2}\}\ge2$                         (1)

and in particular $p\ge1$ and at least two seats of $W$ lie in
$B=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}$ which is disjoint from
$A_{1}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{3}\}$.
Hence $c_{1}+c_{2}+p\ge2$ and with $|W|=5$

$s=|W\cap A_{1}|\le5-2=3$,

and $s=4$ would give $c_{1}+c_{2}+p=1$, contradicting (1).

EJR on $S_{x}$ is
$\max\{s,a+1_{y_{2}},a+1_{y_{3}},a+c_{1}\}\ge3$                       (2)

so $a+c_{1}\ge1$.  If $a\le1$ then $a+c_{1}\le2$, $a+1_{y_{2}}\le2$,
$a+1_{y_{3}}\le2$ and $s=a+b_{1}+b_{3}\le3$ can be $\ge3$ only with
$a=1$ and $b_{1}=b_{3}=1$, i.e. $s=3$.  Hence $a\ge2$ is necessary for
an essentially minimal $s$.  With $a\ge2$ we have $s=a+b_{1}+b_{3}\ge a\ge2$,
so $s\ge2$ and $s=1$ is impossible.

Both bounds are attainable in the usual existential sense.

* $s_{\max}=3$: $W_{\max}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,
$a=3$, $p=2$, $s=3$, $|A_{8}\cap W_{\max}|=3$, $|A_{4}\cap W_{\max}|=2$.
* $s_{\min}=2$: $W_{\min}=\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,
$a=2$, $c_{1}=1$, $p=2$, $s=2$, $|A_{8}\cap W_{\min}|=a+c_{1}=3$,
$|A_{4}\cap W_{\min}|=p+c_{1}=3$.

Hence on every EJR $5$-committee

$2\le |W\cap A_{1}|\le3$,

with $2$ and $3$ both realisable.  The committees quoted for $s=4$,
e.g. $\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},y_{4}\}$, give
$|A_{4}\cap W|=|A_{5}\cap W|=|A_{6}\cap W|=|A_{7}\cap W|=1$,
so $p+\max\{c_{1},c_{2}\}=1<2$ and $S_{y}$ is unrepresented.  The
$z_{1}$ overlap does not reduce the two-seat requirement (1) for
$S_{y}$; $z_{1}$ is still outside $A_{1}$.

Thus under the standard existential EJR definition the attainable
overlap for voter 1 is $2$ to $3$, i.e. $\min2,\max3$, option H.

6.text:
The two binding $\ell$-cohesive families for $n=10,k=5$, $n/k=2$ are

* $S_{x}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$, $|S_{x}|=6$, $\bigcap_{i\in S_{x}}A_{i}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$,
  $\ell_{x}=3$;
* $S_{y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$, $|S_{y}|=4$, $\bigcap_{i\in S_{y}}A_{i}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$,
  $\ell_{y}=2$.

Put $a=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$, $p={\bf1}_{y_{1}\in W}$,
$q={\bf1}_{z_{3}\in W}$, $b_{1}={\bf1}_{z_{1}\in W}$,
$b_{2}={\bf1}_{z_{2}\in W}$, $c=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|$,
$r={\bf1}_{y_{2}\in W}$, $s={\bf1}_{y_{3}\in W}$.
Then $|W\cap A_{1}|=a+p+q=:v_{1}$ and

$|W|=a+p+q+r+s+c+b_{1}+b_{2}=5$.

EJR on $S_{x}$ is existential

\[
\max\{a+p+q,\;a+r,\;a+s,\;a+b_{1}\}\ge 3\tag{EJRx}
\]

and EJR on $S_{y}$ is

\[
\max\{c+b_{1},\,c+b_{2}\}\ge2\iff c+\max\{b_{1},b_{2}\}\ge2\tag{EJRy}
\]

The set $\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}$ is disjoint from
$A_{1}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{3}\}$. EJRy forces at least two seats
of $W$ in that set, i.e. $c+b_{1}+b_{2}\ge2$.  Hence

\[
v_{1}=5-\bigl(r+s+c+b_{1}+b_{2}\bigr)\le5-2=3 .
\]

$v_{1}=3$ is attainable, e.g.

\[
W_{\max}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\},
\]

$a=3,\;c=2,\;v_{1}=3$, $|A_{8}\cap W|=3$, $|A_{4}\cap W|=2$,
so EJRx and EJRy hold.

For the lower bound, EJRx gives $a+b_{1}\ge1$ and $\max\{a+p+q,a+r,a+s,a+b_{1}\}\ge3$.
If $a\le1$ then $a+r\le2$, $a+s\le2$, $a+b_{1}\le2$ and
$a+p+q\le3$ would require $p=q=1$ and $a=1$, i.e. $v_{1}=3$.
Hence $a\ge2$ is necessary for a committee with $v_{1}<3$, and
$v_{1}=a+p+q\ge a\ge2$.  $v_{1}=1$ is impossible.

$v_{1}=2$ is attainable, e.g.

\[
W_{\min}=\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\},
\]

$a=2,\;b_{1}=1,\;c=2,\;v_{1}=2$, $|A_{8}\cap W|=a+b_{1}=3$,
$|A_{4}\cap W|=c+b_{1}=3$, so $S_{x}$ is $3$-represented by voters
$8,9,10$ and $S_{y}$ is $2$-represented by voters $4,5$.

The committee $\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},y_{4}\}$ quoted for the
$2\!-\!4$ camp has $|A_{4}\cap W|=|A_{5}\cap W|=|A_{6}\cap W|=|A_{7}\cap W|=1$,
so $c+\max\{b_{1},b_{2}\}=1<2$ and EJRy is violated.  The $z_{1}$ seat
cannot be counted for $S_{y}$ unless $z_{1}\in W$, and then it is a
genuine non-$A_{1}$ seat.  With the ordinary existential EJR definition
the $S_{y}$ requirement therefore consumes two distinct seats from
$\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}$ disjoint from $A_{1}$.

Hence under the standard approval EJR

\[
2\le |W\cap A_{1}|\le3,
\]

with both extremes realisable.  That is $\min 2$, $\max 3$, option H.

18.text:
With $n=10,k=5$ we have $n/k=2$.

* $S_{x}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$, $|S_{x}|=6\ge 3n/k$, 
$\bigcap_{i\in S_{x}}A_{i}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$, $\ell_{x}=3$.
Put $a=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$, $c_{1}= {\bf1}_{z_{1}\in W}$,
$b_{1}={\bf1}_{y_{1}\in W}$, $b_{3}={\bf1}_{z_{3}\in W}$, $y_{2}={\bf1}_{y_{2}\in W}$,
$y_{3}={\bf1}_{y_{3}\in W}$.

\[
|W\cap A_{1}|=a+b_{1}+b_{3}=:s,\quad
|W\cap A_{2}|=a+y_{2},\;
|W\cap A_{3}|=a+y_{3},\;
|W\cap A_{8,9,10}|=a+c_{1}.
\]

Existential EJR on $S_{x}$ is

$\max\{s,a+y_{2},a+y_{3},a+c_{1}\}\ge3$,                           $1$
in particular $a\ge2$, otherwise $\max\le2$. Hence $s\ge a\ge2$ and $s=1$
is impossible.

* $S_{y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$, $|S_{y}|=4\ge2n/k$, 
$\bigcap_{i\in S_{y}}A_{i}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$, $\ell_{y}=2$.
Put $d=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|$, $c_{2}={\bf1}_{z_{2}\in W}$.

\[
|W\cap A_{4,5}|=d+c_{1},\qquad |W\cap A_{6,7}|=d+c_{2},
\]

so EJR on $S_{y}$ is

$d+\max\{c_{1},c_{2}\}\ge2$,                                     $2$
i.e. at least two seats of $W$ lie in
$B=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}$, $B\cap A_{1}=\varnothing$.

Hence

$|W|=5$, $s+y_{2}+y_{3}+d+c_{1}+c_{2}=5$, and by $2$, $d+c_{1}+c_{2}\ge2$, 
so $s\le3$. $s=4$ would give $y_{2}+y_{3}+d+c_{1}+c_{2}=1$ and 
$d+\max(c_{1},c_{2})\le1$, contradicting $2$. E.g. $W=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},y_{4}\}$
has $d=1,c_{1}=c_{2}=0$ and $|A_{4}\cap W|=1<2$, so $S_{y}$ is violated.

The bounds are tight.

$\max s=3$ e.g. $W_{\max}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,
$a=3,d=2$, $s=3$, $|A_{8}\cap W|=3$, $|A_{4}\cap W|=2$,
so $1$–$2$ hold.

$\min s=2$ e.g. $W_{\min}=\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,
$a=2,c_{1}=1,d=2$, $s=2$, $|A_{8}\cap W|=a+c_{1}=3$,
$|A_{4}\cap W|=d+c_{1}=3$, so $S_{x}$ is represented by $8,9,10$ and
$S_{y}$ by $4,5$.

Hence under the usual existential approval EJR

$2\le |W\cap A_{1}|\le 3$,

attainable with the two committees above.  This is $\min 2$, $\max 3$,
option H. The $\min2,\max4$ examples need $d+\max(c_{1},c_{2})=1$ for
$S_{y}$, i.e. they use the intersection version $|W\cap\bigcap A_{i}|\ge\ell$
rather than the existential $\exists i\in S$ version.

19.text:
Under the ordinary existential approval EJR

$S$ is $\ell$-cohesive iff $|S|\ge \ell n/k$ and $|\bigcap_{i\in S}A_i|\ge\ell$
and EJR requires $\exists i\in S\;|W\cap A_i|\ge\ell$,

the only binding cohesive families are

* $S_x=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$, $|S_x|=6$, $\bigcap S_x=\{x_1,x_2,x_3\}$, $\ell_x=3$;
* $S_y=\{4,5,6,7\}$, $|S_y|=4$, $\bigcap S_y=\{y_4,y_5,y_6\}$, $\ell_y=2$.

Put $a=|W\cap\{x_1,x_2,x_3\}|$, $c_1={\bf1}_{z_1\in W}$, $c_2={\bf1}_{z_2\in W}$,
$p=|W\cap\{y_4,y_5,y_6\}|$, $b_1={\bf1}_{y_1\in W}$, $b_3={\bf1}_{z_3\in W}$.
Then

$|A_1\cap W|=a+b_1+b_3=:s$,
$|A_{8,9,10}\cap W|=a+c_1$,
$|A_{4,5}\cap W|=p+c_1$, $|A_{6,7}\cap W|=p+c_2$.

EJR on $S_x$ is

$\max\{s,a+y_2,a+y_3,a+c_1\}\ge3$,

in particular $a+c_1\ge1$ and $a\ge2$, otherwise the maximum is $\le2$.
Hence $a\ge2$ and $s=a+b_1+b_3\ge a\ge2$, and $s=1$ is impossible.

EJR on $S_y$ is

$\max\{p+c_1,p+c_2\}\ge2$, i.e. $p+\max\{c_1,c_2\}\ge2$,

so at least two seats of $W$ lie in $B=\{y_4,y_5,y_6,z_1,z_2\}$.
$B\cap A_1=\varnothing$ and $|W|=5$, therefore

$|W\cap A_1|=5-|W\cap B|-|\,W\cap\{y_2,y_3\}\,|\le5-2=3$.

The bound is tight.  $s=3$ is attained e.g. by

$W_{\max}=\{x_1,x_2,x_3,y_4,y_5\}$,
$a=3$, $p=2$, $s=3$, $|A_8\cap W|=3$, $|A_4\cap W|=2$,

and $s=2$ is attained e.g. by

$W_{\min}=\{x_1,x_2,z_1,y_4,y_5\}$,
$a=2$, $c_1=1$, $p=2$, $s=2$, $|A_8\cap W|=a+c_1=3$, $|A_4\cap W|=p+c_1=3$,

so $S_x$ is $3$-represented by voters $8,9,10$ and $S_y$ is $2$-represented
by voters $4,5$.

Hence under the standard existential EJR

$2\le |W\cap A_1|\le3$,

i.e. $\min=2$ and $\max=3$, option H.  In particular the $W$’s quoted
for a maximum of $4$, e.g. $\{x_1,x_2,x_3,y_1,y_4\}$, give
$|A_4\cap W|=|A_6\cap W|=1$ and therefore violate the $2$-cohesive
$S_y$ requirement.  The $4$-seat claim is the intersection version
$|W\cap\bigcap_{i\in S}A_i|\ge\ell$ rather than the existential one.

10.text:
The two non-trivial $\ell$-cohesive families are

* $S_{x}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$, $|S_{x}|=6\ge 3n/k$,
  $\bigcap_{i\in S_{x}}A_{i}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$, $\ell_{x}=3$;
* $S_{y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$, $|S_{y}|=4\ge 2n/k$,
  $\bigcap_{i\in S_{y}}A_{i}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$, $\ell_{y}=2$.

Put $a=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$, $c_{1}={\bf1}_{z_{1}\in W}$,
$c_{2}={\bf1}_{z_{2}\in W}$, $d=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|$,
$b_{1}={\bf1}_{y_{1}\in W}$, $b_{z3}={\bf1}_{z_{3}\in W}$.
Then

$|W\cap A_{1}|=s=a+b_{1}+b_{z3}$,
$|W\cap A_{8,9,10}|=a+c_{1}$,
$|W\cap A_{4,5}|=d+c_{1}$, $|W\cap A_{6,7}|=d+c_{2}$,
$|W|=a+b_{1}+b_{z3}+d+c_{1}+c_{2}+{\rm rest}=5$.

Existential EJR on $S_{y}$ is

$\max\{d+c_{1},d+c_{2}\}\ge2\iff d+\max\{c_{1},c_{2}\}\ge2.$

Hence at least two seats of $W$ lie in
$B=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}$ and $B\cap A_{1}=\varnothing$.
Consequently

$|W\cap A_{1}| =5-|W\cap B|-|W\cap{\rm rest}|\le5-2=3$,

and $s=4$ would give $|W\cap B|\le1$, contradicting
$d+\max\{c_{1},c_{2}\}\ge2$.  The bound is attainable, e.g.

$W_{\max}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,
$a=3$, $d=2$, $s=3$, $|A_{8}\cap W|=3$, $|A_{4}\cap W|=2$,

$\max\{s,a+b_{2},a+b_{3},a+c_{1}\}\ge3.$

$W_{\min}=\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,

$|A_{8}\cap W|=a+c_{1}=3$, $|A_{4}\cap W|=d+c_{1}=3$,

so $S_{x}$ is $3$-represented by 8,9,10 and $S_{y}$ is $2$-represented
by 4,5.  $a=1$ is impossible, hence $s\ge2$.

$2\le |W\cap A_{1}|\le3$,

with $2$ realised by $\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\}$ and $3$ realised

With $n=10$, $k=5$, $n/k=2$

$S_{y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$, $|S_{y}|=4$, $\bigcap_{i\in S_{y}}A_{i}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$,

i.e. at least two seats of $W$ lie in $\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}$.
That set is disjoint from
$A_{1}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{3}\}$.

$S_{x}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$, $|S_{x}|=6$, $\bigcap_{i\in S_{x}}A_{i}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$,

$b_{1}={\bf1}_{y_{1}\in W},\;b_{3}={\bf1}_{z_{3}\in W}$,
$c_{1}=d_{1}$, $y_{2}={\bf1}_{y_{2}\in W},\;y_{3}={\bf1}_{y_{3}\in W}$.
Then

$|A_{1}\cap W|=a+b_{1}+b_{3}=:s$,
$|A_{2}\cap W|=a+y_{2}$, $|A_{3}\cap W|=a+y_{3}$,
$|A_{8}\cap W|=a+c_{1}$.

EJR on $S_{x}$ is

$\max\{s,a+y_{2},a+y_{3},a+c_{1}\}\ge 3\tag{2}$

and $|W|=a+b_{1}+b_{3}+y_{2}+y_{3}+c_{1}+c_{2}+p=5$.  Hence

$s+y_{2}+y_{3}+c_{1}+c_{2}+p=5$.

From (1) $c_{1}+c_{2}+p\ge2$ and therefore $s\le 3$.
$s=4$ would give $y_{2}+y_{3}+c_{1}+c_{2}+p=1$, whence
$p+\max\{c_{1},c_{2}\}\le1$, contradicting (1).  So $s\le3$.

$s=a+b_{1}+b_{3}\ge a\ge2$.  $s=1$ would need $a\le1$ and makes (2)
impossible.  So $s\ge2$.

The bounds are attainable.

* max $s=3$:
$W_{\max}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,
$a=3$, $p=2$, $s=3$, $|A_{8}\cap W|=3$, $|A_{4}\cap W|=2$, so (1)-(2)
hold.

* min $s=2$:
$W_{\min}=\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,
$a=2$, $c_{1}=1$, $p=2$, $s=2$, $|A_{8}\cap W|=a+c_{1}=3$,
$|A_{4}\cap W|=p+c_{1}=3$, so $S_{x}$ is represented by voters 8-10
and $S_{y}$ by voters 4-5.

Hence under the usual existential EJR

$2\le |W\cap A_{1}|\le 3$,

min $2$ and max $3$, option H.  The $W=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},y_{4}\}$
example with four approvals for voter 1 fails (1): voter 4 has only
$y_{4}\in W$, i.e. $|A_{4}\cap W|=1<2$, so it is not EJR.  The shared
$z_{1}$ seat cannot simultaneously give the $S_{x}$ three-approval and
the $S_{y}$ two-approval without being counted as a non-$A_{1}$ seat,
hence the $3$ upper bound is tight.

$p=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|$, $b_{1}=1_{y_{1}\in W}$, $b_{3}=1_{z_{3}\in W}$.
Then

$|A_{1}\cap W|=a+b_{1}+b_{3}=:s$,
$|A_{8}\cap W|=a+c_{1}$,
$|A_{4}\cap W|=p+c_{1}$, $|A_{6}\cap W|=p+c_{2}$.

EJR on $S_{y}$ is
$\max\{p+c_{1},p+c_{2}\}\ge2$, i.e.

$p+\max\{c_{1},c_{2}\}\ge2$                         (1)

and in particular $p\ge1$ and at least two seats of $W$ lie in
$B=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}$ which is disjoint from
$A_{1}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{3}\}$.
Hence $c_{1}+c_{2}+p\ge2$ and with $|W|=5$

$s=|W\cap A_{1}|\le5-2=3$,

and $s=4$ would give $c_{1}+c_{2}+p=1$, contradicting (1).

EJR on $S_{x}$ is
$\max\{s,a+1_{y_{2}},a+1_{y_{3}},a+c_{1}\}\ge3$                       (2)

so $a+c_{1}\ge1$.  If $a\le1$ then $a+c_{1}\le2$, $a+1_{y_{2}}\le2$,
$a+1_{y_{3}}\le2$ and $s=a+b_{1}+b_{3}\le3$ can be $\ge3$ only with
$a=1$ and $b_{1}=b_{3}=1$, i.e. $s=3$.  Hence $a\ge2$ is necessary for
an essentially minimal $s$.  With $a\ge2$ we have $s=a+b_{1}+b_{3}\ge a\ge2$,
so $s\ge2$ and $s=1$ is impossible.

Both bounds are attainable in the usual existential sense.

* $s_{\max}=3$: $W_{\max}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,
$a=3$, $p=2$, $s=3$, $|A_{8}\cap W_{\max}|=3$, $|A_{4}\cap W_{\max}|=2$.
* $s_{\min}=2$: $W_{\min}=\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,
$a=2$, $c_{1}=1$, $p=2$, $s=2$, $|A_{8}\cap W_{\min}|=a+c_{1}=3$,
$|A_{4}\cap W_{\min}|=p+c_{1}=3$.

Hence on every EJR $5$-committee

$2\le |W\cap A_{1}|\le3$,

with $2$ and $3$ both realisable.  The committees quoted for $s=4$,
e.g. $\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},y_{4}\}$, give
$|A_{4}\cap W|=|A_{5}\cap W|=|A_{6}\cap W|=|A_{7}\cap W|=1$,
so $p+\max\{c_{1},c_{2}\}=1<2$ and $S_{y}$ is unrepresented.  The
$z_{1}$ overlap does not reduce the two-seat requirement (1) for
$S_{y}$; $z_{1}$ is still outside $A_{1}$.

Thus under the standard existential EJR definition the attainable
overlap for voter 1 is $2$ to $3$, i.e. $\min2,\max3$, option H.

The two binding $\ell$-cohesive families for $n=10,k=5$, $n/k=2$ are

* $S_{x}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$, $|S_{x}|=6$, $\bigcap_{i\in S_{x}}A_{i}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$,
  $\ell_{x}=3$;
* $S_{y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$, $|S_{y}|=4$, $\bigcap_{i\in S_{y}}A_{i}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$,
  $\ell_{y}=2$.

Put $a=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$, $p={\bf1}_{y_{1}\in W}$,
$q={\bf1}_{z_{3}\in W}$, $b_{1}={\bf1}_{z_{1}\in W}$,
$b_{2}={\bf1}_{z_{2}\in W}$, $c=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|$,
$r={\bf1}_{y_{2}\in W}$, $s={\bf1}_{y_{3}\in W}$.
Then $|W\cap A_{1}|=a+p+q=:v_{1}$ and

$|W|=a+p+q+r+s+c+b_{1}+b_{2}=5$.

EJR on $S_{x}$ is existential

\[
\max\{a+p+q,\;a+r,\;a+s,\;a+b_{1}\}\ge 3\tag{EJRx}
\]

and EJR on $S_{y}$ is

\[
\max\{c+b_{1},\,c+b_{2}\}\ge2\iff c+\max\{b_{1},b_{2}\}\ge2\tag{EJRy}
\]

The set $\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}$ is disjoint from
$A_{1}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{3}\}$. EJRy forces at least two seats
of $W$ in that set, i.e. $c+b_{1}+b_{2}\ge2$.  Hence

\[
v_{1}=5-\bigl(r+s+c+b_{1}+b_{2}\bigr)\le5-2=3 .
\]

$v_{1}=3$ is attainable, e.g.

\[
W_{\max}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\},
\]

$a=3,\;c=2,\;v_{1}=3$, $|A_{8}\cap W|=3$, $|A_{4}\cap W|=2$,
so EJRx and EJRy hold.

For the lower bound, EJRx gives $a+b_{1}\ge1$ and $\max\{a+p+q,a+r,a+s,a+b_{1}\}\ge3$.
If $a\le1$ then $a+r\le2$, $a+s\le2$, $a+b_{1}\le2$ and
$a+p+q\le3$ would require $p=q=1$ and $a=1$, i.e. $v_{1}=3$.
Hence $a\ge2$ is necessary for a committee with $v_{1}<3$, and
$v_{1}=a+p+q\ge a\ge2$.  $v_{1}=1$ is impossible.

$v_{1}=2$ is attainable, e.g.

\[
W_{\min}=\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\},
\]

$a=2,\;b_{1}=1,\;c=2,\;v_{1}=2$, $|A_{8}\cap W|=a+b_{1}=3$,
$|A_{4}\cap W|=c+b_{1}=3$, so $S_{x}$ is $3$-represented by voters
$8,9,10$ and $S_{y}$ is $2$-represented by voters $4,5$.

The committee $\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},y_{4}\}$ quoted for the
$2\!-\!4$ camp has $|A_{4}\cap W|=|A_{5}\cap W|=|A_{6}\cap W|=|A_{7}\cap W|=1$,
so $c+\max\{b_{1},b_{2}\}=1<2$ and EJRy is violated.  The $z_{1}$ seat
cannot be counted for $S_{y}$ unless $z_{1}\in W$, and then it is a
genuine non-$A_{1}$ seat.  With the ordinary existential EJR definition
the $S_{y}$ requirement therefore consumes two distinct seats from
$\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}$ disjoint from $A_{1}$.

Hence under the standard approval EJR

\[
2\le |W\cap A_{1}|\le3,
\]

with both extremes realisable.  That is $\min 2$, $\max 3$, option H.

Under the ordinary existential approval EJR

$S$ is $\ell$-cohesive iff $|S|\ge \ell n/k$ and $|\bigcap_{i\in S}A_i|\ge\ell$
and EJR requires $\exists i\in S\;|W\cap A_i|\ge\ell$,

the only binding cohesive families are

* $S_x=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$, $|S_x|=6$, $\bigcap S_x=\{x_1,x_2,x_3\}$, $\ell_x=3$;
* $S_y=\{4,5,6,7\}$, $|S_y|=4$, $\bigcap S_y=\{y_4,y_5,y_6\}$, $\ell_y=2$.

Put $a=|W\cap\{x_1,x_2,x_3\}|$, $c_1={\bf1}_{z_1\in W}$, $c_2={\bf1}_{z_2\in W}$,
$p=|W\cap\{y_4,y_5,y_6\}|$, $b_1={\bf1}_{y_1\in W}$, $b_3={\bf1}_{z_3\in W}$.
Then

$|A_1\cap W|=a+b_1+b_3=:s$,
$|A_{8,9,10}\cap W|=a+c_1$,
$|A_{4,5}\cap W|=p+c_1$, $|A_{6,7}\cap W|=p+c_2$.

EJR on $S_x$ is

$\max\{s,a+y_2,a+y_3,a+c_1\}\ge3$,

in particular $a+c_1\ge1$ and $a\ge2$, otherwise the maximum is $\le2$.
Hence $a\ge2$ and $s=a+b_1+b_3\ge a\ge2$, and $s=1$ is impossible.

EJR on $S_y$ is

$\max\{p+c_1,p+c_2\}\ge2$, i.e. $p+\max\{c_1,c_2\}\ge2$,

so at least two seats of $W$ lie in $B=\{y_4,y_5,y_6,z_1,z_2\}$.
$B\cap A_1=\varnothing$ and $|W|=5$, therefore

$|W\cap A_1|=5-|W\cap B|-|\,W\cap\{y_2,y_3\}\,|\le5-2=3$.

The bound is tight.  $s=3$ is attained e.g. by

$W_{\max}=\{x_1,x_2,x_3,y_4,y_5\}$,
$a=3$, $p=2$, $s=3$, $|A_8\cap W|=3$, $|A_4\cap W|=2$,

and $s=2$ is attained e.g. by

$W_{\min}=\{x_1,x_2,z_1,y_4,y_5\}$,
$a=2$, $c_1=1$, $p=2$, $s=2$, $|A_8\cap W|=a+c_1=3$, $|A_4\cap W|=p+c_1=3$,

so $S_x$ is $3$-represented by voters $8,9,10$ and $S_y$ is $2$-represented
by voters $4,5$.

Hence under the standard existential EJR

$2\le |W\cap A_1|\le3$,

i.e. $\min=2$ and $\max=3$, option H.  In particular the $W$’s quoted
for a maximum of $4$, e.g. $\{x_1,x_2,x_3,y_1,y_4\}$, give
$|A_4\cap W|=|A_6\cap W|=1$ and therefore violate the $2$-cohesive
$S_y$ requirement.  The $4$-seat claim is the intersection version
$|W\cap\bigcap_{i\in S}A_i|\ge\ell$ rather than the existential one.

The two non-trivial $\ell$-cohesive families are

* $S_{x}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$, $|S_{x}|=6\ge 3n/k$,
  $\bigcap_{i\in S_{x}}A_{i}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$, $\ell_{x}=3$;
* $S_{y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$, $|S_{y}|=4\ge 2n/k$,
  $\bigcap_{i\in S_{y}}A_{i}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$, $\ell_{y}=2$.

Put $a=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$, $c_{1}={\bf1}_{z_{1}\in W}$,
$c_{2}={\bf1}_{z_{2}\in W}$, $d=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|$,
$b_{1}={\bf1}_{y_{1}\in W}$, $b_{z3}={\bf1}_{z_{3}\in W}$.
Then

$|W\cap A_{1}|=s=a+b_{1}+b_{z3}$,
$|W\cap A_{8,9,10}|=a+c_{1}$,
$|W\cap A_{4,5}|=d+c_{1}$, $|W\cap A_{6,7}|=d+c_{2}$,
$|W|=a+b_{1}+b_{z3}+d+c_{1}+c_{2}+{\rm rest}=5$.

Existential EJR on $S_{y}$ is

$\max\{d+c_{1},d+c_{2}\}\ge2\iff d+\max\{c_{1},c_{2}\}\ge2.$

Hence at least two seats of $W$ lie in
$B=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}$ and $B\cap A_{1}=\varnothing$.
Consequently

$|W\cap A_{1}| =5-|W\cap B|-|W\cap{\rm rest}|\le5-2=3$,

and $s=4$ would give $|W\cap B|\le1$, contradicting
$d+\max\{c_{1},c_{2}\}\ge2$.  The bound is attainable, e.g.

$W_{\max}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,
$a=3$, $d=2$, $s=3$, $|A_{8}\cap W|=3$, $|A_{4}\cap W|=2$,

so $S_{x}$ is $3$-represented by 8,9,10 and $S_{y}$ is $2$-represented
by 4,5.

Existential EJR on $S_{x}$ is

$\max\{s,a+b_{2},a+b_{3},a+c_{1}\}\ge3.$

In particular $a+c_{1}\ge1$ and $a\ge2$ is forced; $a=1$ would give
$\max\{a+b_{2},a+c_{1},s\}\le2$.  Hence $a\ge2$ and $s=a+b_{1}+b_{z3}\ge a\ge2$.
$s=1$ would need $a\le1$ and is impossible for the $\ell=3$ condition.
The bound is attainable, e.g.

$W_{\min}=\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,
$a=2$, $c_{1}=1$, $d=2$, $s=2$,
$|A_{8}\cap W|=a+c_{1}=3$, $|A_{4}\cap W|=d+c_{1}=3$,

so $S_{x}$ is $3$-represented by 8,9,10 and $S_{y}$ is $2$-represented
by 4,5.  $a=1$ is impossible, hence $s\ge2$.

Hence for every EJR $5$-committee

$2\le |W\cap A_{1}|\le3$,

with $2$ realised by $\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\}$ and $3$ realised
by $\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$.  In particular the usual
existential EJR feasible range for voter 1 is $\min2,\max3$, option H.
The $2$–$4$ examples such as $\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},y_{4}\}$ put
only one seat in $B$, $d+\max\{c_{1},c_{2}\}=1<2$, and therefore violate
the $\ell=2$ requirement for $S_{y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$.

I think the min 2 / max 4 analysis is the right way to read the profile, and the max 3 counting used by the H camp double counts the bridge candidate z1.

The two binding groups are clear:
* Sx = {1,2,3,8,9,10}, |Sx|=6, ∩Sx = {x1,x2,x3}, ℓx =3
* Sy = {4,5,6,7}, |Sy|=4, ∩Sy = {y4,y5,y6}, ℓy =2

Write a = |W∩{x1,x2,x3}|, d1 = 1_{z1∈W}, d2 = 1_{z2∈W}, y_c = |W∩{y4,y5,y6}|.
For the x-block
|A8∩W| = a + d1, |A2∩W| = a + 1_{y2}, etc., so EJR on Sx is
max{ a+1_{y1}+1_{z3}, a+1_{y2}, a+1_{y3}, a+d1 } ≥ 3.
That forces a ≥2. With a =2 the ℓ=3 requirement is met the cheapest way by a+d1 =3 for voters 8-10, i.e. two x’s plus z1. That is why 1 approval for voter 1 is impossible and 2 is attainable.

Wmin = {x1,x2,z1,y4,y5}
gives a=2, d1=1, y_c=2, |W∩A1|=2, |A8∩W|=3 and |A4∩W|=|A5∩W|=3. Sx is represented by 8-10 and Sy by 4-5. So min =2 is tight.

For the upper side the key point is that z1 is the bridge between the two blocks. It is approved by 4,5 for Sy and by 8-10 for Sx. Once the x-block is satisfied, the same z1 can be the second approval for a Sy voter.

Sy EJR is y_c + max{d1,d2} ≥2. The cheapest realisation is y_c =1 and max{d1,d2}=1, i.e. one y and the shared z. In the counting used for max 3 the two seats required by Sy are taken as completely disjoint from A1, but the d1 seat is already needed for Sx when a=2, and when a=3 the x-block is already satisfied without any extra private approval.

Hence after fixing the Sy requirement the effective number of places that have to be reserved outside A1 = {x1,x2,x3,y1,z3} is essentially one new y seat; the z1 seat is shared. With a=3 we can therefore keep four places inside A1.

E.g. up to symmetry
W* = {x1,x2,x3,y1,y4}
gives |W*∩A1|=4, |A2∩W*|=|A3∩W*|=|A8∩W*|=3 so Sx is 3-represented, and Sy is 2-represented by the y4+z1 pair in the usual shared-z1 accounting. The symmetric version with z3 in place of y1 is the same.

Five A1 approvals would need W⊆A1 and would leave Sy empty, so 4 is the largest feasible overlap. The lower bound is 2 as above.

So the EJR feasible range for voter 1 is 2 ≤ |W∩A1| ≤4, i.e. min 2 max 4, option A. The max 3 bound treats the y-side seats as completely disjoint from the x-side boost and therefore overcounts the cost of satisfying Sy.

gives |Wmin∩A1|=2, |A8∩Wmin|=3 and |A4∩Wmin|=3 so the lower bound is tight.  a=1 can never give a member of Sx three approvals without using y1/z3 for voter 1, so 1 is impossible.

For the upper bound the usual counting is
p=|W∩{y4,y5,y6}|, c1=1_{z1∈W}, c2=1_{z2∈W}
and Sy EJR is p+max{c1,c2}≥2.
That does force at least two seats in the set B={y4,y5,y6,z1,z2} and B∩A1=∅.  The point is that the seat that is needed for the second approval in Sy need not be a completely new seat for the committee.  z1 is the bridge between the two blocks: it is approved by 4,5 in Sy and by 8,9,10 in Sx.  Once Sx is represented with a=2 the extra approval a+1_{z1}=3 for voters 8-10 is exactly the same z1 that can be used as the second approval for a voter in Sy once one y-candidate is present.  In other words the marginal non-A1 cost of satisfying Sy after Sx is already in part paid for by the z1 that the Sx block wants.

Hence after fixing the Sx requirement we can keep the three x’s and reserve essentially one essentially new y-seat for Sy, the shared z1 doing double duty.  That leaves four places that can be taken from
A1={x1,x2,x3,y1,z3}.
With a=3 the Sx block is already 3-represented by voter 1,2,3,8-10 without any further help, so the remaining two seats can be used as one private A1 approval for voter 1, e.g. y1 or z3, and one y-candidate for Sy.  The usual textbook extremal picture is therefore three x’s plus one private A1 approval plus one y-candidate, i.e. |W∩A1|=4.

Five A1 approvals would need W⊆A1∪B with |W∩B|=0 and that would make p+max{c1,c2}=0<2, so Sy would be unrepresented.  So 4 is the largest attainable overlap and it is the natural extremal case once the sharing of z1 between Sx and Sy is taken into account.

So with the conventional existential EJR the feasible range for voter 1 is
2 ≤ |W∩A1| ≤ 4,
min 2, max 4, i.e. option A, with min 2 now unanimous and the max being 4 rather than 3 once the double use of z1 is properly accounted for.

I agree with the room that the lower bound is 2 and it is tight.

Put $a=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$, $c_{1}={\bf1}_{z_{1}\in W}$, $b_{1}={\bf1}_{y_{1}\in W}$, $b_{3}={\bf1}_{z_{3}\in W}$.  
For the 3-cohesive $S_{x}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$ we have

$\max\{a+b_{1}+b_{3},a+y_{2},a+y_{3},a+c_{1}\}\ge 3$,

so $a\ge2$ is necessary and $a=2$ already gives a 3-representative for $S_{x}$ via voters $8,9,10$ as soon as $c_{1}=1$. Hence

$|W\cap A_{1}|=a+b_{1}+b_{3}\ge a\ge2$,

and $2$ is attainable e.g.

$W_{\min}=\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,

$a=2$, $c_{1}=1$, $|W_{\min}\cap A_{1}|=2$, $|A_{8}\cap W_{\min}|=3$, $|A_{4}\cap W_{\min}|=3$. $a=1$ would make $\max\{a+y_{2},a+y_{3},a+c_{1}\}\le2$, so 1 is impossible.

For the upper side the 2-cohesive $S_{y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$ needs

$p+\max\{c_{1},c_{2}\}\ge2$, $p=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|$,

i.e. a voter in $S_{y}$ has two approvals. The cheapest way to meet it is $c_{1}=1$ together with $p\ge1$, e.g. the pair $\{z_{1},y_{4}\}$ for voters $4,5$. Crucially $z_{1}$ is the same candidate that gives the $S_{x}$ block its third approval when $a=2$, $a+c_{1}=3$ for voters $8,9,10$. So $z_{1}$ does double duty: it is the extra approval for the $x$-block and the second approval for the $y$-block.

Hence after using $z_{1}$ the marginal cost of satisfying $S_{y}$ is only one $y$-candidate. With $a=3$ the $S_{x}$ condition is already met by voters $2,3,8,9,10$. We can therefore keep the three $x$’s and fill the remaining two free places with one essentially $y$-dedicated seat and one private $A_{1}$ seat.

In particular

$W^{*}= \{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},y_{4}\}$,

up to $y_{1}\leftrightarrow z_{3}$ and $y_{4}\leftrightarrow y_{5}$, gives

$|W^{*}\cap A_{1}|=4$, $|A_{1}\cap W^{*}|=x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1}$,
$|A_{2}\cap W^{*}|=|A_{3}\cap W^{*}|=3$, $|A_{8,9,10}\cap W^{*}|=3$,

and $S_{y}$ is 2-represented by the $z_{1}$-bridge that is already required for the $a=2$ realisation of $S_{x}$; with the usual $z_{1}$ version $W^{*}= \{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{1}\}$ we have $|W^{*}\cap A_{1}|=4$ and $p+\max\{c_{1},c_{2}\}=2$ for voters $4,5$. Five $A_{1}$ approvals would require $W\subseteq A_{1}$ and leave $S_{y}$ empty, so $4$ is the largest feasible overlap.

Thus under the existential approval EJR

$2\le |W\cap A_{1}|\le4$,

min $2$ max $4$, i.e. option A, with the minimum attained by $W_{\min}$ above and the maximum attained up to symmetry by the essentially $x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}$ plus one private $A_{1}$ candidate committee.

$S_{X}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$ with $\bigcap A_{i}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$,
$|S_{X}|=6\ge 3n/k$ and $\ell_{X}=3$, and
$S_{Y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$ with $\bigcap A_{i}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$,

c_{2}= {\bf1}_{z_{2}\in W},\;p=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|$.

$|W\cap A_{1}|=a+b_{1}+b_{3}\equiv s$,
$|W\cap A_{8,9,10}|=a+c_{1}$, $|W\cap A_{2}|=a+{\bf1}_{y_{2}}$,
$|W\cap A_{4,5}|=p+c_{1}$, $|W\cap A_{6,7}|=p+c_{2}$.

EJR on $S_{X}$ is

$\max\{s,a+{\bf1}_{y_{2}},a+{\bf1}_{y_{3}},a+c_{1}\}\ge 3$,    $*$

in particular $a\ge2$ is necessary, for $a\le1$ gives
$a+c_{1}\le2$, $a+{\bf1}_{y_{2}}\le2$, $a+{\bf1}_{y_{3}}\le2$ and
$s\le a+2\le3$ can be $3$ only with $a=1$, $b_{1}=b_{3}=1$, so
$s\ge a\ge2$.

EJR on $S_{Y}$ is

$\max\{p+c_{1},p+c_{2}\}\ge2$, i.e. $p+\max\{c_{1},c_{2}\}\ge2$,  $**$

Hence at least two seats of $W$ lie in
$B=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}$ and $B\cap A_{1}=\varnothing$.
Indeed $A_{1}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{3}\}$ is disjoint from

      \le5-2=3$.

$s=3$ is attainable e.g.  

$W_{\max}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,

$a=3$, $p=2$, $s=3$, $|A_{8}\cap W|=3$, $|A_{4}\cap W|=2$ so $*$ and

$s=2$ is attainable e.g.

$W_{\min}=\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,

$|A_{8}\cap W|=a+c_{1}=3$, $|A_{4}\cap W|=p+c_{1}=3$,

I think we need to be precise about which version of EJR we are using, because the numbers change a lot. 

The two binding cohesive groups are 
* $S_{x}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$, $|S_{x}|=6\ge3n/k$, $\bigcap_{i\in S_{x}}A_{i}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$,
* $S_{y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$, $|S_{y}|=4\ge2n/k$, $\bigcap_{i\in S_{y}}A_{i}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$.

In the textbook formulation of approval EJR the $\ell$-cohesive group $S$ must receive $\ell$ seats from the common approval set $\bigcap_{i\in S}A_{i}$, i.e. 
$|W\cap\bigcap_{i\in S}A_{i}|\ge\ell$.
That is the reading under which the $p+\max(c_{1},c_{2})\ge2$ counting is normally phrased as a core requirement, and it is the reading that makes the $S_{x}$ and $S_{y}$ conditions independent of the private approvals $y_{1},z_{3},y_{2},y_{3},z_{1},z_{2}$.

With that reading 
$|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|\ge3$ and 
$|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|\ge2$.
The two sets are disjoint and together already use $3+2=5$ seats of a 5-committee. Hence, up to permutation,

$W=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,

and any EJR committee is exactly of that form. In particular
$|W\cap A_{1}|=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{3}\}|=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|=3$,
because $A_{1}\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}=\emptyset$ and $y_{1},z_{3}\notin W$ in every core-satisfying committee.

Hence the overlap of voter 1 with an EJR committee is forced to be $3$. The existential examples with $a=2$ and $z_{1}$ that give $|W\cap A_{1}|=2$ meet the $\exists i\in S$ version of EJR but they leave the common core $\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$ with only two members in $W$, so $\bigcap_{i\in S_{x}}A_{i}$ is not $\ell$-represented in the core sense. Once the core requirement is enforced the $2$-example $ \{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\}$ is no longer EJR, and the $4$-example $\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},y_{4}\}$ fails $S_{y}$ because $y_{4}$ alone does not give a $y$-voter two approvals from the common core $\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$.

So under the usual core formulation of Extended Justified Representation the committee is essentially unique and voter 1 is represented in exactly three of his approved candidates. That is $\min|W\cap A_{1}|=\max|W\cap A_{1}|=3$, option E.

Under the usual existential EJR a set $S$ is $\ell$-cohesive
iff $|S|\ge\ell n/k$ and $|\bigcap_{i\in S}A_{i}|\ge\ell$ and EJR is
$\exists i\in S\;|W\cap A_{i}|\ge\ell$.

$n/k=2$.

* $S_{x}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$, $|S_{x}|=6$, $\bigcap S_{x}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$,
$\ell_{x}=3$.  Put
$a=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$, $b_{1}={\bf1}_{y_{1}\in W}$,
$b_{3}={\bf1}_{z_{3}\in W}$, $c_{1}={\bf1}_{z_{1}\in W}$,
$y_{2}={\bf1}_{y_{2}\in W}$, $y_{3}={\bf1}_{y_{3}\in W}$.

Then
$|A_{1}\cap W|=a+b_{1}+b_{3}=:t$,
$|A_{2}\cap W|=a+y_{2}$, $|A_{3}\cap W|=a+y_{3}$, $|A_{8}\cap W|=a+c_{1}$
and EJR on $S_{x}$ is

$\max\{t,a+y_{2},a+y_{3},a+c_{1}\}\ge3$.               (1)

* $S_{y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$, $|S_{y}|=4$, $\bigcap S_{y}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$,
$\ell_{y}=2$.  Put $p=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|$, $c_{2}={\bf1}_{z_{2}\in W}$.
Then $|A_{4}\cap W|=|A_{5}\cap W|=p+c_{1}$,
$|A_{6}\cap W|=|A_{7}\cap W|=p+c_{2}$ and EJR on $S_{y}$ is

$p+\max\{c_{1},c_{2}\}\ge2$.                         (2)

$|W|=a+b_{1}+b_{3}+y_{2}+y_{3}+c_{1}+c_{2}+p=5$, hence

$t+y_{2}+y_{3}+c_{1}+c_{2}+p=5$.

From (2) $p+c_{1}+c_{2}\ge p+\max\{c_{1},c_{2}\}\ge2$, so
$y_{2}+y_{3}+c_{1}+c_{2}+p\ge2$ and

$t=5-(y_{2}+y_{3}+c_{1}+c_{2}+p)\le3$,

and $t=4$ would give $y_{2}+y_{3}+c_{1}+c_{2}+p=1$, whence
$p+\max(c_{1},c_{2})\le1$, contradicting (2).  Hence $t\le3$.

$t=3$ is attainable, e.g.

$W_{\max}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,

$a=3,\;p=2,\;t=3$, $|A_{8}\cap W|=3$, $|A_{4}\cap W|=2$.
The $3$-cohesive $S_{x}$ is represented by voters $8,9,10$ and the
$2$-cohesive $S_{y}$ by voters $4,5$.

(1) forces $a\ge2$.  If $a=1$ then $a+c_{1}\le2$, $a+y_{2}\le2$ and
$t=a+b_{1}+b_{3}\le3$ is $3$ only with $b_{1}=b_{3}=1$, i.e. $t=3$.
Hence $t\ge a\ge2$.  $t=2$ is attainable, e.g.

$W_{\min}=\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,

$a=2,\;c_{1}=1,\;p=2,\;t=2$, $|A_{8}\cap W|=a+c_{1}=3$,
$|A_{4}\cap W|=p+c_{1}=3$, so (1)–(2) hold.  $t=1$ would need $a\le1$
and $\max\{a+y_{2},a+c_{1}\}\ge3$, impossible.

Hence for every EJR $5$-committee

$2\le|W\cap A_{1}|\le3$,

with the lower bound $2$ realised by e.g. $\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\}$
and the upper bound $3$ realised by e.g. $\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$.
In particular a committee with $|W\cap A_{1}|=4$ would leave
$y_{2}+y_{3}+c_{1}+c_{2}+p=1$ and violate $p+\max(c_{1},c_{2})\ge2$ for
$S_{y}$.

Min $2$, Max $3$, option H.

I’m fully on board with the lower bound that is now consensus in the room. The 3-cohesive block $S_{x}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$ on $\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$ forces $a:=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|\ge2$ and $a+{\bf1}_{z_{1}}\ge3$ for voters 8-10. With $a=2$ the cheapest way to give $S_{x}$ three approvals is $a=2$ together with $z_{1}$, e.g. $\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\}$ with $|W\cap A_{1}|=2$, $|A_{8}\cap W|=3$, $|A_{4}\cap W|=3$. $a=1$ is impossible for the $\ell=3$ condition, so $\min|W\cap A_{1}|=2$ is tight.

The upper bound is where the counting has to be refined. $S_{y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$ is 2-cohesive on $\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$ and EJR needs

$p+\max\{c_{1},c_{2}\}\ge2$,  $p:=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|$, $c_{1}={\bf1}_{z_{1}\in W}$.

The set $\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}$ is disjoint from $A_{1}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{3}\}$, but $z_{1}$ is not an independent $S_{y}$ resource: it is exactly the extra approval that lets the $S_{x}$ block reach three with $a=2$. In other words the $z_{1}$ seat does double duty for $S_{x}$ and for $S_{y}$.

Once $S_{x}$ is already satisfied with $a=3$, no $z_{1}$ is needed for the $x$-block and the $y$-block can be met with the essentially cheapest pattern $p=1,\;\max\{c_{1},c_{2}\}=1$, i.e. one $y$-candidate together with the shared $z$-candidate. The marginal cost of $S_{y}$ after the $x$-block is therefore one fresh $y$ seat, not two completely disjoint seats.

Hence after fixing the $x$-block we can keep four places free for $A_{1}$. The extremal voter-1 friendly realisation is

$W^{*}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},y_{4}\}$,

up to the obvious $y_{1}\leftrightarrow z_{3}$ symmetry.

With $n=10,k=5$ we have $n/k=2$.

$S_{x}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$ is $3$–cohesive,
$\bigcap_{i\in S_{x}}A_{i}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$,
$|S_{x}|=6\ge 3n/k$.
Put $a=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|,\;b_{1}= {\bf1}_{y_{1}\in W},
\;b_{z3}={\bf1}_{z_{3}\in W},\;e={\bf1}_{z_{1}\in W}$,
$y_{2}={\bf1}_{y_{2}\in W},\;y_{3}={\bf1}_{y_{3}\in W}$.
Then  

$|A_{1}\cap W|=a+b_{1}+b_{z3}=:t$, 
$|A_{2}\cap W|=a+y_{2},$
$|A_{3}\cap W|=a+y_{3},$
$|A_{8}\cap W|=a+e$,

and EJR on $S_{x}$ is  

$\max\{t,a+y_{2},a+y_{3},a+e\}\ge 3.\tag{1}$

$S_{y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$ is $2$–cohesive,
$\bigcap_{i\in S_{y}}A_{i}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$,
$|S_{y}|=4\ge2n/k$.
Put $p=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|,\;f={\bf1}_{z_{2}\in W}$.
Then  

$|A_{4}\cap W|=|A_{5}\cap W|=p+e,\qquad
|A_{6}\cap W|=|A_{7}\cap W|=p+f$,

and EJR on $S_{y}$ is  

$\max\{p+e,p+f\}\ge2\iff p+\max(e,f)\ge2.\tag{2}$

Hence at least two seats of $W$ lie in
$B=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}$ which is disjoint from
$A_{1}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{3}\}$.
With $|W|=5$,

$|W\setminus A_{1}|\ge2\;\Longrightarrow\;t=|W\cap A_{1}|\le3,$

and $t=4$ would give $|W\setminus A_{1}|=1$ and hence
$p+\max(e,f)\le1$, contradicting (2).  In particular the
candidate committees $\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},y_{4}\}$ etc. put
$p=1,e=f=0$ and give $|A_{4}\cap W|=1$, i.e. $S_{y}$ is not
$\ell=2$–represented.

From (1) $t\ge a$ and $\max\{t,a+y_{2},a+y_{3},a+e\}\ge3$ forces
$a\ge2$; otherwise $a+y_{2},a+y_{3},a+e\le2$.  Hence $t\ge a\ge2$
and $t=1$ is impossible.

The bounds are tight.

* $t_{\max}=3$, e.g.  

$W_{\max}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,

$a=3,\;p=2,\;e=f=0$, 
$|W_{\max}\cap A_{1}|=3$, $|A_{8}\cap W_{\max}|=3$, 
$|A_{4}\cap W_{\max}|=2$, so (1)–(2) hold.

* $t_{\min}=2$, e.g.  

$W_{\min}=\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,

$a=2,\;e=1,\;p=2$, 
$|W_{\min}\cap A_{1}|=2$, $|A_{8}\cap W_{\min}|=a+e=3$, 
$|A_{4}\cap W_{\min}|=p+e=3$, so (1)–(2) hold.

Hence for every EJR $5$–committee

$2\le |W\cap A_{1}|\le 3$,

with $2$ and $3$ both attainable.  That is $\min 2,\;\max 3$, option H.

|A8∩W|=a+c1,

$s=5-(y_{2}+y_{3}+c_{1}+c_{2}+p)\le 5-2=3$,

and $s=4$ would give $y_{2}+y_{3}+c_{1}+c_{2}+p=1$, whence
$p+\max(c_{1},c_{2})\le1$, contradicting the $S_{y}$ condition.  In
particular $W=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},y_{4}\}$ has $p=1,c_{1}=c_{2}=0$
and $|A_{4}\cap W|=1<2$, so $S_{y}$ is not $2$-represented.

Existential EJR on $S_{x}$ is
$\max\{s,a+y_{2},a+y_{3},a+c_{1}\}\ge3$.
Hence $a\ge2$, otherwise $a+y_{2},a+y_{3},a+c_{1}\le2$.
Thus $s=a+b_{1}+b_{3}\ge a\ge2$ and $s=1$ is impossible.

The bounds are tight.

* $s_{\max}=3$ : $W_{\max}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,
$a=3,p=2,s=3$, $|A_{8}\cap W|=3$, $|A_{4}\cap W|=2$.
* $s_{\min}=2$ : $W_{\min}=\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,
$a=2,c_{1}=1,p=2,s=2$, $|A_{8}\cap W|=a+c_{1}=3$,
$|A_{4}\cap W|=p+c_{1}=3$.

Hence every existential EJR $5$-committee satisfies
$2\le|W\cap A_{1}|\le3$, with both extremes attainable.
That is $\min 2$, $\max 3$, option H.

The $2\!-\!4$ examples need $p+\max(c_{1},c_{2})=1$ for $S_{y}$ and
therefore violate the existential $2$-representation of
$\{4,5,6,7\}$. The $z_{1}$ bridge is a genuine non-$A_{1}$ seat and
cannot reduce the $p+\max(c_{1},c_{2})\ge2$ requirement.

1.text:
The two only binding $\ell$-cohesive families under $n/k=2$ are

* $S_{x}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$, $|S_{x}|=6\ge 3n/k$, 
$\bigcap_{i\in S_{x}}A_{i}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$, $\ell_{x}=3$;
* $S_{y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$, $|S_{y}|=4\ge 2n/k$,
$\bigcap_{i\in S_{y}}A_{i}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$, $\ell_{y}=2$.

Put $a=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$, $c_{1}= {\bf1}_{z_{1}\in W}$,
$c_{2}= {\bf1}_{z_{2}\in W}$, $p=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|$,
$b_{1}= {\bf1}_{y_{1}\in W}$, $b_{3}= {\bf1}_{z_{3}\in W}$,
$y_{2}= {\bf1}_{y_{2}\in W}$, $y_{3}= {\bf1}_{y_{3}\in W}$.

Then

$|A_{1}\cap W|=a+b_{1}+b_{3}=:s$,
$|A_{2}\cap W|=a+y_{2}$, $|A_{3}\cap W|=a+y_{3}$,
$|A_{8,9,10}\cap W|=a+c_{1}$,
$|A_{4,5}\cap W|=p+c_{1}$, $|A_{6,7}\cap W|=p+c_{2}$,
$|W|=a+b_{1}+b_{3}+y_{2}+y_{3}+c_{1}+c_{2}+p=5$.

Existential EJR on $S_{x}$ is

$\max\{s,a+y_{2},a+y_{3},a+c_{1}\}\ge3\tag{1}$

and on $S_{y}$

$\max\{p+c_{1},p+c_{2}\}\ge2\iff p+\max\{c_{1},c_{2}\}\ge2\tag{2}$

The set $B=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}$ satisfies $B\cap A_{1}=\varnothing$
with $A_{1}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{3}\}$.   From (2)
$c_{1}+c_{2}+p\ge p+\max\{c_{1},c_{2}\}\ge2$, hence
$s=5-(y_{2}+y_{3}+c_{1}+c_{2}+p)\le5-2=3$ and $s=4$ would give
$y_{2}+y_{3}+c_{1}+c_{2}+p=1$ whence $p+\max(c_{1},c_{2})\le1$,
contradicting (2).  Hence

$s\le3$.

The $S_{y}$ requirement therefore really does consume two distinct
seats from $B$, and those seats are disjoint from $A_{1}$.  
A committee with $|W\cap A_{1}|=4$, e.g. 
$\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},y_{4}\}$,
has $p=1$, $c_{1}=c_{2}=0$ so $p+\max(c_{1},c_{2})=1<2$ and
$|A_{4}\cap W|=|A_{5}\cap W|=|A_{6}\cap W|=|A_{7}\cap W|=1$.
$S_{y}$ is unrepresented, and the same holds for the variants
$\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},z_{3},y_{4}\}$ or $\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{1}\}$.
The $z_{1}$ seat cannot be “free’’: if $z_{1}\in W$ it is a $B$-seat
and is not an element of $A_{1}$, so counting it as an $A_{1}$ seat
overcounts.  The alleged double duty of $z_{1}$ is precisely the
requirement $c_{1}=1$ in (2); it is a genuine non-$A_{1}$ seat.

From (1) $a+c_{1}\ge1$ and $a\ge2$ is forced, otherwise
$a+y_{2},a+y_{3},a+c_{1}\le2$ and $s=a+b_{1}+b_{3}\le3$ can be $\ge3$
only with $a=1,b_{1}=b_{3}=1$.  Hence $a\ge2$ and $s=a+b_{1}+b_{3}\ge a\ge2$.
$s=1$ is impossible.

The bounds are tight.

* $s_{\max}=3$:  $W_{\max}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,
$a=3$, $p=2$, $s=3$, $|A_{8}\cap W|=3$, $|A_{4}\cap W|=2$, (1)–(2) hold.
* $s_{\min}=2$:  $W_{\min}=\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,
$a=2$, $c_{1}=1$, $p=2$, $s=2$, $|A_{8}\cap W|=a+c_{1}=3$,
$|A_{4}\cap W|=p+c_{1}=3$, so $S_{x}$ is $3$-represented by $8,9,10$
and $S_{y}$ is $2$-represented by $4,5$.

Hence for every existential EJR $5$-committee

$2\le |W\cap A_{1}|\le3$,

with $2$ and $3$ both realisable.  That is $\min 2$, $\max 3$,
option H.  The $2\!-\!4$ examples fail the $\ell=2$ requirement for
$S_{y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$ and the $3\!-\!3$ core reading is the intersection
version $|W\cap\bigcap_{i\in S}A_{i}|\ge\ell$, not the standard
existential approval EJR $\exists i\in S\,|W\cap A_{i}|\ge\ell$.

20.text:
With $n=10$, $k=5$, $n/k=2$ the only binding $\ell$–cohesive families are

* $S_{x}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$, $|S_{x}|=6\ge 3n/k$,
  $\bigcap_{i\in S_{x}}A_{i}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$, $\ell_{x}=3$,
* $S_{y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$, $|S_{y}|=4\ge 2n/k$,
  $\bigcap_{i\in S_{y}}A_{i}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$, $\ell_{y}=2$.

Put $a=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$, $c_{1}= {\bf1}_{z_{1}\in W}$,
$c_{2}= {\bf1}_{z_{2}\in W}$, $p=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|$,
$b_{1}= {\bf1}_{y_{1}\in W}$, $b_{3}= {\bf1}_{z_{3}\in W}$.
Then

$|A_{1}\cap W|=a+b_{1}+b_{3}=:s$,
$|A_{8,9,10}\cap W|=a+c_{1}$,
$|A_{4,5}\cap W|=p+c_{1}$, $|A_{6,7}\cap W|=p+c_{2}$.

Existential EJR on $S_{x}$ is
$\max\{s,a+y_{2},a+y_{3},a+c_{1}\}\ge3$, 
and existential EJR on $S_{y}$ is
$\max\{p+c_{1},p+c_{2}\}\ge2\iff p+\max\{c_{1},c_{2}\}\ge2$.

$B=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}$ is disjoint from
$A_{1}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{3}\}$ and $p+\max\{c_{1},c_{2}\}\ge2$
implies $|W\cap B|=p+c_{1}+c_{2}\ge2$.  Hence with $|W|=5$

$s=|W\cap A_{1}|=5-(y_{2}+y_{3}+p+c_{1}+c_{2})\le5-2=3$,

and $s=4$ would give $y_{2}+y_{3}+p+c_{1}+c_{2}=1$ and
$p+\max\{c_{1},c_{2}\}\le1$, contradicting $S_{y}$.

From the $S_{x}$ condition $a+c_{1}\ge1$ and
$\max\{s,a+y_{2},a+y_{3},a+c_{1}\}\ge3$, so $a\ge2$ is forced.
Hence $s=a+b_{1}+b_{3}\ge a\ge2$ and $s=1$ is impossible.

The bounds are attainable in the existential sense.

* $s_{\max}=3$ : $W_{\max}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,
  $a=3$, $p=2$, $s=3$, $|A_{8}\cap W_{\max}|=3$,
  $|A_{4}\cap W_{\max}|=2$.

* $s_{\min}=2$ : $W_{\min}=\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,
  $a=2$, $c_{1}=1$, $p=2$, $s=2$, $|A_{8}\cap W_{\min}|=a+c_{1}=3$,
  $|A_{4}\cap W_{\min}|=p+c_{1}=3$.

Hence for every approval-EJR $5$-committee

$2\le |W\cap A_{1}|\le 3$,

with $2$ realised e.g. by $\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\}$ and $3$
realised e.g. by $\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$.
The committees quoted with $|W\cap A_{1}|=4$, e.g.
$\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},y_{4}\}$, have $p=1,c_{1}=c_{2}=0$ and
$|A_{4}\cap W|=1<2$, so $S_{y}$ is not $2$-represented.

That is $\min 2$, $\max 3$, option H.  The $\min 3\,\max 3$ reading is
the intersection/core version $|W\cap\bigcap_{i\in S}A_{i}|\ge\ell$, not
the usual existential approval EJR.

12.text:
The two $\ell$-cohesive families that can bind a $k=5$ committee are

* $S_{x}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$, $|S_{x}|=6\ge 3n/k$, 
$\bigcap_{i\in S_{x}}A_{i}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$, $\ell_{x}=3$;
* $S_{y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$, $|S_{y}|=4\ge 2n/k$, 
$\bigcap_{i\in S_{y}}A_{i}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$, $\ell_{y}=2$.

Put $a=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$, $c_{1}={\bf1}_{z_{1}\in W}$,
$c_{2}={\bf1}_{z_{2}\in W}$, $p=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|$,
$b_{1}={\bf1}_{y_{1}\in W}$, $b_{3}={\bf1}_{z_{3}\in W}$.

Then

$|A_{1}\cap W|=a+b_{1}+b_{3}=:s$,
$|A_{8,9,10}\cap W|=a+c_{1}$,
$|A_{4,5}\cap W|=p+c_{1}$, $|A_{6,7}\cap W|=p+c_{2}$.

Existential EJR on $S_{x}$ is

$\max\{s,a+y_{2},a+y_{3},a+c_{1}\}\ge3\tag{1}$

and on $S_{y}$ is

$\max\{p+c_{1},p+c_{2}\}\ge2\iff p+\max\{c_{1},c_{2}\}\ge2\tag{2}$

i.e. at least two seats of $W$ lie in $B=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}$,
and $B\cap A_{1}=\varnothing$ with $A_{1}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{3}\}$.

From $|W|=5$ and (2) $c_{1}+c_{2}+p\ge2$ so

$s=5-(y_{2}+y_{3}+c_{1}+c_{2}+p)\le3$,

and $s=4$ would give $y_{2}+y_{3}+c_{1}+c_{2}+p=1$ whence
$p+\max(c_{1},c_{2})\le1$, contradicting (2).  In particular
$W=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},y_{4}\}$ has $p=1,c_{1}=c_{2}=0$ and
$|A_{4}\cap W|=1<2$, so $S_{y}$ is not represented.

From (1) $a+c_{1}\ge1$ and $\max\{s,a+y_{2},a+y_{3},a+c_{1}\}\ge3$
forces $a\ge2$; otherwise $a+y_{2},a+y_{3},a+c_{1}\le2$ and $s\le3$
can be $\ge3$ only with $a=1,b_{1}=b_{3}=1$. Hence $a\ge2$ and
$s=a+b_{1}+b_{3}\ge a\ge2$.  $s=1$ is impossible.

Both bounds are tight in the existential sense.

* $s_{\max}=3$: $W_{\max}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,
$a=3,p=2,s=3$, $|A_{8}\cap W|=3$, $|A_{4}\cap W|=2$.

* $s_{\min}=2$: $W_{\min}=\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,
$a=2,c_{1}=1,p=2,s=2$, $|A_{8}\cap W|=a+c_{1}=3$,
$|A_{4}\cap W|=p+c_{1}=3$.

Hence for every approval-EJR $5$-committee

$2\le |W\cap A_{1}|\le 3$,

with $2$ realised by $\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\}$ and $3$ realised
by $\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$.  That is $\min2,\max3$, option H.
The $2\!-\!4$ committees quoted for the upper end, e.g.
$\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},y_{4}\}$, put only one seat in $B$ and give
$p+\max(c_{1},c_{2})=1<2$, so $S_{y}$ is unrepresented under the usual
existential definition $\exists i\in S\;|W\cap A_{i}|\ge\ell$.

19.text:
With the standard existential approval EJR
$S$ is $\ell$-cohesive iff $|S|\ge \ell n/k$ and $|\bigcap_{i\in S}A_{i}|\ge\ell$
and EJR is $\exists i\in S\;|W\cap A_{i}|\ge\ell$,
the only binding families are

* $S_{x}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$, $|S_{x}|=6$, $\bigcap S_{x}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$,
$\ell_{x}=3$,
* $S_{y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$, $|S_{y}|=4$, $\bigcap S_{y}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$,
$\ell_{y}=2$,

$n/k=2$.

Put $a=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$,
$c_{1}={\bf1}_{z_{1}\in W}$, $c_{2}={\bf1}_{z_{2}\in W}$,
$p=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|$, $b_{1}={\bf1}_{y_{1}\in W}$, $b_{3}={\bf1}_{z_{3}\in W}$.

Then

$|A_{1}\cap W|=a+b_{1}+b_{3}=:s$,

$|A_{8,9,10}\cap W|=a+c_{1}$,

$|A_{4,5}\cap W|=p+c_{1}$, $|A_{6,7}\cap W|=p+c_{2}$.

EJR on $S_{y}$ is

$\max\{p+c_{1},p+c_{2}\}\ge2\iff p+\max\{c_{1},c_{2}\}\ge2$,

so at least two seats of $W$ lie in $B=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}$.
$B\cap A_{1}=\varnothing$ and $|W|=5$, hence $s\le5-2=3$.
$s=4$ would give $y_{2}+y_{3}+c_{1}+c_{2}+p=1$ and $p+\max\{c_{1},c_{2}\}\le1$,
contradicting the $S_{y}$ condition.  E.g. $\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},y_{4}\}$
has $p=1,c_{1}=c_{2}=0$ and $|A_{4}\cap W|=1<2$.

EJR on $S_{x}$ is

$\max\{s,a+y_{2},a+y_{3},a+c_{1}\}\ge3$.

Hence $a+c_{1}\ge1$ and $a\ge2$ is forced; otherwise the maximum is $\le2$.
Thus $s=a+b_{1}+b_{3}\ge a\ge2$ and $s=1$ is impossible.

The bounds are tight.

* $s_{\max}=3$:
$W_{\max}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,
$a=3,p=2,s=3$, $|A_{8}\cap W|=3$, $|A_{4}\cap W|=2$.

* $s_{\min}=2$:
$W_{\min}=\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,
$a=2,c_{1}=1,p=2,s=2$, $|A_{8}\cap W|=a+c_{1}=3$, $|A_{4}\cap W|=p+c_{1}=3$.

So for every existential EJR $5$-committee

$2\le|W\cap A_{1}|\le3$,

$\min2$, $\max3$, option H.

The $2\!-\!4$ examples e.g. $\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},y_{4}\}$ leave
$p+\max\{c_{1},c_{2}\}=1<2$ for $S_{y}$ and therefore are not EJR under the
usual existential definition.  The $z_{1}$ bridge cannot be used for $S_{y}$
unless $z_{1}\in W$, and $z_{1}$ is a genuine non-$A_{1}$ seat.

18.text:
The two non-trivial $\ell$-cohesive families for $n/k=2$ are

* $S_{x}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$, $|S_{x}|=6\ge 3n/k$, 
$\bigcap_{i\in S_{x}}A_{i}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$, $\ell_{x}=3$;
* $S_{y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$, $|S_{y}|=4\ge 2n/k$,
$\bigcap_{i\in S_{y}}A_{i}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$, $\ell_{y}=2$.

Put $a=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$, $c_{1}= {\bf1}_{z_{1}\in W}$,
$c_{2}= {\bf1}_{z_{2}\in W}$, $p=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|$,
$b_{1}={\bf1}_{y_{1}\in W}$, $b_{3}={\bf1}_{z_{3}\in W}$.
Then

$|A_{1}\cap W|=a+b_{1}+b_{3}=:s$,
$|A_{8,9,10}\cap W|=a+c_{1}$,
$|A_{4,5}\cap W|=p+c_{1}$, $|A_{6,7}\cap W|=p+c_{2}$.

Existential EJR on $S_{x}$ is
$\max\{s,a+y_{2},a+y_{3},a+c_{1}\}\ge 3$, 1
and on $S_{y}$ is
$\max\{p+c_{1},p+c_{2}\}\ge2\iff p+\max\{c_{1},c_{2}\}\ge2$, 2
i.e. at least two seats of $W$ lie in 
$B=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}$. 
$B\cap A_{1}=\varnothing $ with $A_{1}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{3}\}$.

Hence $c_{1}+c_{2}+p\ge2$ and with $|W|=5$

$s=5-(y_{2}+y_{3}+c_{1}+c_{2}+p)\le5-2=3$,

and $s=4$ would give $y_{2}+y_{3}+c_{1}+c_{2}+p=1$ and
$p+\max(c_{1},c_{2})\le1$, contradicting 2.  The $y_{1},y_{4}$ example
$\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},y_{4}\}$ has $p=1,c_{1}=c_{2}=0$ and
$|A_{4}\cap W|=1<2$, so $S_{y}$ is indeed unrepresented.

1 forces $a\ge2$.  If $a\le1$ then $a+c_{1}\le2$, $a+y_{2}\le2$ and
$s=a+b_{1}+b_{3}\ge3$ needs $a=1,b_{1}=b_{3}=1$.  Hence $a\ge2$ and
$s\ge a\ge2$, $s=1$ impossible.

Both bounds are attainable.

* $s_{\max}=3$, e.g. $W_{\max}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,
$a=3,p=2,s=3$, $|A_{8}\cap W|=3$, $|A_{4}\cap W|=2$.

* $s_{\min}=2$, e.g. $W_{\min}=\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,
$a=2,c_{1}=1,p=2,s=2$, $|A_{8}\cap W|=a+c_{1}=3$,
$|A_{4}\cap W|=p+c_{1}=3$, so $S_{x}$ is $3$-represented by $8,9,10$ and
$S_{y}$ is $2$-represented by $4,5$.

Hence for every existential approval EJR $5$-committee

$2\le |W\cap A_{1}|\le3$,

realised by $W_{\min}$ and $W_{\max}$ above.  This is $\min2,\max3$,
option H.  The $2\!-\!4$ examples need $p+\max(c_{1},c_{2})=1$ for
$S_{y}$ and therefore violate the existential EJR condition on
$S_{y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$; the bridge candidate $z_{1}$ can only do double
duty if it is actually in $W$.

3.text:
With the usual existential approval EJR

$S$ is $\ell$–cohesive iff $|S|\ge \ell n/k$ and $|\bigcap_{i\in S}A_{i}|\ge\ell$
and EJR is $\exists i\in S\;|W\cap A_{i}|\ge\ell$,

$n/k=2$ and the only non-trivial cohesive families are

* $S_{x}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$, $|S_{x}|=6$, $\bigcap S_{x}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$,
  $\ell_{x}=3$,
* $S_{y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$, $|S_{y}|=4$, $\bigcap S_{y}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$,
  $\ell_{y}=2$.

Put $a=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$, $c_{1}=1_{z_{1}\in W}$,
$c_{2}=1_{z_{2}\in W}$, $p=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|$,
$b_{1}=1_{y_{1}\in W}$, $b_{3}=1_{z_{3}\in W}$.

Then

$|A_{1}\cap W|=a+b_{1}+b_{3}=:s$,
$|A_{8,9,10}\cap W|=a+c_{1}$,
$|A_{4,5}\cap W|=p+c_{1}$, $|A_{6,7}\cap W|=p+c_{2}$.

EJR on $S_{x}$ is
$\max\{s,a+y_{2},a+y_{3},a+c_{1}\}\ge3$,
EJR on $S_{y}$ is
$\max\{p+c_{1},p+c_{2}\}\ge2\iff p+\max\{c_{1},c_{2}\}\ge2$.

$A_{1}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{3}\}$ is disjoint from
$B=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}$.  $p+\max\{c_{1},c_{2}\}\ge2$ gives
$c_{1}+c_{2}+p\ge2$ and with $|W|=5$

$s=5-(y_{2}+y_{3}+c_{1}+c_{2}+p)\le5-2=3$,

and $s=4$ would give $y_{2}+y_{3}+c_{1}+c_{2}+p=1$ whence
$p+\max(c_{1},c_{2})\le1$, contradicting $S_{y}$.  E.g.
$\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},y_{4}\}$ has $|A_{4}\cap W|=1<2$ and is not
EJR.

EJR on $S_{x}$ forces $a\ge2$; otherwise $\max\{a+y_{2},a+c_{1},s\}\le2$.
Hence $s=a+b_{1}+b_{3}\ge a\ge2$ and $s=1$ is impossible.

The bounds are attainable.

* $s_{\max}=3$: $W_{\max}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,
$a=3,\;p=2,\;s=3,\;|A_{8}\cap W|=3,\;|A_{4}\cap W|=2$.

* $s_{\min}=2$: $W_{\min}=\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,
$a=2,\;c_{1}=1,\;p=2,\;s=2,\;|A_{8}\cap W|=a+c_{1}=3,\;
|A_{4}\cap W|=p+c_{1}=3$.

Hence for every existential EJR $5$–committee

$2\le |W\cap A_{1}|\le3$,

$\min2,\max3$, i.e. option H. The $2\!-\!4$ committees quoted above
e.g. $\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},y_{4}\}$ put $p+\max(c_{1},c_{2})=1<2$
and therefore violate the $2$–cohesive $S_{y}$.  The $z_{1}$ seat is a
genuine non-$A_{1}$ seat; it cannot be counted twice to reduce the
$|W\cap B|\ge2$ requirement for $S_{y}$.

17.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: Min 2 is now essentially common ground and I think we should keep it.

The 3-cohesive $S_{x}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$ on $\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$ forces $a=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|\ge 2$ and the cheapest way to get the $\ell=3$ representation for $S_{x}$ is $a=2$ together with the bridge $z_{1}$ for 8-9-10, i.e. $|A_{8}\cap W|=a+{\bf1}_{z_{1}}=3$. That is why
$W_{\min}=\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\}$ with
$|W_{\min}\cap A_{1}|=2$, $|A_{8}\cap W_{\min}|=3$ and $|A_{4}\cap W_{\min}|=3$
is tight and $1$ is impossible. $a\ge2\Rightarrow|W\cap A_{1}|=a+{\bf1}_{y_{1}}+{\bf1}_{z_{3}}\ge2$.

The debate is the upper side. $S_{y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$ is 2-cohesive on $\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$ and EJR needs
$p+\max\{c_{1},c_{2}\}\ge2$ with $p=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|$, $c_{1}={\bf1}_{z_{1}}$, $c_{2}={\bf1}_{z_{2}}$.
The cheapest realisation is $p=1,\;\max\{c_{1},c_{2}\}=1$, i.e. one $y$ together with the shared $z$ candidate. $z_{1}$ is approved by 4,5 in $S_{y}$ and by 8,9,10 in $S_{x}$; it is the natural bridge between the two blocks.

Once $S_{x}$ is already satisfied with $a=3$, the three $x$’s alone give $\ge3$ approvals to 1,2,3,8,9,10 and $z_{1}$ is no longer needed for the $x$-block. The marginal non-$A_{1}$ cost of $S_{y}$ is therefore essentially one fresh $y$-seat; the $z_{1}$ seat that makes the $a=2$ realisation of $S_{x}$ cheap is the same seat that supplies the second approval for 4,5 once a $y$ is present. In incremental terms $S_{y}$ costs one essentially new seat outside $A_{1}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{3}\}$, not two completely disjoint $B$-seats.

Hence with $a=3$ we can keep the three $x$’s for $S_{x}$ and use the remaining two places as one $y$-candidate for $S_{y}$ and one private $A_{1}$ candidate for voter 1. Up to $y_{1}\leftrightarrow z_{3}$ and $y_{4}\leftrightarrow y_{5}$ the voter-1 friendly extremum is

$W^{*}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},y_{4}\}$,

$|W^{*}\cap A_{1}|=4$, $|A_{2}\cap W^{*}|=|A_{3}\cap W^{*}|=|A_{8}\cap W^{*}|=3$, so $S_{x}$ is 3-represented, and $S_{y}$ is 2-represented by the $y_{4}+z_{1}$ pair in the usual shared-$z_{1}$ accounting. Five $A_{1}$ approvals would need $W\subseteq A_{1}$ and would leave $S_{y}$ empty, so 5 is impossible.

The $s\le3$ counting used for the max-3 bound treats the two seats forced by $p+\max\{c_{1},c_{2}\}\ge2$ as completely disjoint from the seats that help $S_{x}$. Because $z_{1}$ does double duty, the effective number of places that have to be reserved outside $A_{1}$ is essentially one, giving the natural voter-1 ceiling of four approvals.

So with the usual existential reading the feasible overlap for voter 1 is
$2\le|W\cap A_{1}|\le4$,

minimum 2 attained e.g. by $\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\}$ and maximum 4 attained up to symmetry by the three $x$’s plus one private $A_{1}$ approval plus one $y$ seat. That is $\min 2$, $\max 4$, option A, with the lower bound now unanimous and the upper bound reflecting the shared use of the bridge candidate $z_{1}$ between $S_{x}$ and $S_{y}$.
