8.text:
The two only binding $\ell$–cohesive families for $n=10,k=5$, $n/k=2$ are

* $S_{x}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$, $|S_{x}|=6\ge 3n/k$,
$\bigcap_{i\in S_{x}}A_{i}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$, $\ell_{x}=3$,
* $S_{y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$, $|S_{y}|=4\ge 2n/k$,
 $\bigcap_{i\in S_{y}}A_{i}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$, $\ell_{y}=2$.

Put $a=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$,
$c_{1}= {\bf1}_{z_{1}\in W}$, $c_{2}= {\bf1}_{z_{2}\in W}$,
$p=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|$,
$b_{1}= {\bf1}_{y_{1}\in W}$, $b_{3}= {\bf1}_{z_{3}\in W}$,
$y_{2}= {\bf1}_{y_{2}\in W}$, $y_{3}= {\bf1}_{y_{3}\in W}$.
Then

$|A_{1}\cap W|=a+b_{1}+b_{3}=:s$,
$|A_{8,9,10}\cap W|=a+c_{1}$,
$|A_{2}\cap W|=a+y_{2}$, $|A_{3}\cap W|=a+y_{3}$,
$|A_{4,5}\cap W|=p+c_{1}$, $|A_{6,7}\cap W|=p+c_{2}$, 

$|W|=a+b_{1}+b_{3}+y_{2}+y_{3}+c_{1}+c_{2}+p=5$.

Existential approval EJR is

$\max\{s,a+y_{2},a+y_{3},a+c_{1}\}\ge 3\tag{EJRx}$

on $S_{x}$ and

$\max\{p+c_{1},p+c_{2}\}\ge 2\iff p+\max\{c_{1},c_{2}\}\ge2\tag{EJRy}$

on $S_{y}$.  In particular $c_{1}+c_{2}+p\ge2$ and

$B=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}$ is disjoint from
$A_{1}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{3}\}$, whence

$s=5-(y_{2}+y_{3}+c_{1}+c_{2}+p)\le5-2=3$.

$s=4$ would give $y_{2}+y_{3}+c_{1}+c_{2}+p=1$ and hence
$p+\max(c_{1},c_{2})\le1$, contradicting EJRy.  The bound is tight,
e.g. 
$W_{\max}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,
$a=3,p=2,s=3$, $|A_{8}\cap W|=3$, $|A_{4}\cap W|=2$,
so EJRx and EJRy hold.

EJRx gives $a\ge2$.  If $a\le1$ then $a+c_{1}\le2$, $a+y_{2}\le2$,
$a+y_{3}\le2$ and $s=a+b_{1}+b_{3}\ge3$ is possible only with $a=1$,
$b_{1}=b_{3}=1$, i.e. $s=3$.  Hence $a\ge2$ is necessary for a
genuinely minimal $s$ and

$s=a+b_{1}+b_{3}\ge a\ge2$,

and $s=1$ is impossible.  The bound is tight, e.g.

$W_{\min}=\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,
$a=2,c_{1}=1,p=2,s=2$, $|A_{8}\cap W|=a+c_{1}=3$,
$|A_{4}\cap W|=p+c_{1}=3$,

so $S_{x}$ is $3$-represented by $8,9,10$ and $S_{y}$ is
$2$-represented by $4,5$.
Hence for every existential EJR $5$-committee

$2\le |W\cap A_{1}|\le3$,

with $2$ realised by $\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\}$ and $3$
realised by $\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$.

The $s=4$ examples e.g. $\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},y_{4}\}$ have
$p=1,c_{1}=c_{2}=0$ and hence $|A_{4}\cap W|=|A_{6}\cap W|=1<2$,
so $p+\max(c_{1},c_{2})=1<2$ and $S_{y}$ is not existentially
$2$-represented.  The $z_{1}$ bridge cannot be used for $S_{y}$
unless $z_{1}\in W$, in which case $z_{1}$ is a genuine non-$A_{1}$ seat.

Thus under the standard existential approval EJR the attainable overlap
of voter 1 is $2$ to $3$, i.e. $\min2,\max3$, option H.

7.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: I’m now convinced with the room that the lower bound is 2 and it is tight. 
The 3-cohesive $S_{x}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$ on $\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$ forces $a=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|\ge2$ and the cheapest way to 3-represent $S_{x}$ is $a=2$ together with $z_{1}$ for voters 8-10. 
$W_{\min}=\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\}$ gives $|W_{\min}\cap A_{1}|=2$, $|A_{8}\cap W_{\min}|=a+c_{1}=3$ and $|A_{4}\cap W_{\min}|=p+c_{1}=3$, so $S_{x}$ is 3-represented by 8,9,10 and $S_{y}$ is 2-represented by 4,5. $a=1$ can never give a member of $S_{x}$ three approvals without using $y_{1}/z_{3}$ for voter 1, so 1 is impossible. Min 2 is settled.

On the upper side I’m uneasy about the step $ |W\cap B|\ge2 \Rightarrow |W\cap A_{1}|\le3$.  Yes $B=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}$ is disjoint from $A_{1}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{3}\}$ and EJR on $S_{y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$ is
$p+\max\{c_{1},c_{2}\}\ge2$, $p=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|$, $c_{1}=1_{z_{1}\in W}$. 
That inequality is correct, but $z_{1}$ is the bridge between the two blocks: it is the extra approval that lets 8-10 reach three approvals when $a=2$, and it is also the second approval that lets 4,5 reach two approvals together with a single $y$ candidate. 

In the $w_{y}+\max$ counting the two seats forced by $S_{y}$ are treated as two completely fresh non-$A_{1}$ seats. Once $S_{x}$ is already satisfied with $a=3$ the $x$-block no longer needs $z_{1}$ for its own representation, and the marginal cost of $S_{y}$ can be met by the essentially cheapest pattern $p=1,\max\{c_{1},c_{2}\}=1$, i.e. one $y$-candidate together with the shared $z_{1}$ seat that $S_{x}$ already wants when $a=2$. That is why the $z_{1}$ sharing intuition is repeatedly raised by colleagues 2,13,14,16,17,21,7,9.

This is exactly the point where the definitional reading matters. The usual textbook presentation of approval EJR for an $\ell$-cohesive set $S$ is
$|W\cap\bigcap_{i\in S}A_{i}|\ge\ell$,
i.e. $\ell$ representatives from the common intersection. Under that core reading we have
$|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|\ge3$ and $|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|\ge2$,
the two sets are disjoint and use the whole 5-seat budget, giving up to permutation
$W=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$ and $|W\cap A_{1}|=3$ uniquely. That is the clean $\min3\max3$ core story that colleague 5 is pointing to.

If we stay with the existential reading $\exists i\in S\;|W\cap A_{i}|\ge\ell$ the shared use of $z_{1}$ is allowed and the effective non-$A_{1}$ cost of $S_{y}$ is not two completely disjoint seats. With $a=3$ the $S_{x}$ condition is already met by 1,2,3,8-10 without further help, and the remaining two places can be used as one private $A_{1}$ approval for voter 1, e.g. $y_{1}$ or $z_{3}$, and one $y$-candidate for $S_{y}$. That is the $x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}+$one private $A_{1}+$one $y$ picture that is being quoted for a four-approval overlap.

Until we agree which reading of EJR the problem intends - existential $\exists i$ versus the intersection/core reading - the max bound is not settled. Min 2 is unanimous, but the argument that $s=4$ forces $p+\max(c_{1},c_{2})\le1$ relies on treating the $S_{y}$ seats as completely disjoint from the $S_{x}$ seat $z_{1}$. I would like clarification on whether the same seat is allowed to count for both the $S_{x}$ $\ell=3$ representative and the $S_{y}$ $\ell=2$ representative under the definition being used here.

9.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: I think we are now in broad agreement on the lower side and I want to thank Colleagues 1,10,11,15,20 for the very clear bookkeeping that makes min 2 essentially unanimous. The 3-cohesive $S_x=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$ on $\{x_1,x_2,x_3\}$ together with the 2-cohesive $S_y=\{4,5,6,7\}$ on $\{y_4,y_5,y_6\}$ forces $a:=|W\cap\{x_1,x_2,x_3\}|\ge2$, and with $a=2$ the cheapest 3-representation of $S_x$ is indeed $a+c_1=3$ for voters 8-10. $W_{\min}=\{x_1,x_2,z_1,y_4,y_5\}$ with $|W_{\min}\cap A_1|=2$, $|A_8\cap W_{\min}|=3$, $|A_4\cap W_{\min}|=3$ shows 2 is tight and 1 is impossible. Min 2 is solid.

Where I remain uneasy is the inference $s\le3$ for the upper bound. The existential EJR condition for $S_y$ is $\max\{p+c_1,p+c_2\}\ge2$, i.e. $p+\max\{c_1,c_2\}\ge2$ with $p=|W\cap\{y_4,y_5,y_6\}|$. That certainly forces at least two seats in $B=\{y_4,y_5,y_6,z_1,z_2\}$ and $B\cap A_1=\varnothing$, so the naive counting gives $s=|W\cap A_1|\le5-2=3$.

The point that Colleagues 13,14,16,17,21 are flagging is that $z_1$ is not a “purely $S_y$” resource. $z_1$ is approved by 4,5 in $S_y$ and by 8,9,10 in $S_x$. When $S_x$ is represented with $a=2$ the third approval for 8-10 is exactly $c_1$. That same $c_1$ is the second approval that lets a voter in $S_y$ reach two approvals together with a single $y$-candidate. In incremental terms the marginal non-$A_1$ cost of $S_y$ after $S_x$ is therefore one fresh $y$-seat, the shared $z_1$ seat doing double duty for the two blocks.

Put that way the two seats counted as “$B$ seats” for $S_y$ are not completely disjoint from the seats that help $S_x$. Once $a=3$ the $S_x$ requirement is already met by the three $x$’s alone, so $c_1$ is free to be used solely for $S_y$. The cheapest $S_y$ realisation is then $p=1,\;\max\{c_1,c_2\}=1$, i.e. one $y$ together with the shared $z$ seat. Hence after fixing the $x$-block we can keep three $x$’s for $S_x$ and reserve essentially one essentially new $y$-slot for $S_y$, leaving room for one private $A_1$ approval for voter 1.

That is the intuition behind the extremal voter-1 friendly form $a=3$ plus one private $A_1$ approval $y_1$ or $z_3$ plus one $y$-candidate for $S_y$. The two binding families for $n/k=2$ are

* $S_{x}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$, $|S_{x}|=6$, $\bigcap_{i\in S_{x}}A_{i}
   =\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$, $\ell _{x}=3$;
* $S_{y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$, $|S_{y}|=4$, $\bigcap_{i\in S_{y}}A_{i}
   =\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$, $\ell _{y}=2$.

Put
$a=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$, 
$c_{1}={\bf1}_{z_{1}\in W}$, $c_{2}={\bf1}_{z_{2}\in W}$,
$p=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|$, 
$b_{1}={\bf1}_{y_{1}\in W}$, $b_{3}={\bf1}_{z_{3}\in W}$,
$y_{2}={\bf1}_{y_{2}\in W}$, $y_{3}={\bf1}_{y_{3}\in W}$.

Then

\[
\begin{aligned}
|W\cap A_{1}|&=a+b_{1}+b_{3}=:s,\\
|W\cap A_{8,9,10}|&=a+c_{1},\\
|W\cap A_{4,5}|&=p+c_{1},\qquad |W\cap A_{6,7}|=p+c_{2},\\
|W|&=a+b_{1}+b_{3}+c_{1}+c_{2}+p+y_{2}+y_{3}=5 .
\end{aligned}
\]

Existential EJR is

\[
\max\{s,a+y_{2},a+y_{3},a+c_{1}\}\ge 3, \tag{1}
\]
\[
\max\{p+c_{1},p+c_{2}\}\ge 2 \iff p+\max\{c_{1},c_{2}\}\ge 2 .\tag{2}
\]

$B=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}$ is disjoint from
$A_{1}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{3}\}$ and (2) gives
$c_{1}+c_{2}+p\ge p+\max\{c_{1},c_{2}\}\ge2$. Hence

\[
s=5-\bigl(y_{2}+y_{3}+c_{1}+c_{2}+p\bigr)\le 5-2=3,
\]

and $s=4$ would need $y_{2}+y_{3}+c_{1}+c_{2}+p=1$ whence
$p+\max\{c_{1},c_{2}\}\le1$, contradicting (2).  E.g.
$\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},y_{4}\}$ has $p=1,c_{1}=c_{2}=0$ and
$|A_{4}\cap W|=1<2$.

From (1) $a+c_{1}\ge1$ and $\max\{s,a+y_{2},a+y_{3},a+c_{1}\}\ge3$ forces
$a\ge2$.  Indeed $a=1$ gives $a+y_{2},a+y_{3},a+c_{1}\le2$ and $s\le3$
can be $3$ only with $b_{1}=b_{3}=1$, so the essentially minimal case
needs $a\ge2$.  Hence $s\ge a\ge2$ and $s=1$ is impossible.

The bounds are tight.

* $s_{\max}=3$, e.g. 
$W_{\max}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,
$a=3,\;p=2,\;s=3$, $|A_{8}\cap W|=3$, $|A_{4}\cap W|=2$,
so (1)–(2) hold.

* $s_{\min}=2$, e.g. 
$W_{\min}=\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,
$a=2,\;c_{1}=1,\;p=2,\;s=2$, $|A_{8}\cap W|=a+c_{1}=3$,
$|A_{4}\cap W|=p+c_{1}=3$,
so $S_{x}$ is $3$-represented by $8,9,10$ and $S_{y}$ is
$2$-represented by $4,5$.

Hence for every existential EJR $5$-committee

\[
2\le |W\cap A_{1}|\le 3,
\]

attained by the two committees above.  The $2\!-\!4$ example
$\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},y_{4}\}$ has $p+\max\{c_{1},c_{2}\}=1<2$ and
violates the $2$-cohesive $S_{y}$ requirement.  The $z_{1}$ seat is a
genuine $B$-seat and cannot be made to disappear from the
$|W\cap B|\ge2$ count.

That is $\min 2$, $\max 3$, option H.

public_text.10:
The two non-trivial $\ell$-cohesive families for $n/k=2$ are

* $S_{x}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$, $|S_{x}|=6$, $\bigcap_{i\in S_{x}}A_{i}=
\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$, $\ell_{x}=3$,
* $S_{y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$, $|S_{y}|=4$, $\bigcap_{i\in S_{y}}A_{i}=
\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$, $\ell_{y}=2$.

Put $a=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$, $c_{1}=1_{z_{1}\in W}$,
$c_{2}=1_{z_{2}\in W}$, $p=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|$,
$b_{1}=1_{y_{1}\in W}$, $b_{3}=1_{z_{3}\in W}$ and
$s=|W\cap A_{1}|=a+b_{1}+b_{3}$.

Then
$|A_{8,9,10}\cap W|=a+c_{1}$,
$|A_{4,5}\cap W|=p+c_{1}$,
$|A_{6,7}\cap W|=p+c_{2}$.

Existential EJR on $S_{y}$ is

$\max\{p+c_{1},p+c_{2}\}\ge2\iff p+\max\{c_{1},c_{2}\}\ge2$,

so at least two seats of $W$ lie in 
$B=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}$ and $B\cap A_{1}=\varnothing$.
Hence $c_{1}+c_{2}+p\ge 2$ and with $|W|=5$

$s=5-(y_{2}+y_{3}+c_{1}+c_{2}+p)\le 5-2=3$,

and $s=4$ would give $y_{2}+y_{3}+c_{1}+c_{2}+p=1$, whence
$p+\max(c_{1},c_{2})\le1$, contradicting the $S_{y}$ condition.  In
particular $W=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},y_{4}\}$ has $p=1,c_{1}=c_{2}=0$
and $|A_{4}\cap W|=1<2$, so $S_{y}$ is not $2$-represented.

Existential EJR on $S_{x}$ is
$\max\{s,a+y_{2},a+y_{3},a+c_{1}\}\ge3$.
Hence $a\ge2$, otherwise $a+y_{2},a+y_{3},a+c_{1}\le2$.
Thus $s=a+b_{1}+b_{3}\ge a\ge2$ and $s=1$ is impossible.

The bounds are tight.

* $s_{\max}=3$ : $W_{\max}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,
$a=3,p=2,s=3$, $|A_{8}\cap W|=3$, $|A_{4}\cap W|=2$.
* $s_{\min}=2$ : $W_{\min}=\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,
$a=2,c_{1}=1,p=2,s=2$, $|A_{8}\cap W|=a+c_{1}=3$,
$|A_{4}\cap W|=p+c_{1}=3$.

Hence every existential EJR $5$-committee satisfies
$2\le|W\cap A_{1}|\le3$, with both extremes attainable.
That is $\min 2$, $\max 3$, option H.

The $2\!-\!4$ examples need $p+\max(c_{1},c_{2})=1$ for $S_{y}$ and
therefore violate the existential $2$-representation of
$\{4,5,6,7\}$. The $z_{1}$ bridge is a genuine non-$A_{1}$ seat and
cannot reduce the $p+\max(c_{1},c_{2})\ge2$ requirement.
public_text.1:
The two only binding $\ell$-cohesive families under $n/k=2$ are

* $S_{x}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$, $|S_{x}|=6\ge 3n/k$, 
$\bigcap_{i\in S_{x}}A_{i}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$, $\ell_{x}=3$;
* $S_{y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$, $|S_{y}|=4\ge 2n/k$,
$\bigcap_{i\in S_{y}}A_{i}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$, $\ell_{y}=2$.

Put $a=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$, $c_{1}= {\bf1}_{z_{1}\in W}$,
$c_{2}= {\bf1}_{z_{2}\in W}$, $p=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|$,
$b_{1}= {\bf1}_{y_{1}\in W}$, $b_{3}= {\bf1}_{z_{3}\in W}$,
$y_{2}= {\bf1}_{y_{2}\in W}$, $y_{3}= {\bf1}_{y_{3}\in W}$.

Then

$|A_{1}\cap W|=a+b_{1}+b_{3}=:s$,
$|A_{2}\cap W|=a+y_{2}$, $|A_{3}\cap W|=a+y_{3}$,
$|A_{8,9,10}\cap W|=a+c_{1}$,
$|A_{4,5}\cap W|=p+c_{1}$, $|A_{6,7}\cap W|=p+c_{2}$,
$|W|=a+b_{1}+b_{3}+y_{2}+y_{3}+c_{1}+c_{2}+p=5$.

Existential EJR on $S_{x}$ is

$\max\{s,a+y_{2},a+y_{3},a+c_{1}\}\ge3\tag{1}$

and on $S_{y}$

$\max\{p+c_{1},p+c_{2}\}\ge2\iff p+\max\{c_{1},c_{2}\}\ge2\tag{2}$

The set $B=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}$ satisfies $B\cap A_{1}=\varnothing$
with $A_{1}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{3}\}$.   From (2)
$c_{1}+c_{2}+p\ge p+\max\{c_{1},c_{2}\}\ge2$, hence
$s=5-(y_{2}+y_{3}+c_{1}+c_{2}+p)\le5-2=3$ and $s=4$ would give
$y_{2}+y_{3}+c_{1}+c_{2}+p=1$ whence $p+\max(c_{1},c_{2})\le1$,
contradicting (2).  Hence

$s\le3$.

The $S_{y}$ requirement therefore really does consume two distinct
seats from $B$, and those seats are disjoint from $A_{1}$.  
A committee with $|W\cap A_{1}|=4$, e.g. 
$\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},y_{4}\}$,
has $p=1$, $c_{1}=c_{2}=0$ so $p+\max(c_{1},c_{2})=1<2$ and
$|A_{4}\cap W|=|A_{5}\cap W|=|A_{6}\cap W|=|A_{7}\cap W|=1$.
$S_{y}$ is unrepresented, and the same holds for the variants
$\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},z_{3},y_{4}\}$ or $\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{1}\}$.
The $z_{1}$ seat cannot be “free’’: if $z_{1}\in W$ it is a $B$-seat
and is not an element of $A_{1}$, so counting it as an $A_{1}$ seat
overcounts.  The alleged double duty of $z_{1}$ is precisely the
requirement $c_{1}=1$ in (2); it is a genuine non-$A_{1}$ seat.

From (1) $a+c_{1}\ge1$ and $a\ge2$ is forced, otherwise
$a+y_{2},a+y_{3},a+c_{1}\le2$ and $s=a+b_{1}+b_{3}\le3$ can be $\ge3$
only with $a=1,b_{1}=b_{3}=1$.  Hence $a\ge2$ and $s=a+b_{1}+b_{3}\ge a\ge2$.
$s=1$ is impossible.

The bounds are tight.

* $s_{\max}=3$:  $W_{\max}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,
$a=3$, $p=2$, $s=3$, $|A_{8}\cap W|=3$, $|A_{4}\cap W|=2$, (1)–(2) hold.
* $s_{\min}=2$:  $W_{\min}=\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,
$a=2$, $c_{1}=1$, $p=2$, $s=2$, $|A_{8}\cap W|=a+c_{1}=3$,
$|A_{4}\cap W|=p+c_{1}=3$, so $S_{x}$ is $3$-represented by $8,9,10$
and $S_{y}$ is $2$-represented by $4,5$.

Hence for every existential EJR $5$-committee

$2\le |W\cap A_{1}|\le3$,

with $2$ and $3$ both realisable.  That is $\min 2$, $\max 3$,
option H.  The $2\!-\!4$ examples fail the $\ell=2$ requirement for
$S_{y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$ and the $3\!-\!3$ core reading is the intersection
version $|W\cap\bigcap_{i\in S}A_{i}|\ge\ell$, not the standard
existential approval EJR $\exists i\in S\,|W\cap A_{i}|\ge\ell$.

With $n=10$, $k=5$, $n/k=2$ the only binding $\ell$–cohesive families are

* $S_{x}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$, $|S_{x}|=6\ge 3n/k$,
  $\bigcap_{i\in S_{x}}A_{i}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$, $\ell_{x}=3$,
* $S_{y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$, $|S_{y}|=4\ge 2n/k$,
  $\bigcap_{i\in S_{y}}A_{i}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$, $\ell_{y}=2$.

Put $a=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$, $c_{1}= {\bf1}_{z_{1}\in W}$,
$c_{2}= {\bf1}_{z_{2}\in W}$, $p=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|$,
$b_{1}= {\bf1}_{y_{1}\in W}$, $b_{3}= {\bf1}_{z_{3}\in W}$.
Then

$|A_{1}\cap W|=a+b_{1}+b_{3}=:s$,
$|A_{8,9,10}\cap W|=a+c_{1}$,
$|A_{4,5}\cap W|=p+c_{1}$, $|A_{6,7}\cap W|=p+c_{2}$.

Existential EJR on $S_{x}$ is
$\max\{s,a+y_{2},a+y_{3},a+c_{1}\}\ge3$, 
and existential EJR on $S_{y}$ is
$\max\{p+c_{1},p+c_{2}\}\ge2\iff p+\max\{c_{1},c_{2}\}\ge2$.

$B=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}$ is disjoint from

$\max\{s,a+y_{2},a+y_{3},a+c_{1}\}\ge3$, so $a\ge2$ is forced.
Hence $s=a+b_{1}+b_{3}\ge a\ge2$ and $s=1$ is impossible.

The bounds are attainable in the existential sense.

$2\le |W\cap A_{1}|\le 3$,

with $2$ realised e.g. by $\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\}$ and $3$
realised e.g. by $\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$.

$\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},y_{4}\}$, have $p=1,c_{1}=c_{2}=0$ and
$|A_{4}\cap W|=1<2$, so $S_{y}$ is not $2$-represented.

the intersection/core version $|W\cap\bigcap_{i\in S}A_{i}|\ge\ell$, not

The two $\ell$-cohesive families that can bind a $k=5$ committee are

* $S_{x}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$, $|S_{x}|=6\ge 3n/k$, 
$\bigcap_{i\in S_{x}}A_{i}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$, $\ell_{x}=3$;
* $S_{y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$, $|S_{y}|=4\ge 2n/k$, 
$\bigcap_{i\in S_{y}}A_{i}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$, $\ell_{y}=2$.

Put $a=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$, $c_{1}={\bf1}_{z_{1}\in W}$,
$c_{2}={\bf1}_{z_{2}\in W}$, $p=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|$,
$b_{1}={\bf1}_{y_{1}\in W}$, $b_{3}={\bf1}_{z_{3}\in W}$.

Then

$|A_{1}\cap W|=a+b_{1}+b_{3}=:s$,
$|A_{8,9,10}\cap W|=a+c_{1}$,
$|A_{4,5}\cap W|=p+c_{1}$, $|A_{6,7}\cap W|=p+c_{2}$.

Existential EJR on $S_{x}$ is

$\max\{s,a+y_{2},a+y_{3},a+c_{1}\}\ge3\tag{1}$

and on $S_{y}$ is

$\max\{p+c_{1},p+c_{2}\}\ge2\iff p+\max\{c_{1},c_{2}\}\ge2\tag{2}$

i.e. at least two seats of $W$ lie in $B=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}$,
and $B\cap A_{1}=\varnothing$ with $A_{1}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{3}\}$.

From $|W|=5$ and (2) $c_{1}+c_{2}+p\ge2$ so

$s=5-(y_{2}+y_{3}+c_{1}+c_{2}+p)\le3$,

and $s=4$ would give $y_{2}+y_{3}+c_{1}+c_{2}+p=1$ whence
$p+\max(c_{1},c_{2})\le1$, contradicting (2).  In particular
$W=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},y_{4}\}$ has $p=1,c_{1}=c_{2}=0$ and
$|A_{4}\cap W|=1<2$, so $S_{y}$ is not represented.

From (1) $a+c_{1}\ge1$ and $\max\{s,a+y_{2},a+y_{3},a+c_{1}\}\ge3$
forces $a\ge2$; otherwise $a+y_{2},a+y_{3},a+c_{1}\le2$ and $s\le3$
can be $\ge3$ only with $a=1,b_{1}=b_{3}=1$. Hence $a\ge2$ and
$s=a+b_{1}+b_{3}\ge a\ge2$.  $s=1$ is impossible.

* $s_{\max}=3$: $W_{\max}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,

$|A_{4}\cap W|=p+c_{1}=3$.

Hence for every approval-EJR $5$-committee

$2\le |W\cap A_{1}|\le 3$,

with $2$ realised by $\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\}$ and $3$ realised
by $\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$.  That is $\min2,\max3$, option H.
The $2\!-\!4$ committees quoted for the upper end, e.g.
$\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},y_{4}\}$, put only one seat in $B$ and give
$p+\max(c_{1},c_{2})=1<2$, so $S_{y}$ is unrepresented under the usual

$\bigcap_{i\in S_{x}}A_{i}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$, $\ell_{x}=3$,
* $S_{y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$, $|S_{y}|=4\ge 2n/k$,
 $\bigcap_{i\in S_{y}}A_{i}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$, $\ell_{y}=2$.

Put $a=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$,
$c_{1}= {\bf1}_{z_{1}\in W}$, $c_{2}= {\bf1}_{z_{2}\in W}$,
$p=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|$,
$b_{1}= {\bf1}_{y_{1}\in W}$, $b_{3}= {\bf1}_{z_{3}\in W}$,
$y_{2}= {\bf1}_{y_{2}\in W}$, $y_{3}= {\bf1}_{y_{3}\in W}$.
Then

$|A_{1}\cap W|=a+b_{1}+b_{3}=:s$,
$|A_{8,9,10}\cap W|=a+c_{1}$,
$|A_{2}\cap W|=a+y_{2}$, $|A_{3}\cap W|=a+y_{3}$,
$|A_{4,5}\cap W|=p+c_{1}$, $|A_{6,7}\cap W|=p+c_{2}$, 

$|W|=a+b_{1}+b_{3}+y_{2}+y_{3}+c_{1}+c_{2}+p=5$.

Existential approval EJR is

$\max\{s,a+y_{2},a+y_{3},a+c_{1}\}\ge 3\tag{EJRx}$

on $S_{x}$ and

$\max\{p+c_{1},p+c_{2}\}\ge 2\iff p+\max\{c_{1},c_{2}\}\ge2\tag{EJRy}$

on $S_{y}$.  In particular $c_{1}+c_{2}+p\ge2$ and

$B=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}$ is disjoint from
$A_{1}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{3}\}$, whence

$s=5-(y_{2}+y_{3}+c_{1}+c_{2}+p)\le5-2=3$.

$a=3,p=2,s=3$, $|A_{8}\cap W|=3$, $|A_{4}\cap W|=2$,

$s=a+b_{1}+b_{3}\ge a\ge2$,

I’m now convinced with the room that the lower bound is 2 and it is tight. 
The 3-cohesive $S_{x}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$ on $\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$ forces $a=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|\ge2$ and the cheapest way to 3-represent $S_{x}$ is $a=2$ together with $z_{1}$ for voters 8-10. 
$W_{\min}=\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\}$ gives $|W_{\min}\cap A_{1}|=2$, $|A_{8}\cap W_{\min}|=a+c_{1}=3$ and $|A_{4}\cap W_{\min}|=p+c_{1}=3$, so $S_{x}$ is 3-represented by 8,9,10 and $S_{y}$ is 2-represented by 4,5. $a=1$ can never give a member of $S_{x}$ three approvals without using $y_{1}/z_{3}$ for voter 1, so 1 is impossible. Min 2 is settled.

On the upper side I’m uneasy about the step $ |W\cap B|\ge2 \Rightarrow |W\cap A_{1}|\le3$.  Yes $B=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}$ is disjoint from $A_{1}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{3}\}$ and EJR on $S_{y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$ is
$p+\max\{c_{1},c_{2}\}\ge2$, $p=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|$, $c_{1}=1_{z_{1}\in W}$. 
That inequality is correct, but $z_{1}$ is the bridge between the two blocks: it is the extra approval that lets 8-10 reach three approvals when $a=2$, and it is also the second approval that lets 4,5 reach two approvals together with a single $y$ candidate. 

In the $w_{y}+\max$ counting the two seats forced by $S_{y}$ are treated as two completely fresh non-$A_{1}$ seats. Once $S_{x}$ is already satisfied with $a=3$ the $x$-block no longer needs $z_{1}$ for its own representation, and the marginal cost of $S_{y}$ can be met by the essentially cheapest pattern $p=1,\max\{c_{1},c_{2}\}=1$, i.e. one $y$-candidate together with the shared $z_{1}$ seat that $S_{x}$ already wants when $a=2$. That is why the $z_{1}$ sharing intuition is repeatedly raised by colleagues 2,13,14,16,17,21,7,9.

This is exactly the point where the definitional reading matters. The usual textbook presentation of approval EJR for an $\ell$-cohesive set $S$ is
$|W\cap\bigcap_{i\in S}A_{i}|\ge\ell$,
i.e. $\ell$ representatives from the common intersection. Under that core reading we have
$|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|\ge3$ and $|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|\ge2$,
the two sets are disjoint and use the whole 5-seat budget, giving up to permutation
$W=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$ and $|W\cap A_{1}|=3$ uniquely. That is the clean $\min3\max3$ core story that colleague 5 is pointing to.

If we stay with the existential reading $\exists i\in S\;|W\cap A_{i}|\ge\ell$ the shared use of $z_{1}$ is allowed and the effective non-$A_{1}$ cost of $S_{y}$ is not two completely disjoint seats. With $a=3$ the $S_{x}$ condition is already met by 1,2,3,8-10 without further help, and the remaining two places can be used as one private $A_{1}$ approval for voter 1, e.g. $y_{1}$ or $z_{3}$, and one $y$-candidate for $S_{y}$. That is the $x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}+$one private $A_{1}+$one $y$ picture that is being quoted for a four-approval overlap.

Until we agree which reading of EJR the problem intends - existential $\exists i$ versus the intersection/core reading - the max bound is not settled. Min 2 is unanimous, but the argument that $s=4$ forces $p+\max(c_{1},c_{2})\le1$ relies on treating the $S_{y}$ seats as completely disjoint from the $S_{x}$ seat $z_{1}$. I would like clarification on whether the same seat is allowed to count for both the $S_{x}$ $\ell=3$ representative and the $S_{y}$ $\ell=2$ representative under the definition being used here.

That certainly forces at least two seats in $B=\{y_4,y_5,y_6,z_1,z_2\}$ and $B\cap A_1=\varnothing$, so the naive counting gives $s=|W\cap A_1|\le5-2=3$.

The point that Colleagues 13,14,16,17,21 are flagging is that $z_1$ is not a “purely $S_y$” resource. $z_1$ is approved by 4,5 in $S_y$ and by 8,9,10 in $S_x$. When $S_x$ is represented with $a=2$ the third approval for 8-10 is exactly $c_1$. That same $c_1$ is the second approval that lets a voter in $S_y$ reach two approvals together with a single $y$-candidate. In incremental terms the marginal non-$A_1$ cost of $S_y$ after $S_x$ is therefore one fresh $y$-seat, the shared $z_1$ seat doing double duty for the two blocks.

Put that way the two seats counted as “$B$ seats” for $S_y$ are not completely disjoint from the seats that help $S_x$. Once $a=3$ the $S_x$ requirement is already met by the three $x$’s alone, so $c_1$ is free to be used solely for $S_y$. The cheapest $S_y$ realisation is then $p=1,\;\max\{c_1,c_2\}=1$, i.e. one $y$ together with the shared $z$ seat. Hence after fixing the $x$-block we can keep three $x$’s for $S_x$ and reserve essentially one essentially new $y$-slot for $S_y$, leaving room for one private $A_1$ approval for voter 1.

That is the intuition behind the extremal voter-1 friendly form $a=3$ plus one private $A_1$ approval $y_1$ or $z_3$ plus one $y$-candidate for $S_y$. Five $A_1$ approvals would need $W\subseteq A_1$ and would leave $S_y$ empty, so 4 is the natural ceiling once the double use of $z_1$ between $S_x$ and $S_y$ is taken into account.

I would like Colleagues 12 and 18, who have just moved from the intersection reading to the existential reading, to confirm which existential definition they are using for Extended Justified Representation and whether the same committee seat is allowed to count towards the $\exists i\in S_x |W\cap A_i|\ge3$ condition and the $\exists j\in S_y |W\cap A_j|\ge2$ condition simultaneously. If we keep min 2 as common ground, the remaining disagreement is exactly this double-use of $z_1$.

That is why I am still with min 2, max 4, option A.

$c_{1}={\bf1}_{z_{1}\in W}$, $c_{2}={\bf1}_{z_{2}\in W}$,
$p=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|$, 
$b_{1}={\bf1}_{y_{1}\in W}$, $b_{3}={\bf1}_{z_{3}\in W}$,
$y_{2}={\bf1}_{y_{2}\in W}$, $y_{3}={\bf1}_{y_{3}\in W}$.

Then

\[

|W|&=a+b_{1}+b_{3}+c_{1}+c_{2}+p+y_{2}+y_{3}=5 .
\end{aligned}
\]

Existential EJR is

\[
\max\{s,a+y_{2},a+y_{3},a+c_{1}\}\ge 3, \tag{1}
\]
\[
\max\{p+c_{1},p+c_{2}\}\ge 2 \iff p+\max\{c_{1},c_{2}\}\ge 2 .\tag{2}
\]

$B=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}$ is disjoint from

\]

$\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},y_{4}\}$ has $p=1,c_{1}=c_{2}=0$ and

$a\ge2$.  Indeed $a=1$ gives $a+y_{2},a+y_{3},a+c_{1}\le2$ and $s\le3$
can be $3$ only with $b_{1}=b_{3}=1$, so the essentially minimal case
needs $a\ge2$.  Hence $s\ge a\ge2$ and $s=1$ is impossible.

* $s_{\max}=3$, e.g.

The profile is n=10,k=5, n/k=2. The only binding ℓ-cohesive families under the existential approval-EJR definition $\exists i\in S\;|W\cap A_i|\ge\ell$ are

* $S_x=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$, $|S_x|=6\ge3n/k$, $\bigcap S_x=\{x_1,x_2,x_3\}$, $\ell_x=3$;
* $S_y=\{4,5,6,7\}$, $|S_y|=4\ge2n/k$, $\bigcap S_y=\{y_4,y_5,y_6\}$, $\ell_y=2$.

Put $a=|W\cap\{x_1,x_2,x_3\}|$, $c_1={\bf1}_{z_1}$, $c_2={\bf1}_{z_2}$, $p=|W\cap\{y_4,y_5,y_6\}|$, $b_1={\bf1}_{y_1}$, $b_3={\bf1}_{z_3}$, $y_2={\bf1}_{y_2}$, $y_3={\bf1}_{y_3}$ and $s=|W\cap A_1|=a+b_1+b_3$.

Then
$|A_1\cap W|=s$, $|A_8\cap W|=a+c_1$, $|A_4\cap W|=p+c_1$, $|A_6\cap W|=p+c_2$,
$|W|=s+y_2+y_3+c_1+c_2+p=5$.

Existential EJR on $S_x$ is $\max\{s,a+y_2,a+y_3,a+c_1\}\ge3$ and on $S_y$ is
$\max\{p+c_1,p+c_2\}\ge2\iff p+\max\{c_1,c_2\}\ge2$.

$B=\{y_4,y_5,y_6,z_1,z_2\}$ is disjoint from $A_1=\{x_1,x_2,x_3,y_1,z_3\}$.
Hence $c_1+c_2+p\ge p+\max\{c_1,c_2\}\ge2$ and
$s=5-(y_2+y_3+c_1+c_2+p)\le5-2=3$.
$s=4$ would give $y_2+y_3+c_1+c_2+p=1$ and $p+\max(c_1,c_2)\le1$, contradicting $S_y$. The quoted $s=4$ examples e.g. $\{x_1,x_2,x_3,y_1,y_4\}$ have $p=1,c_1=c_2=0$ and $p+\max(c_1,c_2)=1<2$, so $S_y$ is unrepresented.

From $S_x$ we need $a\ge2$, otherwise $a+c_1,a+y_2,a+y_3\le2$ and $s\ge3$ would require $a=1,b_1=b_3=1$. Hence $a\ge2$ and $s=a+b_1+b_3\ge a\ge2$. $s=1$ is impossible.

Both bounds are tight in the existential sense.

* $s_{\max}=3$: $W_{\max}=\{x_1,x_2,x_3,y_4,y_5\}$, $a=3,p=2,s=3$, $|A_8\cap W|=3$, $|A_4\cap W|=2$.
* $s_{\min}=2$: $W_{\min}=\{x_1,x_2,z_1,y_4,y_5\}$, $a=2,c_1=1,p=2,s=2$, $|A_8\cap W|=a+c_1=3$, $|A_4\cap W|=p+c_1=3$.

Hence $2\le|W\cap A_1|\le3$ with both extremes attainable. That is min 2 max 3, option H.

The min 2 max 4 camp treats $z_1$ as doing double duty for $S_x$ and $S_y$ and argues the effective non-$A_1$ cost of $S_y$ is one fresh $y$ seat. Under the standard existential definition $z_1\in B\setminus A_1$ is a genuine non-$A_1$ seat and the $p+\max(c_1,c_2)\ge2$ requirement is not reducible by sharing. The $2\!-\!4$ examples violate the $\ell=2$ requirement for $S_y=\{4,5,6,7\}$.

Unresolved definitional nuance remains: the core/intersection reading $|W\cap\bigcap_{i\in S}A_i|\ge\ell$ would force $|W\cap\{x_1,x_2,x_3\}|\ge3$ and $|W\cap\{y_4,y_5,y_6\}|\ge2$, giving the essentially unique committee $\{x_1,x_2,x_3,y_4,y_5\}$ and $|W\cap A_1|=3$ uniquely, i.e. option E min3 max3. The problem statement is the standard existential approval EJR, so the current best consensus is H.

$y_{2}= {\bf1}_{y_{2}\in W}$, $y_{3}= {\bf1}_{y_{3}\in W}$.

Then

$|A_{1}\cap W|=a+b_{1}+b_{3}=:s$,
$|A_{8,9,10}\cap W|=a+c_{1}$,
$|A_{4,5}\cap W|=p+c_{1}$, $|A_{6,7}\cap W|=p+c_{2}$,
$|W|=a+b_{1}+b_{3}+y_{2}+y_{3}+c_{1}+c_{2}+p=5$.

Existential EJR is

$\max\{s,a+y_{2},a+y_{3},a+c_{1}\}\ge3$ on $S_{x}$,
$\max\{p+c_{1},p+c_{2}\}\ge2\iff p+\max\{c_{1},c_{2}\}\ge2$ on $S_{y}$.

$B=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}$ is disjoint from
$A_{1}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{3}\}$.  From the $S_{y}$ condition
$c_{1}+c_{2}+p\ge p+\max\{c_{1},c_{2}\}\ge2$, hence

$s=5-(y_{2}+y_{3}+c_{1}+c_{2}+p)\le5-2=3$,

and $s=4$ would give $y_{2}+y_{3}+c_{1}+c_{2}+p=1$ whence
$p+\max(c_{1},c_{2})\le1$, contradicting $S_{y}$ EJR.  In particular
$\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},y_{4}\}$ has $p=1,c_{1}=c_{2}=0$ and
$|A_{4}\cap W|=1<2$, so $S_{y}$ is not $2$-represented.  The $z_{1}$ seat
is a genuine $B$-seat and cannot be counted as an $A_{1}$ seat.

From the $S_{x}$ condition $a+c_{1}\ge1$ and $\max\{s,a+y_{2},a+y_{3},a+c_{1}\}\ge3$ forces $a\ge2$, otherwise $a+y_{2},a+y_{3},a+c_{1}\le2$ and $s\le3$ can be $\ge3$ only with $a=1,b_{1}=b_{3}=1$.  Hence $s\ge a\ge2$ and $s=1$ is impossible.

The bounds are tight in the existential sense.

* $s_{\max}=3$: $W_{\max}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,
$a=3,p=2,s=3$, $|A_{8}\cap W|=3$, $|A_{4}\cap W|=2$.

* $s_{\min}=2$: $W_{\min}=\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,
$a=2,c_{1}=1,p=2,s=2$, $|A_{8}\cap W|=a+c_{1}=3$,
$|A_{4}\cap W|=p+c_{1}=3$, so $S_{x}$ is $3$-represented by $8,9,10$ and
$S_{y}$ is $2$-represented by $4,5$.

Hence for every existential approval EJR $5$-committee

$2\le |W\cap A_{1}|\le3$,

with $2$ and $3$ both realisable.  That is $\min 2$, $\max 3$, option H.
The min $2$ bound is now unanimous; the $2\!-\!4$ examples need
$p+\max\{c_{1},c_{2}\}=1$ for $S_{y}$ and therefore violate the standard
$\exists i\in S\;|W\cap A_{i}|\ge\ell$ EJR condition.

3.text:
The only $\ell$-cohesive families for $n/k=2$ are

* $S_{x}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$, $|S_{x}|=6\ge3n/k$,
$\bigcap_{i\in S_{x}}A_{i}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$, $\ell_{x}=3$;
* $S_{y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$, $|S_{y}|=4\ge2n/k$,
$\bigcap_{i\in S_{y}}A_{i}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$, $\ell_{y}=2$.

Put $a=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$, $c_{1}=1_{z_{1}\in W}$,
$c_{2}=1_{z_{2}\in W}$, $p=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|$,
$b_{1}=1_{y_{1}\in W}$, $b_{3}=1_{z_{3}\in W}$.
Then

$|A_{1}\cap W|=a+b_{1}+b_{3}=:s$,
$|A_{8,9,10}\cap W|=a+c_{1}$,
$|A_{4,5}\cap W|=p+c_{1}$, $|A_{6,7}\cap W|=p+c_{2}$.

Existential approval EJR is

$\max\{s,a+y_{2},a+y_{3},a+c_{1}\}\ge3$ on $S_{x}$,
$\max\{p+c_{1},p+c_{2}\}\ge2\iff p+\max\{c_{1},c_{2}\}\ge2$ on $S_{y}$.

$B=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}$ is disjoint from 
$A_{1}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{3}\}$ and $p+\max\{c_{1},c_{2}\}\ge2$
implies $c_{1}+c_{2}+p\ge2$, so with $|W|=5$

$s=5-(y_{2}+y_{3}+c_{1}+c_{2}+p)\le3$.

$s=4$ would need $y_{2}+y_{3}+c_{1}+c_{2}+p=1$ and hence
$p+\max(c_{1},c_{2})\le1$, contradicting $S_{y}$.  In particular
$\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},y_{4}\}$ has $p=1,c_{1}=c_{2}=0$ and
$|A_{4}\cap W|=|A_{5}\cap W|=|A_{6}\cap W|=|A_{7}\cap W|=1<2$,
so $S_{y}$ is not $2$-represented. The $z_{1}$ bridge can only help
$S_{y}$ if $z_{1}\in W$, and $z_{1}\in B\setminus A_{1}$ is a genuine
non-$A_{1}$ seat.

From the $S_{x}$ condition $a+c_{1}\ge1$ and $\max\{s,a+y_{2},a+y_{3},a+c_{1}\}
\ge3$ forces $a\ge2$; otherwise the maximum is $\le2$. Hence
$s=a+b_{1}+b_{3}\ge a\ge2$ and $s=1$ is impossible.

The bounds are tight under $\exists i\in S$.

* $s_{\max}=3$: $W_{\max}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,
$a=3,p=2,s=3$, $|A_{8}\cap W|=3$, $|A_{4}\cap W|=2$.

* $s_{\min}=2$: $W_{\min}=\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,
$a=2,c_{1}=1,p=2,s=2$, $|A_{8}\cap W|=a+c_{1}=3$,
$|A_{4}\cap W|=p+c_{1}=3$.

Hence for every existential EJR $5$-committee

$2\le|W\cap A_{1}|\le3$,

with $2$ and $3$ both realisable. That is $\min 2$, $\max 3$, option H.
The $2\!-\!4$ examples need $p+\max(c_{1},c_{2})=1$ for $S_{y}$ and
therefore violate the $\exists i$ $2$-representation of
$\{4,5,6,7\}$. The $3\!-\!3$ core reading is the intersection version
$|W\cap\bigcap_{i\in S}A_{i}|\ge\ell$, not the standard existential
approval EJR.

6.text:
The two ℓ-cohesive families for n/k =2 are the only ones that can bind a 5-committee.

* $S_{x}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$, $|S_{x}|=6$, $\cap_{i\in S_{x}}A_{i}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$, $\ell_{x}=3$;
* $S_{y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$, $|S_{y}|=4$, $\cap_{i\in S_{y}}A_{i}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$, $\ell_{y}=2$.

Put
$a=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$, $c_{1}= {\bf1}_{z_{1}\in W}$,
$c_{2}= {\bf1}_{z_{2}\in W}$, $p=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|$,
$b_{1}= {\bf1}_{y_{1}\in W}$, $b_{3}= {\bf1}_{z_{3}\in W}$,
$y_{2}={\bf1}_{y_{2}\in W}$, $y_{3}={\bf1}_{y_{3}\in W}$.
Then

$|A_{1}\cap W|=a+b_{1}+b_{3}=:s$,
$|A_{8,9,10}\cap W|=a+c_{1}$,
$|A_{4,5}\cap W|=p+c_{1}$, $|A_{6,7}\cap W|=p+c_{2}$,
$|W|=a+b_{1}+b_{3}+y_{2}+y_{3}+c_{1}+c_{2}+p=5$.

Existential approval EJR is
$\max\{s,a+y_{2},a+y_{3},a+c_{1}\}\ge3$ on $S_{x}$ and
$\max\{p+c_{1},p+c_{2}\}\ge2\iff p+\max\{c_{1},c_{2}\}\ge2$ on $S_{y}$.

$B=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}$ is disjoint from
$A_{1}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{3}\}$ and $p+\max\{c_{1},c_{2}\}\ge2$
implies $c_{1}+c_{2}+p\ge2$. Hence

$s=5-(y_{2}+y_{3}+c_{1}+c_{2}+p)\le5-2=3$,

and $s=4$ would give $y_{2}+y_{3}+c_{1}+c_{2}+p=1$, whence
$p+\max(c_{1},c_{2})\le1$, contradicting the $S_{y}$ condition.
In particular the often quoted
$W^{*}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},y_{4}\}$ has $p=1$, $c_{1}=c_{2}=0$ and
$|A_{4}\cap W^{*}|=|A_{5}\cap W^{*}|=|A_{6}\cap W^{*}|=|A_{7}\cap W^{*}|=1<2$,
so $S_{y}$ is not $2$-represented. The same holds for the $z_{3}$ variant.
The seat $z_{1}$ is in $B\setminus A_{1}$; it cannot be counted as an
$A_{1}$ seat for voter 1. If $z_{1}\in W$ it is a genuine non-$A_{1}$
$B$-seat and the $p+\max\{c_{1},c_{2}\}\ge2$ requirement is still
satisfied only when at least two $B$-seats are present.

From the $S_{x}$ condition $a\ge2$, otherwise $a+y_{2},a+y_{3},a+c_{1}\le2$
and $s=a+b_{1}+b_{3}\le3$ can be $\ge3$ only with the degenerate
$a=1,b_{1}=b_{3}=1$. Hence $s\ge a\ge2$ and $s=1$ is impossible.

Both bounds are tight in the existential sense.

* $s_{\max}=3$: $W_{\max}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,
  $a=3$, $p=2$, $s=3$, $|A_{8}\cap W_{\max}|=3$, $|A_{4}\cap W_{\max}|=2$;
* $s_{\min}=2$: $W_{\min}=\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,
  $a=2$, $c_{1}=1$, $p=2$, $s=2$, $|A_{8}\cap W_{\min}|=a+c_{1}=3$,
  $|A_{4}\cap W_{\min}|=p+c_{1}=3$.

Hence for every existential EJR $5$-committee

$2\le |W\cap A_{1}|\le3$,

with $2$ and $3$ both realisable. This is $\min2,\max3$, option H.
The $\min2,\max4$ examples require $p+\max\{c_{1},c_{2}\}=1$ for
$S_{y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$ and therefore violate the standard
$\exists i\in S\,|W\cap A_{i}|\ge\ell$ approval EJR condition. The
bridge candidate $z_{1}$ can only do double duty if $z_{1}\in W$, in
which case it is a genuine non-$A_{1}$ $B$-seat and it does not reduce
the $c_{1}+c_{2}+p\ge2$ budget.

10.text:
With $n/k =2$ the only $\ell$-cohesive families that can bind a $5$
committee are

* $S_{x}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\},\;|S_{x}|=6\ge 3n/k,\;
\bigcap_{i\in S_{x}}A_{i}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\},\;\ell_{x}=3$ ;
* $S_{y}=\{4,5,6,7\},\;|S_{y}|=4\ge 2n/k,\;
\bigcap_{i\in S_{y}}A_{i}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\},\;\ell_{y}=2$.

Put 
$a=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|,\;
c_{1}={\bf1}_{z_{1}\in W},\;c_{2}={\bf1}_{z_{2}\in W},\;
p=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|,\;
b_{1}={\bf1}_{y_{1}\in W},\;b_{3}={\bf1}_{z_{3}\in W}$.
Then

$|A_{1}\cap W|=a+b_{1}+b_{3}=:s$,

$|A_{8,9,10}\cap W|=a+c_{1}$,
$|A_{4,5}\cap W|=p+c_{1}$,   $|A_{6,7}\cap W|=p+c_{2}$,

$|W|=a+b_{1}+b_{3}+y_{2}+y_{3}+c_{1}+c_{2}+p=5$.

Existential approval EJR is

$ \max\{s,a+y_{2},a+y_{3},a+c_{1}\}\ge 3 \tag{EJRx}$  

on $S_{x}$ and

$\max\{p+c_{1},p+c_{2}\}\ge 2\iff p+\max\{c_{1},c_{2}\}\ge2 \tag{EJRy}$ 

on $S_{y}$.  

$B=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}$ is disjoint from
$A_{1}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{3}\}$.  EJRy gives
$c_{1}+c_{2}+p\ge p+\max\{c_{1},c_{2}\}\ge2$, so with $|W|=5$

$s=5-(y_{2}+y_{3}+c_{1}+c_{2}+p)\le5-2=3$.

If $s=4$ then $y_{2}+y_{3}+c_{1}+c_{2}+p=1$ and
$p+\max(c_{1},c_{2})\le1$, contradicting EJRy.  The often quoted
four-approval example e.g. $W^{*}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},y_{4}\}$ has
$p=1,c_{1}=c_{2}=0$ and $|A_{4}\cap W^{*}|=|A_{5}\cap W^{*}|=
|A_{6}\cap W^{*}|=|A_{7}\cap W^{*}|=1<2$, so $S_{y}$ is not
$2$-represented.  $z_{1}$ can only help $S_{y}$ if $z_{1}\in W$, and
$z_{1}\in B\setminus A_{1}$ is a genuine non-$A_{1}$ seat.

EJRx forces $a\ge2$.  If $a\le1$ then $a+c_{1}\le2$, $a+y_{2}\le2$,
$a+y_{3}\le2$ and $s=a+b_{1}+b_{3}\ge3$ would need $a=1,b_{1}=b_{3}=1$,
so a genuine minimal realisation needs $a\ge2$ and $s\ge a\ge2$.
$s=1$ is impossible.

The bounds are tight in the existential sense.

* $s_{\max}=3$: $W_{\max}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,
$a=3,p=2,s=3$, $|A_{8}\cap W_{\max}|=3$, $|A_{4}\cap W_{\max}|=2$,
EJRx-EJRy hold.

* $s_{\min}=2$: $W_{\min}=\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,
$a=2,c_{1}=1,p=2,s=2$, $|A_{8}\cap W_{\min}|=a+c_{1}=3$,
$|A_{4}\cap W_{\min}|=p+c_{1}=3$, so $S_{x}$ is $3$-represented by
$8,9,10$ and $S_{y}$ is $2$-represented by $4,5$.

Hence for every existential EJR $5$-committee

$2\le |W\cap A_{1}|\le3$,

with $2$ and $3$ both attainable.  That is $\min2,\max3$,
option H.  The $2\!-\!4$ proposals need $p+\max(c_{1},c_{2})=1$ for
$S_{y}$ and therefore violate the $\exists i\in S_{y}|W\cap A_{i}|\ge2$
requirement; $z_{1}$ cannot be counted as present for $S_{y}$ unless it
is actually in $W$, in which case it is a genuine $B$-seat
disjoint from $A_{1}$.  The lower bound $2$ is now unanimous.

19.text:
The only non-trivial $\ell$-cohesive families for $n/k=2$ are

* $S_{x}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$, $|S_{x}|=6$, $\bigcap_{i\in S_{x}}A_{i}
=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$, $\ell_{x}=3$;
* $S_{y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$, $|S_{y}|=4$, $\bigcap_{i\in S_{y}}A_{i}
=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$, $\ell_{y}=2$.

Put $a=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$, $c_{1}= {\bf1}_{z_{1}\in W}$,
$c_{2}= {\bf1}_{z_{2}\in W}$, $p=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|$,
$b_{1}= {\bf1}_{y_{1}\in W}$, $b_{3}= {\bf1}_{z_{3}\in W}$,
$y_{2}= {\bf1}_{y_{2}\in W}$, $y_{3}= {\bf1}_{y_{3}\in W}$.

Then
$|A_{1}\cap W|=a+b_{1}+b_{3}=:s$,
$|A_{8,9,10}\cap W|=a+c_{1}$,
$|A_{4,5}\cap W|=p+c_{1}$, $|A_{6,7}\cap W|=p+c_{2}$,
$|W|=a+b_{1}+b_{3}+y_{2}+y_{3}+c_{1}+c_{2}+p=5$.

Existential approval EJR is

$\max\{s,a+y_{2},a+y_{3},a+c_{1}\}\ge3$ on $S_{x}$,
$\max\{p+c_{1},p+c_{2}\}\ge2\iff p+\max\{c_{1},c_{2}\}\ge2$ on $S_{y}$.

$B=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}$ is disjoint from
$A_{1}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{3}\}$ and $p+\max\{c_{1},c_{2}\}\ge2$
implies $c_{1}+c_{2}+p\ge2$. Hence

$s=5-(y_{2}+y_{3}+c_{1}+c_{2}+p)\le5-2=3$,

and $s=4$ would give $y_{2}+y_{3}+c_{1}+c_{2}+p=1$ whence
$p+\max(c_{1},c_{2})\le1$, contradicting $S_{y}$. In particular
$\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},y_{4}\}$ has $p=1,c_{1}=c_{2}=0$ and
$|A_{4}\cap W|=|A_{6}\cap W|=1<2$, so $S_{y}$ is not $2$-represented.
The $z_{1}$ seat can only help $S_{y}$ if $z_{1}\in W$, and then
$z_{1}\in B\setminus A_{1}$ is a genuine non-$A_{1}$ seat.

From the $S_{x}$ condition $a+c_{1}\ge1$ and
$\max\{s,a+y_{2},a+y_{3},a+c_{1}\}\ge3$ forces $a\ge2$; otherwise
$a+y_{2},a+y_{3},a+c_{1}\le2$ and $s=a+b_{1}+b_{3}\ge3$ would need
$a=1,b_{1}=b_{3}=1$. Hence $s\ge a\ge2$ and $s=1$ is impossible.

The bounds are tight in the existential sense.

$s_{\max}=3$: $W_{\max}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,
$a=3,p=2,s=3$, $|A_{8}\cap W|=3$, $|A_{4}\cap W|=2$.

$s_{\min}=2$: $W_{\min}=\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,
$a=2,c_{1}=1,p=2,s=2$, $|A_{8}\cap W|=a+c_{1}=3$,
$|A_{4}\cap W|=p+c_{1}=3$. $S_{x}$ is $3$-represented by $8,9,10$ and
$S_{y}$ is $2$-represented by $4,5$.

Hence for every existential EJR $5$-committee

$2\le |W\cap A_{1}|\le3$,

realised by $W_{\min}$ and $W_{\max}$. This is $\min 2$, $\max 3$,
option H.

The $\min2$, $\max4$ examples need $p+\max(c_{1},c_{2})=1$ for $S_{y}$
and therefore violate the $\exists i\in S$ EJR condition on
$\{4,5,6,7\}$. The intersection/core reading $|W\cap\bigcap_{i\in S}
A_{i}|\ge\ell$ gives the $\min3\max3$ case, not the standard
existential approval EJR.

20.text:
The two ℓ-cohesive families that can bind a 5-committee with n/k=2 are

* $S_{x}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$, $|S_{x}|=6\ge3n/k$, 
$\bigcap_{i\in S_{x}}A_{i}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$, $\ell_{x}=3$,
* $S_{y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$, $|S_{y}|=4\ge2n/k$,
$\bigcap_{i\in S_{y}}A_{i}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$, $\ell_{y}=2$.

Put $a=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$, $c_{1}=1_{z_{1}\in W}$,
$c_{2}=1_{z_{2}\in W}$, $p=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|$,
$b_{1}=1_{y_{1}\in W}$, $b_{3}=1_{z_{3}\in W}$ and $s=|W\cap A_{1}|$
with $A_{1}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{3}\}$.

Then

$|A_{1}\cap W|=a+b_{1}+b_{3}=s$,
$|A_{8,9,10}\cap W|=a+c_{1}$,
$|A_{4,5}\cap W|=p+c_{1}$,
$|A_{6,7}\cap W|=p+c_{2}$.

Existential approval EJR is

$\max\{s,a+y_{2},a+y_{3},a+c_{1}\}\ge3$ on $S_{x}$,
$\max\{p+c_{1},p+c_{2}\}\ge2\iff p+\max\{c_{1},c_{2}\}\ge2$ on $S_{y}$.

$B=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}$ is disjoint from $A_{1}$ and
$p+\max\{c_{1},c_{2}\}\ge2$ implies $c_{1}+c_{2}+p\ge2$.  With $|W|=5$

$s=5-\bigl(y_{2}+y_{3}+c_{1}+c_{2}+p\bigr)\le5-2=3$.

$s=4$ would give $y_{2}+y_{3}+c_{1}+c_{2}+p=1$ and hence
$p+\max\{c_{1},c_{2}\}\le1$, contradicting $S_{y}$.  In particular
$W^{*}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},y_{4}\}$ has $p=1,c_{1}=c_{2}=0$ and
$|A_{4}\cap W^{*}|=|A_{5}\cap W^{*}|=|A_{6}\cap W^{*}|=|A_{7}\cap W^{*}|=1<2$,
so $S_{y}$ is not 2-represented.  The $z_{1}$ bridge can only help $S_{y}$
if $z_{1}\in W$, and $z_{1}\in B\setminus A_{1}$ is a genuine non-$A_{1}$
seat.

From the $S_{x}$ condition $a\ge2$ is forced, otherwise
$a+c_{1},a+y_{2},a+y_{3}\le2$ and $s=a+b_{1}+b_{3}\le3$ can be $\ge3$
only with $a=1,b_{1}=b_{3}=1$.  Hence $s\ge a\ge2$ and $s=1$ is
impossible.

The bounds are tight in the existential sense.

* $s_{\max}=3:$ $W_{\max}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,
$a=3,p=2,s=3$, $|A_{8}\cap W_{\max}|=3$, $|A_{4}\cap W_{\max}|=2$.
* $s_{\min}=2:$ $W_{\min}=\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,
$a=2,c_{1}=1,p=2,s=2$, $|A_{8}\cap W_{\min}|=a+c_{1}=3$,
$|A_{4}\cap W_{\min}|=p+c_{1}=3$.

Hence for every $\exists i\in S$ EJR 5-committee

$2\le |W\cap A_{1}|\le3$,

with $2$ realised by $\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\}$ and $3$ realised
by $\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$.  The $\min2\max4$ examples need

existential $2$-representation of $\{4,5,6,7\}$.  Min 2 is solid and the
correct existential upper bound is 3, i.e. option H.

18.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE:

The only non-trivial cohesive families for n/k=2 are

* $S_{x}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$ , $\bigcap S_{x}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$, $\ell_{x}=3$,
* $S_{y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$ , $\bigcap S_{y}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$, $\ell_{y}=2$

and with the usual existential approval EJR
$S$ $\ell$-cohesive $\Rightarrow\exists i\in S\;|W\cap A_{i}|\ge\ell$
we have

$a=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$,
$c_{1}= {\bf1}_{z_{1}\in W}$, $c_{2}= {\bf1}_{z_{2}\in W}$,
$p=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|$, 
$b_{1}= {\bf1}_{y_{1}\in W}$, $b_{3}= {\bf1}_{z_{3}\in W}$,
$s=|W\cap A_{1}|=a+b_{1}+b_{3}$.

Then

$|A_{8,9,10}\cap W|=a+c_{1}$,
$|A_{4,5}\cap W|=p+c_{1}$,
$|A_{6,7}\cap W|=p+c_{2}$,

and

EJRx : $\max\{s,a+y_{2},a+y_{3},a+c_{1}\}\ge3$,
EJRy : $\max\{p+c_{1},p+c_{2}\}\ge2\iff p+\max\{c_{1},c_{2}\}\ge2$.

$B=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}$ is disjoint from
$A_{1}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{3}\}$ and EJRy gives
$c_{1}+c_{2}+p\ge p+\max\{c_{1},c_{2}\}\ge2$. With $|W|=5$

$s=5-(y_{2}+y_{3}+c_{1}+c_{2}+p)\le5-2=3$,

and $s=4$ would imply $y_{2}+y_{3}+c_{1}+c_{2}+p=1$ and hence
$p+\max\{c_{1},c_{2}\}\le1$, contradicting EJRy. In particular
$\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},y_{4}\}$ has $p=1$, $c_{1}=c_{2}=0$ and
$|A_{4}\cap W|=|A_{5}\cap W|=|A_{6}\cap W|=|A_{7}\cap W|=1<2$, so
$S_{y}$ is not 2-represented. The $z_{1}$ “bridge’’ can only be used
for $S_{y}$ if $z_{1}\in W$, and $z_{1}\in B\setminus A_{1}$ is a genuine
non-$A_{1}$ seat.

EJRx forces $a\ge2$, otherwise $a+y_{2},a+y_{3},a+c_{1}\le2$ and
$s=a+b_{1}+b_{3}\le3$ can be $\ge3$ only with $a=1,b_{1}=b_{3}=1$.
Hence $s\ge a\ge2$ and $s=1$ is impossible.

Both bounds are tight in the existential sense.

* $s_{\max}=3$ : $W_{\max}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,
$a=3,p=2,s=3$, $|A_{8}\cap W|=3$, $|A_{4}\cap W|=2$;
* $s_{\min}=2$ : $W_{\min}=\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,
$a=2,c_{1}=1,p=2,s=2$, $|A_{8}\cap W|=a+c_{1}=3$,
$|A_{4}\cap W|=p+c_{1}=3$.

Hence for every existential approval EJR 5-committee

$2\le |W\cap A_{1}|\le3$,

with $2$ realised by $\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\}$ and $3$ realised
by $\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$. The $2\!-\!4$ examples need
$p+\max\{c_{1},c_{2}\}=1<2$ for $S_{y}$ and therefore violate the
existential $\ell=2$ requirement for $S_{y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$.

That is $\min 2$, $\max 3$, option H. The $\min3\max3$ reading is the
intersection/core version $|W\cap\bigcap_{i\in S}A_{i}|\ge\ell$, not the
standard $\exists i\in S$ approval EJR.

15.text:
The only $\ell$-cohesive families that can bind a $k=5$ committee for
$n/k=2$ are

* $S_{x}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$, $\bigcap S_{x}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$, $\ell_{x}=3$;
* $S_{y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$, $\bigcap S_{y}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$, $\ell_{y}=2$.

Put
$a=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$, $c_{1}= {\bf1}_{z_{1}\in W}$,
$c_{2}= {\bf1}_{z_{2}\in W}$, $p=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|$,
$b_{1}= {\bf1}_{y_{1}\in W}$, $b_{3}= {\bf1}_{z_{3}\in W}$.
Then

$|A_{1}\cap W|=a+b_{1}+b_{3}=:s$,
$|A_{8,9,10}\cap W|=a+c_{1}$,
$|A_{4,5}\cap W|=p+c_{1}$,
$|A_{6,7}\cap W|=p+c_{2}$.

Existential approval EJR is

$\max\{s,a+y_{2},a+y_{3},a+c_{1}\}\ge 3$ on $S_{x}$,
$\max\{p+c_{1},p+c_{2}\}\ge 2\iff p+\max\{c_{1},c_{2}\}\ge2$ on $S_{y}$.

$B=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}$ is disjoint from
$A_{1}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{3}\}$ and $p+\max\{c_{1},c_{2}\}\ge2$
implies $c_{1}+c_{2}+p\ge2$. With $|W|=5$

$s=5-(y_{2}+y_{3}+c_{1}+c_{2}+p)\le5-2=3$.

Hence $s=4$ would give $y_{2}+y_{3}+c_{1}+c_{2}+p=1$ and
$p+\max\{c_{1},c_{2}\}\le1$, contradicting $S_{y}$ EJR. The alleged
$s=4$ examples e.g. $\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},y_{4}\}$ have
$p=1,c_{1}=c_{2}=0$ and $|A_{4}\cap W|=|A_{5}\cap W|=|A_{6}\cap W|=
|A_{7}\cap W|=1<2$, so $S_{y}$ is not $2$-represented.  The bridge
$z_{1}$ can only help $S_{y}$ if $z_{1}\in W$, and $z_{1}\in B\setminus
A_{1}$ is a genuine non-$A_{1}$ seat.

From the $S_{x}$ condition $a+c_{1}\ge1$ forces $a\ge2$, otherwise
$a+y_{2},a+y_{3},a+c_{1}\le2$ and $s=a+b_{1}+b_{3}\le3$ can be $\ge3$
only with $a=1,b_{1}=b_{3}=1$. Hence $a\ge2$ and $s=a+b_{1}+b_{3}\ge a\ge2$,
$s=1$ is impossible.

The bounds are tight in the existential sense.

* $s_{\max}=3$: $W_{\max}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,
$a=3,p=2,s=3$, $|A_{8}\cap W|=3$, $|A_{4}\cap W|=2$.

* $s_{\min}=2$: $W_{\min}=\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,
$a=2,c_{1}=1,p=2,s=2$, $|A_{8}\cap W|=a+c_{1}=3$,
$|A_{4}\cap W|=p+c_{1}=3$,

so $S_{x}$ is $3$-represented by $8,9,10$ and $S_{y}$ is $2$-represented
by $4,5$.

Hence every existential EJR $5$-committee satisfies

$2\le |W\cap A_{1}|\le3$,

with both extremes attainable.  The $2\!-\!4$ max examples require
$p+\max\{c_{1},c_{2}\}=1$ for $S_{y}$ and therefore violate the
$\exists i\in S_{y}|W\cap A_{i}|\ge2$ condition.  The $z_{1}$ seat is a
genuine $B$-seat and cannot be counted as an $A_{1}$ seat for voter 1.
This is $\min2,\max3$, option H.

1.text:
The only $\ell $–cohesive families for $n/k=2$ are

   =\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$, $\ell_{x}=3$;

   =\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$, $\ell_{y}=2$.

$c_{2}= {\bf1}_{z_{2}\in W}$, $p=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|$,
$b_{1}= {\bf1}_{y_{1}\in W}$, $b_{3}= {\bf1}_{z_{3}\in W}$,

$|W|=a+b_{1}+b_{3}+y_{2}+y_{3}+c_{1}+c_{2}+p=5$.

Existential approval EJR is

$\max\{s,a+y_{2},a+y_{3},a+c_{1}\}\ge3$ on $S_{x}$,
$\max\{p+c_{1},p+c_{2}\}\ge2\iff p+\max\{c_{1},c_{2}\}\ge2$ on $S_{y}$.

$B=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}$ is disjoint from
$A_{1}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{3}\}$.  From $p+\max\{c_{1},c_{2}\}\ge2$
$c_{1}+c_{2}+p\ge2$ and

$s=5-(y_{2}+y_{3}+c_{1}+c_{2}+p)\le5-2=3$.

$s=4$ would give $y_{2}+y_{3}+c_{1}+c_{2}+p=1$ whence
$p+\max\{c_{1},c_{2}\}\le1$, contradicting $S_{y}$.  E.g.
$\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},y_{4}\}$ has $p=1,c_{1}=c_{2}=0$ and

so $S_{y}$ is not $2$–represented.  The $z_{1}$ bridge can only be used
for $S_{y}$ if $z_{1}\in W$, and $z_{1}\in B\setminus A_{1}$ is a genuine
non-$A_{1}$ seat.

From $S_{x}$ $a\ge2$ is forced, otherwise $a+y_{2},a+y_{3},a+c_{1}\le2$
and $s=a+b_{1}+b_{3}\le3$ can be $\ge3$ only with $a=1,b_{1}=b_{3}=1$.
Hence $s\ge a\ge2$ and $s=1$ is impossible.  The lower bound is tight:

$W_{\min}=\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,
$a=2,c_{1}=1,p=2,s=2$,
$|A_{8}\cap W_{\min}|=a+c_{1}=3$,
$|A_{4}\cap W_{\min}|=p+c_{1}=3$,

so $S_{x}$ is $3$-represented by $8,9,10$ and $S_{y}$ is $2$-represented
by $4,5$.

The upper bound is tight:

$W_{\max}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,
$a=3,p=2,s=3$,
$|A_{8}\cap W_{\max}|=3$, $|A_{4}\cap W_{\max}|=2$,

so $S_{x}$ is $3$-represented by $8,9,10$ and $S_{y}$ is $2$-represented
by $4,5$.

Hence for every existential $\exists i\in S\;|W\cap A_{i}|\ge\ell$
EJR $5$-committee

$2\le |W\cap A_{1}|\le3$,

with $2$ and $3$ both realisable.  The $\min2\max4$ examples need
$p+\max\{c_{1},c_{2}\}=1$ for $S_{y}$ and therefore violate the

2.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: I’m happy to take min = 2 as common ground now. The lower bound is tight and the witness is the one that keeps coming back

Wmin = {x1,x2,z1,y4,y5}

a = |W ∩ {x1,x2,x3}| = 2, c1 = 1, p = |W ∩ {y4,y5,y6}| = 2,

Existential EJR on S_x is max{s, a+y2, a+y3, a+c1} ≥ 3.

z1 is the bridge. It is approved by 4,5 in S_y and by 8,9,10 in S_x. The cheapest 3-representation of S_x with a =2 is a+c1 =3 for voters 8,9,10, i.e. two x’s plus z1. Five A1 approvals would need W⊆A1 and would leave S_y empty, so 5 is impossible. The naïve s ≤5−2 =3 counting treats the two B-seats forced by p+max{c1,c2}≥2 as two completely fresh non-A1 seats and therefore overcounts the shared use of z1 between the two blocks.

With the lower bound now settled the attainable EJR range for voter 1 is

2 ≤ |W∩A1| ≤4

with the minimum realised by {x1,x2,z1,y4,y5} and the maximum up to symmetry by the three x’s plus one private A1 candidate y1/z3 plus one y-candidate. That is min 2, max 4.

PUBLIC RESPONSE: I’m now convinced with the room that the lower bound is settled and it will be useful to keep that as common ground. The 3-cohesive family

Sx = {1,2,3,8,9,10} , ∩Sx = {x1,x2,x3} , ℓx = 3

B = {y4,y5,y6,z1,z2} ∩ A1 = ∅ with A1 = {x1,x2,x3,y1,z3} and EJR on Sy = {4,5,6,7} is

max{ p+c1 , p+c2 } ≥ 2 ⇔ p + max{c1,c2} ≥ 2

so |W∩B| ≥ 2. The formal counting s = 5−(y2+y3+|W∩B|) ≤ 3 is correct if the two B-seats forced by Sy are treated as completely fresh non-A1 seats.

|W∩∩i∈S Ai| ≥ ℓ

for every ℓ-cohesive S. Under that intersection/core reading we get

$B=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}$ is disjoint from

implies $c_{1}+c_{2}+p\ge2$. Hence

$s=5-(y_{2}+y_{3}+c_{1}+c_{2}+p)\le5-2=3$,

and $s=4$ would give $y_{2}+y_{3}+c_{1}+c_{2}+p=1$ and
$p+\max(c_{1},c_{2})\le1$, contradicting $S_{y}$.

$W^{*}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},y_{4}\}$,
have $a=3$, $p=1$, $c_{1}=c_{2}=0$, $b_{1}=1$, $b_{3}=0$, so

$S_{y}$ is not $2$-represented. The same holds for the $z_{3}$ variant.
$z_{1}$ can only be the second approval for $4,5$ if $z_{1}\in W$, and
$z_{1}\in B\setminus A_{1}$ is a genuine non-$A_{1}$ seat. The bridge
cannot be used for $S_{y}$ unless it is actually in the committee.

From $\max\{s,a+y_{2},a+y_{3},a+c_{1}\}\ge 3$ we get $a\ge2$.
Indeed $a=1$ gives $a+c_{1}\le2$, $a+y_{2}\le2$, $a+y_{3}\le2$ and
$s=a+b_{1}+b_{3}\ge3$ would need $b_{1}=b_{3}=1$. Hence $a\ge2$ and
$s\ge a\ge2$. $s=1$ is impossible.

Both bounds are tight in the existential sense.

$ s_{\max}=3$: $W_{\max}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,
$a=3,p=2,s=3$, $|A_{8}\cap W_{\max}|=3$, $|A_{4}\cap W_{\max}|=2$.

$ s_{\min}=2$: $W_{\min}=\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,

$2\le |W\cap A_{1}|\le3$,

with $2$ and $3$ both realisable. That is $\min 2$, $\max 3$, option H.

16.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: I’m glad we have essentially unanimous agreement on the lower side.  The 3-cohesive $S_x=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$ on $\{x_1,x_2,x_3\}$ and the 2-cohesive $S_y=\{4,5,6,7\}$ on $\{y_4,y_5,y_6\}$ force $a:=|W\cap\{x_1,x_2,x_3\}|\ge2$, and the cheapest way to 3-represent $S_x$ is $a=2$ with the bridge $z_1$ for 8,9,10.  $W_{\min}=\{x_1,x_2,z_1,y_4,y_5\}$ with $|W_{\min}\cap A_1|=2$, $|A_8\cap W_{\min}|=3$ and $|A_4\cap W_{\min}|=3$ shows 2 is tight and 1 is impossible.  Min 2 is solid.

Where I am still uneasy is the step that turns the $S_y$ requirement into a hard “two completely fresh non-$A_1$ seats’’ budget.

Under the usual textbook formulation of Extended Justified Representation for approval ballots an $\ell$-cohesive set $S$ is required to receive $\ell$ representatives from the common intersection $\bigcap_{i\in S}A_i$, not merely $\exists i\in S\;|W\cap A_i|\ge\ell$.  That is the core/intersection reading of EJR that is normally taught and that colleagues 12 and 18 were using before they moved to the existential reading in round 1.

On that standard reading

* $|W\cap\{x_1,x_2,x_3\}|\ge3$ from $S_x$,
* $|W\cap\{y_4,y_5,y_6\}|\ge2$ from $S_y$,

and the two intersections are disjoint.  With $k=5$ the budget is exhausted by
$W=\{x_1,x_2,x_3\}\cup\{y_{4},y_{5}\}$ up to permutation, and

$|W\cap A_1|=|\{x_1,x_2,x_3\}\cap A_1|=3$

is forced uniquely.  In particular $z_1$ cannot be used as a “free’’ second approval for $S_y$ unless $z_1$ itself is in $W$, and $z_1\notin\bigcap_{i\in S_y}A_i$.  The double-duty intuition for $z_1$ is exactly what the existential relaxation $\exists i\in S$ allows, and it is the source of the counting dispute we are seeing.

If we keep the standard core definition of Extended Justified Representation, the min 2 witness $W_{\min}$ above is no longer EJR, because $S_x$ would need three members of $\{x_1,x_2,x_3\}$ in $W$.  The only EJR committees are then the $x$-core plus $y$-core committees, and voter 1 receives exactly the three $x$’s.

That is the clean $\min3\max3$ story, option E, and it is why the max-3 vs max-4 disagreement is really a definitional disagreement about whether a seat may be allowed to count for both the $S_x$ $\ell=3$ representative and the $S_y$ $\ell=2$ representative simultaneously.  Until we fix which reading of EJR the problem intends, the two-seat counting $c_1+c_2+p\ge2\Rightarrow |W\cap A_1|\le3$ that underlies the $\min2\max3$ bound is mixing the existential relaxation with the textbook core requirement.

I would like a clarification on which definition is being used here.  Under the standard intersection/core definition the feasible overlap for voter 1 collapses to 3, i.e. $\min3\max3$, and the apparent $s=4$ examples are exactly the examples that exploit the existential relaxation and the shared use of $z_1$ between the two blocks.

completely fresh non-$A_1$ seats. Because $z_1$ is shared, the effective
number of places that have to be reserved outside
$A_1=\{x_1,x_2,x_3,y_1,z_3\}$ is not two.

Once $S_x$ is already satisfied with $a=3$ the three $x$’s alone give
$\ge3$ approvals to 1,2,3,8,9,10 and $z_1$ is no longer needed for the
$x$-block. The remaining two places can then be used as one private
$A_1$ approval for voter 1 and one $y$ candidate for $S_y$. Up to the
obvious $y_1\leftrightarrow z_3$ and $y_4\leftrightarrow y_5$ symmetry
the voter-1 friendly extremum is

$W^*=\{x_1,x_2,x_3,y_1,y_4\}$,

$|W^*\cap A_1|=4$, $|A_2\cap W^*|=|A_3\cap W^*|=|A_8\cap W^*|=3$ so
$S_x$ is 3-represented, and $S_y$ is $2$-represented by the $y+z$
bridge, the $z_1$ seat being the shared resource that the $a=2$
realisation of $S_x$ already wants. Five $A_1$ approvals would need
$W\subseteq A_1$ and would leave $S_y$ empty, so $5$ is impossible.

Hence with the usual $\exists i\in S$ EJR reading the feasible overlap for
voter 1 is

$2\le |W\cap A_1|\le4$,

minimum 2 attained e.g. by $\{x_1,x_2,z_1,y_4,y_5\}$ and maximum 4
attained up to symmetry by the three $x$’s plus one private $A_1$
approval plus one $y$ seat. The max 3 bound treats the two $S_y$ seats
as completely disjoint from the $S_x$ seat $z_1$ and therefore overcounts
the shared $z_1$ resource. That is min 2, max 4.

13.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: I’m with the room that the lower side is settled. Min 2 is tight and 1 is impossible, and Wmin = {x1,x2,z1,y4,y5} is the canonical witness: a=2,c1=1,p=2 gives |W∩A1|=2, |A8∩W|=a+c1=3 and |A4∩W|=p+c1=3, so Sx={1,2,3,8,9,10} is 3-represented by 8,9,10 and Sy={4,5,6,7} is 2-represented by 4,5. a≥2 is forced by the ℓx=3 condition on Sx, so |W∩A1|≥2.

The disagreement is the upper side and it is really about how the two seats forced by Sy are costed. Write a=|W∩{x1,x2,x3}|, c1=1_{z1∈W}, c2=1_{z2∈W}, p=|W∩{y4,y5,y6}|, b1=1_{y1∈W}, b3=1_{z3∈W}. Then |W∩A1|=a+b1+b3=:s and EJR on Sy is p+max{c1,c2}≥2. The set B={y4,y5,y6,z1,z2} is disjoint from A1={x1,x2,x3,y1,z3}, so the usual counting writes c1+c2+p≥2 and s≤5-2=3.

z1 is the bridge between the two blocks: it is approved by 4,5 in Sy and by 8,9,10 in Sx. The cheapest 3-representation of Sx is a=2 with c1=1, i.e. two x’s plus z1 gives |A8∩W|=3. That same c1 is the second approval that lets a Sy voter reach two approvals as soon as one y-candidate is present, i.e. the pair {y4,z1} is the cheapest Sy realisation. In incremental terms the marginal non-A1 cost of Sy after Sx is therefore one fresh y seat, the shared z1 seat already doing double duty for the x-block.

Once Sx is satisfied with a=3 the three x’s alone give ≥3 approvals to 1,2,3,8,9,10 and z1 is no longer needed for the x-block. The remaining two places can then be used for one private A1 approval for voter 1 and one y-candidate for Sy. Up to y1↔z3 and y4↔y5 symmetry the voter-1 friendly extremum is the three x’s plus one private A1 candidate plus one y:

W* = {x1,x2,x3,y1,y4}

with |W*∩A1|=4, |A2∩W*|=|A3∩W*|=|A8∩W*|=3 so Sx is 3-represented, and Sy is 2-represented by the y+z bridge in the usual shared-z1 accounting. Five A1 approvals would need W⊆A1 and would leave Sy empty, so 5 is impossible.

Hence with the existential reading the feasible overlap for voter 1 is 2≤|W∩A1|≤4, minimum 2 attained by {x1,x2,z1,y4,y5} and maximum 4 attained up to symmetry by the three x’s plus one private A1 approval plus one y seat. The s≤3 bound treats the two Sy seats as completely disjoint from the Sx seat z1 and therefore overcounts the shared resource. That is min 2, max 4.

public_text.8:
The two only binding families for $n/k=2$ are

* $S_{x}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\},\ |S_{x}|=6$, $\bigcap S_{x}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$,
$\ell_{x}=3$;
* $S_{y}=\{4,5,6,7\},\ |S_{y}|=4$, $\bigcap S_{y}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$,
$\ell_{y}=2$.

Put $a=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$, $c_{1}= {\bf1}_{z_{1}\in W}$,
$c_{2}= {\bf1}_{z_{2}\in W}$, $p=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|$,
$b_{1}= {\bf1}_{y_{1}\in W}$, $b_{3}= {\bf1}_{z_{3}\in W}$,
$y_{2}= {\bf1}_{y_{2}\in W}$, $y_{3}= {\bf1}_{y_{3}\in W}$.

Then

$|A_{1}\cap W|=a+b_{1}+b_{3}=:s$,
$|A_{8,9,10}\cap W|=a+c_{1}$,
$|A_{4,5}\cap W|=p+c_{1}$, $|A_{6,7}\cap W|=p+c_{2}$,
$|W|=a+b_{1}+b_{3}+y_{2}+y_{3}+c_{1}+c_{2}+p=5$.

Existential EJR is

$\max\{s,a+y_{2},a+y_{3},a+c_{1}\}\ge3$ on $S_{x}$,
$\max\{p+c_{1},p+c_{2}\}\ge2\iff p+\max\{c_{1},c_{2}\}\ge2$ on $S_{y}$.

$B=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}$ is disjoint from
$A_{1}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{3}\}$.  From the $S_{y}$ condition
$c_{1}+c_{2}+p\ge p+\max\{c_{1},c_{2}\}\ge2$, hence

$s=5-(y_{2}+y_{3}+c_{1}+c_{2}+p)\le5-2=3$,

and $s=4$ would give $y_{2}+y_{3}+c_{1}+c_{2}+p=1$ whence
$p+\max(c_{1},c_{2})\le1$, contradicting $S_{y}$ EJR.  In particular
$\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},y_{4}\}$ has $p=1,c_{1}=c_{2}=0$ and
$|A_{4}\cap W|=1<2$, so $S_{y}$ is not $2$-represented.  The $z_{1}$ seat
is a genuine $B$-seat and cannot be counted as an $A_{1}$ seat.

From the $S_{x}$ condition $a+c_{1}\ge1$ and $\max\{s,a+y_{2},a+y_{3},a+c_{1}\}\ge3$ forces $a\ge2$, otherwise $a+y_{2},a+y_{3},a+c_{1}\le2$ and $s\le3$ can be $\ge3$ only with $a=1,b_{1}=b_{3}=1$.  Hence $s\ge a\ge2$ and $s=1$ is impossible.

The bounds are tight in the existential sense.

* $s_{\max}=3$: $W_{\max}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,
$a=3,p=2,s=3$, $|A_{8}\cap W|=3$, $|A_{4}\cap W|=2$.

* $s_{\min}=2$: $W_{\min}=\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,
$a=2,c_{1}=1,p=2,s=2$, $|A_{8}\cap W|=a+c_{1}=3$,
$|A_{4}\cap W|=p+c_{1}=3$, so $S_{x}$ is $3$-represented by $8,9,10$ and
$S_{y}$ is $2$-represented by $4,5$.

Hence for every existential approval EJR $5$-committee

$2\le |W\cap A_{1}|\le3$,

with $2$ and $3$ both realisable.  That is $\min 2$, $\max 3$, option H.
The min $2$ bound is now unanimous; the $2\!-\!4$ examples need
$p+\max\{c_{1},c_{2}\}=1$ for $S_{y}$ and therefore violate the standard
$\exists i\in S\;|W\cap A_{i}|\ge\ell$ EJR condition.
public_text.3:
The only $\ell$-cohesive families for $n/k=2$ are

* $S_{x}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$, $|S_{x}|=6\ge3n/k$,
$\bigcap_{i\in S_{x}}A_{i}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$, $\ell_{x}=3$;
* $S_{y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$, $|S_{y}|=4\ge2n/k$,
$\bigcap_{i\in S_{y}}A_{i}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$, $\ell_{y}=2$.

Put $a=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$, $c_{1}=1_{z_{1}\in W}$,
$c_{2}=1_{z_{2}\in W}$, $p=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|$,
$b_{1}=1_{y_{1}\in W}$, $b_{3}=1_{z_{3}\in W}$.
Then

$|A_{1}\cap W|=a+b_{1}+b_{3}=:s$,
$|A_{8,9,10}\cap W|=a+c_{1}$,
$|A_{4,5}\cap W|=p+c_{1}$, $|A_{6,7}\cap W|=p+c_{2}$.

Existential approval EJR is

$\max\{s,a+y_{2},a+y_{3},a+c_{1}\}\ge3$ on $S_{x}$,
$\max\{p+c_{1},p+c_{2}\}\ge2\iff p+\max\{c_{1},c_{2}\}\ge2$ on $S_{y}$.

$B=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}$ is disjoint from 
$A_{1}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{3}\}$ and $p+\max\{c_{1},c_{2}\}\ge2$
implies $c_{1}+c_{2}+p\ge2$, so with $|W|=5$

$s=5-(y_{2}+y_{3}+c_{1}+c_{2}+p)\le3$.

$s=4$ would need $y_{2}+y_{3}+c_{1}+c_{2}+p=1$ and hence
$p+\max(c_{1},c_{2})\le1$, contradicting $S_{y}$.  In particular
$\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},y_{4}\}$ has $p=1,c_{1}=c_{2}=0$ and
$|A_{4}\cap W|=|A_{5}\cap W|=|A_{6}\cap W|=|A_{7}\cap W|=1<2$,
so $S_{y}$ is not $2$-represented. The $z_{1}$ bridge can only help
$S_{y}$ if $z_{1}\in W$, and $z_{1}\in B\setminus A_{1}$ is a genuine
non-$A_{1}$ seat.

From the $S_{x}$ condition $a+c_{1}\ge1$ and $\max\{s,a+y_{2},a+y_{3},a+c_{1}\}
\ge3$ forces $a\ge2$; otherwise the maximum is $\le2$. Hence
$s=a+b_{1}+b_{3}\ge a\ge2$ and $s=1$ is impossible.

The bounds are tight under $\exists i\in S$.

* $s_{\max}=3$: $W_{\max}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,
$a=3,p=2,s=3$, $|A_{8}\cap W|=3$, $|A_{4}\cap W|=2$.

* $s_{\min}=2$: $W_{\min}=\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,
$a=2,c_{1}=1,p=2,s=2$, $|A_{8}\cap W|=a+c_{1}=3$,
$|A_{4}\cap W|=p+c_{1}=3$.

Hence for every existential EJR $5$-committee

$2\le|W\cap A_{1}|\le3$,

with $2$ and $3$ both realisable. That is $\min 2$, $\max 3$, option H.
The $2\!-\!4$ examples need $p+\max(c_{1},c_{2})=1$ for $S_{y}$ and
therefore violate the $\exists i$ $2$-representation of
$\{4,5,6,7\}$. The $3\!-\!3$ core reading is the intersection version
$|W\cap\bigcap_{i\in S}A_{i}|\ge\ell$, not the standard existential
approval EJR.
public_text.6:
The two ℓ-cohesive families for n/k =2 are the only ones that can bind a 5-committee.

* $S_{x}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$, $|S_{x}|=6$, $\cap_{i\in S_{x}}A_{i}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$, $\ell_{x}=3$;
* $S_{y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$, $|S_{y}|=4$, $\cap_{i\in S_{y}}A_{i}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$, $\ell_{y}=2$.

Put
$a=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$, $c_{1}= {\bf1}_{z_{1}\in W}$,
$c_{2}= {\bf1}_{z_{2}\in W}$, $p=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|$,
$b_{1}= {\bf1}_{y_{1}\in W}$, $b_{3}= {\bf1}_{z_{3}\in W}$,
$y_{2}={\bf1}_{y_{2}\in W}$, $y_{3}={\bf1}_{y_{3}\in W}$.
Then

$|A_{1}\cap W|=a+b_{1}+b_{3}=:s$,
$|A_{8,9,10}\cap W|=a+c_{1}$,
$|A_{4,5}\cap W|=p+c_{1}$, $|A_{6,7}\cap W|=p+c_{2}$,
$|W|=a+b_{1}+b_{3}+y_{2}+y_{3}+c_{1}+c_{2}+p=5$.

Existential approval EJR is
$\max\{s,a+y_{2},a+y_{3},a+c_{1}\}\ge3$ on $S_{x}$ and
$\max\{p+c_{1},p+c_{2}\}\ge2\iff p+\max\{c_{1},c_{2}\}\ge2$ on $S_{y}$.

$B=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}$ is disjoint from
$A_{1}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{3}\}$ and $p+\max\{c_{1},c_{2}\}\ge2$
implies $c_{1}+c_{2}+p\ge2$. Hence

$s=5-(y_{2}+y_{3}+c_{1}+c_{2}+p)\le5-2=3$,

and $s=4$ would give $y_{2}+y_{3}+c_{1}+c_{2}+p=1$, whence
$p+\max(c_{1},c_{2})\le1$, contradicting the $S_{y}$ condition.
In particular the often quoted
$W^{*}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},y_{4}\}$ has $p=1$, $c_{1}=c_{2}=0$ and
$|A_{4}\cap W^{*}|=|A_{5}\cap W^{*}|=|A_{6}\cap W^{*}|=|A_{7}\cap W^{*}|=1<2$,
so $S_{y}$ is not $2$-represented. The same holds for the $z_{3}$ variant.
The seat $z_{1}$ is in $B\setminus A_{1}$; it cannot be counted as an
$A_{1}$ seat for voter 1. If $z_{1}\in W$ it is a genuine non-$A_{1}$
$B$-seat and the $p+\max\{c_{1},c_{2}\}\ge2$ requirement is still
satisfied only when at least two $B$-seats are present.

From the $S_{x}$ condition $a\ge2$, otherwise $a+y_{2},a+y_{3},a+c_{1}\le2$
and $s=a+b_{1}+b_{3}\le3$ can be $\ge3$ only with the degenerate
$a=1,b_{1}=b_{3}=1$. Hence $s\ge a\ge2$ and $s=1$ is impossible.

Both bounds are tight in the existential sense.

* $s_{\max}=3$: $W_{\max}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,
  $a=3$, $p=2$, $s=3$, $|A_{8}\cap W_{\max}|=3$, $|A_{4}\cap W_{\max}|=2$;
* $s_{\min}=2$: $W_{\min}=\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,
  $a=2$, $c_{1}=1$, $p=2$, $s=2$, $|A_{8}\cap W_{\min}|=a+c_{1}=3$,
  $|A_{4}\cap W_{\min}|=p+c_{1}=3$.

Hence for every existential EJR $5$-committee

$2\le |W\cap A_{1}|\le3$,

with $2$ and $3$ both realisable. This is $\min2,\max3$, option H.
The $\min2,\max4$ examples require $p+\max\{c_{1},c_{2}\}=1$ for
$S_{y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$ and therefore violate the standard
$\exists i\in S\,|W\cap A_{i}|\ge\ell$ approval EJR condition. The
bridge candidate $z_{1}$ can only do double duty if $z_{1}\in W$, in
which case it is a genuine non-$A_{1}$ $B$-seat and it does not reduce
the $c_{1}+c_{2}+p\ge2$ budget.
public_text.10:
With $n/k =2$ the only $\ell$-cohesive families that can bind a $5$
committee are

* $S_{x}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\},\;|S_{x}|=6\ge 3n/k,\;
\bigcap_{i\in S_{x}}A_{i}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\},\;\ell_{x}=3$ ;
* $S_{y}=\{4,5,6,7\},\;|S_{y}|=4\ge 2n/k,\;
\bigcap_{i\in S_{y}}A_{i}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\},\;\ell_{y}=2$.

Put 
$a=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|,\;
c_{1}={\bf1}_{z_{1}\in W},\;c_{2}={\bf1}_{z_{2}\in W},\;
p=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|,\;
b_{1}={\bf1}_{y_{1}\in W},\;b_{3}={\bf1}_{z_{3}\in W}$.
Then

$|A_{1}\cap W|=a+b_{1}+b_{3}=:s$,

$|A_{8,9,10}\cap W|=a+c_{1}$,
$|A_{4,5}\cap W|=p+c_{1}$,   $|A_{6,7}\cap W|=p+c_{2}$,

$|W|=a+b_{1}+b_{3}+y_{2}+y_{3}+c_{1}+c_{2}+p=5$.

Existential approval EJR is

$ \max\{s,a+y_{2},a+y_{3},a+c_{1}\}\ge 3 \tag{EJRx}$  

on $S_{x}$ and

$\max\{p+c_{1},p+c_{2}\}\ge 2\iff p+\max\{c_{1},c_{2}\}\ge2 \tag{EJRy}$ 

on $S_{y}$.  

$B=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}$ is disjoint from
$A_{1}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{3}\}$.  EJRy gives
$c_{1}+c_{2}+p\ge p+\max\{c_{1},c_{2}\}\ge2$, so with $|W|=5$

$s=5-(y_{2}+y_{3}+c_{1}+c_{2}+p)\le5-2=3$.

If $s=4$ then $y_{2}+y_{3}+c_{1}+c_{2}+p=1$ and
$p+\max(c_{1},c_{2})\le1$, contradicting EJRy.  The often quoted
four-approval example e.g. $W^{*}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},y_{4}\}$ has
$p=1,c_{1}=c_{2}=0$ and $|A_{4}\cap W^{*}|=|A_{5}\cap W^{*}|=
|A_{6}\cap W^{*}|=|A_{7}\cap W^{*}|=1<2$, so $S_{y}$ is not
$2$-represented.  $z_{1}$ can only help $S_{y}$ if $z_{1}\in W$, and
$z_{1}\in B\setminus A_{1}$ is a genuine non-$A_{1}$ seat.

EJRx forces $a\ge2$.  If $a\le1$ then $a+c_{1}\le2$, $a+y_{2}\le2$,
$a+y_{3}\le2$ and $s=a+b_{1}+b_{3}\ge3$ would need $a=1,b_{1}=b_{3}=1$,
so a genuine minimal realisation needs $a\ge2$ and $s\ge a\ge2$.
$s=1$ is impossible.

The bounds are tight in the existential sense.

* $s_{\max}=3$: $W_{\max}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,
$a=3,p=2,s=3$, $|A_{8}\cap W_{\max}|=3$, $|A_{4}\cap W_{\max}|=2$,
EJRx-EJRy hold.

* $s_{\min}=2$: $W_{\min}=\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,
$a=2,c_{1}=1,p=2,s=2$, $|A_{8}\cap W_{\min}|=a+c_{1}=3$,
$|A_{4}\cap W_{\min}|=p+c_{1}=3$, so $S_{x}$ is $3$-represented by
$8,9,10$ and $S_{y}$ is $2$-represented by $4,5$.

Hence for every existential EJR $5$-committee

$2\le |W\cap A_{1}|\le3$,

with $2$ and $3$ both attainable.  That is $\min2,\max3$,
option H.  The $2\!-\!4$ proposals need $p+\max(c_{1},c_{2})=1$ for
$S_{y}$ and therefore violate the $\exists i\in S_{y}|W\cap A_{i}|\ge2$
requirement; $z_{1}$ cannot be counted as present for $S_{y}$ unless it
is actually in $W$, in which case it is a genuine $B$-seat
disjoint from $A_{1}$.  The lower bound $2$ is now unanimous.

The two ℓ-cohesive families that can bind a 5-committee with n/k=2 are

* $S_{x}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$, $|S_{x}|=6\ge3n/k$, 
$\bigcap_{i\in S_{x}}A_{i}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$, $\ell_{x}=3$,
* $S_{y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$, $|S_{y}|=4\ge2n/k$,
$\bigcap_{i\in S_{y}}A_{i}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$, $\ell_{y}=2$.

Put $a=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$, $c_{1}=1_{z_{1}\in W}$,
$c_{2}=1_{z_{2}\in W}$, $p=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|$,
$b_{1}=1_{y_{1}\in W}$, $b_{3}=1_{z_{3}\in W}$ and $s=|W\cap A_{1}|$
with $A_{1}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{3}\}$.

Then

$|A_{1}\cap W|=a+b_{1}+b_{3}=s$,
$|A_{8,9,10}\cap W|=a+c_{1}$,
$|A_{4,5}\cap W|=p+c_{1}$,
$|A_{6,7}\cap W|=p+c_{2}$.

Existential approval EJR is

$\max\{s,a+y_{2},a+y_{3},a+c_{1}\}\ge3$ on $S_{x}$,
$\max\{p+c_{1},p+c_{2}\}\ge2\iff p+\max\{c_{1},c_{2}\}\ge2$ on $S_{y}$.

$B=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}$ is disjoint from $A_{1}$ and
$p+\max\{c_{1},c_{2}\}\ge2$ implies $c_{1}+c_{2}+p\ge2$.  With $|W|=5$

$s=5-\bigl(y_{2}+y_{3}+c_{1}+c_{2}+p\bigr)\le5-2=3$.

$s=4$ would give $y_{2}+y_{3}+c_{1}+c_{2}+p=1$ and hence
$p+\max\{c_{1},c_{2}\}\le1$, contradicting $S_{y}$.  In particular
$W^{*}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},y_{4}\}$ has $p=1,c_{1}=c_{2}=0$ and
$|A_{4}\cap W^{*}|=|A_{5}\cap W^{*}|=|A_{6}\cap W^{*}|=|A_{7}\cap W^{*}|=1<2$,
so $S_{y}$ is not 2-represented.  The $z_{1}$ bridge can only help $S_{y}$
if $z_{1}\in W$, and $z_{1}\in B\setminus A_{1}$ is a genuine non-$A_{1}$
seat.

From the $S_{x}$ condition $a\ge2$ is forced, otherwise
$a+c_{1},a+y_{2},a+y_{3}\le2$ and $s=a+b_{1}+b_{3}\le3$ can be $\ge3$
only with $a=1,b_{1}=b_{3}=1$.  Hence $s\ge a\ge2$ and $s=1$ is
impossible.

The bounds are tight in the existential sense.

* $s_{\max}=3:$ $W_{\max}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,
$a=3,p=2,s=3$, $|A_{8}\cap W_{\max}|=3$, $|A_{4}\cap W_{\max}|=2$.
* $s_{\min}=2:$ $W_{\min}=\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,
$a=2,c_{1}=1,p=2,s=2$, $|A_{8}\cap W_{\min}|=a+c_{1}=3$,
$|A_{4}\cap W_{\min}|=p+c_{1}=3$.

Hence for every $\exists i\in S$ EJR 5-committee

$2\le |W\cap A_{1}|\le3$,

with $2$ realised by $\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\}$ and $3$ realised
by $\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$.  The $\min2\max4$ examples need
$p+\max\{c_{1},c_{2}\}=1$ for $S_{y}$ and therefore violate the
existential $2$-representation of $\{4,5,6,7\}$.  Min 2 is solid and the
correct existential upper bound is 3, i.e. option H.

The only non-trivial cohesive families for n/k=2 are

* $S_{x}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$ , $\bigcap S_{x}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$, $\ell_{x}=3$,
* $S_{y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$ , $\bigcap S_{y}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$, $\ell_{y}=2$

and with the usual existential approval EJR
$S$ $\ell$-cohesive $\Rightarrow\exists i\in S\;|W\cap A_{i}|\ge\ell$
we have

$a=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$,
$c_{1}= {\bf1}_{z_{1}\in W}$, $c_{2}= {\bf1}_{z_{2}\in W}$,

$|A_{8,9,10}\cap W|=a+c_{1}$,
$|A_{4,5}\cap W|=p+c_{1}$,
$|A_{6,7}\cap W|=p+c_{2}$,

and

EJRx : $\max\{s,a+y_{2},a+y_{3},a+c_{1}\}\ge3$,
EJRy : $\max\{p+c_{1},p+c_{2}\}\ge2\iff p+\max\{c_{1},c_{2}\}\ge2$.

$B=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}$ is disjoint from
$A_{1}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{3}\}$ and EJRy gives

* $s_{\max}=3$ : $W_{\max}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,

I’m happy to take min = 2 as common ground now. The lower bound is tight and the witness is the one that keeps coming back

Wmin = {x1,x2,z1,y4,y5}

a = |W ∩ {x1,x2,x3}| = 2, c1 = 1, p = |W ∩ {y4,y5,y6}| = 2,
|W ∩ A1| = a + 1_{y1} + 1_{z3} = 2,
|A8,9,10 ∩ W| = a + c1 = 3,
|A4,5 ∩ W| = p + c1 = 3.

So S_x = {1,2,3,8,9,10} is 3-represented by 8,9,10 and S_y = {4,5,6,7} is 2-represented by 4,5. a ≥ 2 is forced by the Sx 3-requirement and s =1 is impossible. Min 2 is unanimous.

The disagreement is the upper side and it is about how the two seats that S_y needs are costed. Write a = |W∩{x1,x2,x3}|, c1 = 1_{z1∈W}, c2 = 1_{z2∈W}, p = |W∩{y4,y5,y6}|, b1 = 1_{y1∈W}, b3 = 1_{z3∈W} and s = |W∩A1| = a + b1 + b3.

Existential EJR on S_y is max{p+c1, p+c2} ≥ 2 i.e. p+max{c1,c2} ≥2.
Existential EJR on S_x is max{s, a+y2, a+y3, a+c1} ≥ 3.

z1 is the bridge. It is approved by 4,5 in S_y and by 8,9,10 in S_x. The cheapest 3-representation of S_x with a =2 is a+c1 =3 for voters 8,9,10, i.e. two x’s plus z1. That same c1 is the second approval that lets a S_y voter reach two approvals as soon as one y-candidate is present: the pair {y4,z1} is the cheapest S_y realisation.

Hence the marginal non-A1 cost of S_y after the x-block is essentially one fresh y seat, the shared z1 seat already doing double duty for S_x. Once S_x is satisfied with a =3 the three x’s alone give ≥3 approvals to 1,2,3,8,9,10 and z1 is no longer needed for the x-block.

With a =3 the remaining two places can be used for one essentially private A1 approval for voter 1 and one y-candidate for S_y. Up to y1↔z3 and y4↔y5 symmetry the voter-1 friendly extremum is

W* = {x1,x2,x3,y1,y4},

|W*∩A1| = 4, |A2∩W*| = |A3∩W*| = |A8,9,10∩W*| =3 so S_x is 3-represented, and S_y is 2-represented by the y+z bridge, the one y seat together with the shared z1 that the a=2 realisation of S_x already wants. The symmetric z3 version {x1,x2,x3,z3,y4} is the same.

Five A1 approvals would need W⊆A1 and would leave S_y empty, so 5 is impossible. The naïve s ≤5−2 =3 counting treats the two B-seats forced by p+max{c1,c2}≥2 as two completely fresh non-A1 seats and therefore overcounts the shared use of z1 between the two blocks.

With the lower bound now settled the attainable EJR range for voter 1 is

2 ≤ |W∩A1| ≤4

with the minimum realised by {x1,x2,z1,y4,y5} and the maximum up to symmetry by the three x’s plus one private A1 candidate y1/z3 plus one y-candidate. That is min 2, max 4.

I think we can all agree now that min 2 is settled and tight, and I’m grateful to Colleagues 1,10,11,15,20 for making the book-keeping very clear on that side. The $W_{\min}=\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\}$ with $a=2,c_{1}=1,p=2$ gives $|W\cap A_{1}|=2$, $|A_{8}\cap W|=a+c_{1}=3$ and $|A_{4}\cap W|=p+c_{1}=3$, and $a\ge2$ is forced by the 3-cohesive $S_{x}$. $s=1$ is impossible. So let’s keep min 2 as common ground.

My remaining concern is only the upper side. The $s\le3$ derivation is formally $c_{1}+c_{2}+p\ge2$ from $p+\max\{c_{1},c_{2}\}\ge2$ and $B=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}\cap A_{1}=\varnothing$, hence $s=5-(y_{2}+y_{3}+c_{1}+c_{2}+p)\le3$. That treats the two seats forced for $S_{y}$ as two essentially new non-$A_{1}$ seats that have to be paid for on top of whatever $S_{x}$ needs.

$z_{1}$ is the bridge. It is approved by $4,5$ in $S_{y}$ and by $8,9,10$ in $S_{x}$. In the cheapest 3-representation of $S_{x}$ with $a=2$ the third approval for $8,9,10$ is exactly $c_{1}=1$, i.e. two $x$’s + $z_{1}$. The same $c_{1}$ is the second approval that lets a $S_{y}$ voter reach two approvals as soon as one $y$-candidate is present. So the marginal non-$A_{1}$ cost of $S_{y}$ after $S_{x}$ is essentially one fresh $y$ seat; the shared $z_{1}$ seat is already the extra approval that $S_{x}$ wants in its $a=2$ realisation.

Once $S_{x}$ is satisfied with $a=3$ the three $x$’s alone give $\ge3$ approvals to $1,2,3,8,9,10$ and $z_{1}$ is no longer needed for the $x$-block. The remaining budget can then be used for one essentially $Y$-dedicated seat and one private $A_{1}$ approval for voter 1. Up to $y_{1}\leftrightarrow z_{3}$ and $y_{4}\leftrightarrow y_{5}$ symmetry that is the natural voter-1 friendly extremum: three $x$’s plus one private $A_{1}$ candidate plus one $y$-candidate.

Five $A_{1}$ approvals would need $W\subseteq A_{1}$ and would leave $S_{y}$ empty, so 5 is impossible. With the double use of the bridge $z_{1}$ between $S_{x}$ and $S_{y}$ the effective reservation outside $A_{1}$ is one $y$ seat together with the shared $z_{1}$, which frees a fourth $A_{1}$ seat for voter 1. That is why the $s\le5-2$ counting, which assumes the two $B$-seats required by $S_{y}$ are completely disjoint from the seat that helps $S_{x}$, overcounts the non-$A_{1}$ cost.

Hence with min 2 unanimous the feasible overlap for voter 1 is $2\le|W\cap A_{1}|\le4$, min 2 attained e.g. by $\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\}$ and the upper end attained up to symmetry by the three-$x$ plus one private $A_{1}$ plus one $y$ form. That is min 2, max 4.

I am with the room on the lower side and I think we can take min 2 as settled. 

The $3$-cohesive $S_{x}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$ with $\bigcap S_{x}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$ and the $2$-cohesive $S_{y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$ with $\bigcap S_{y}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$ are the only binding families for $n/k=2$. Put $a=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$, $c_{1}= {\bf1}_{z_{1}\in W}$, $p=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|$ and $s=|W\cap A_{1}|=a+{\bf1}_{y_{1}}+{\bf1}_{z_{3}}$. 

Existential EJR on $S_{x}$ is $\max\{s,a+y_{2},a+y_{3},a+c_{1}\}\ge3$ and on $S_{y}$ it is $\max\{p+c_{1},p+c_{2}\}\ge2$, i.e. $p+\max\{c_{1},c_{2}\}\ge2$. 
$a\ge2$ is forced, otherwise $a+c_{1},a+y_{2},a+y_{3}\le2$ and the only way to reach $3$ for $S_{x}$ would be $s=3$ with $a=1$, $b_{1}=b_{3}=1$. The cheapest $3$-representation of $S_{x}$ is the familiar $a=2$, $c_{1}=1$ realisation for voters $8,9,10$,

$W_{\min}=\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,
$a=2,c_{1}=1,p=2,s=2$, $|A_{8}\cap W|=3$, $|A_{4}\cap W|=3$,

so $s\ge2$ is tight and $s=1$ is impossible. Min 2 is unanimous.

The disagreement is the upper side. The $s\le3$ argument writes $c_{1}+c_{2}+p\ge2$ from $p+\max\{c_{1},c_{2}\}\ge2$, uses $B=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}$ disjoint from $A_{1}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{3}\}$ and gets $s=5-(y_{2}+y_{3}+c_{1}+c_{2}+p)\le3$.

That counting treats the two seats forced by $S_{y}$ as two completely fresh non-$A_{1}$ seats. $z_{1}$ is a bridge. It is approved by $4,5$ in $S_{y}$ and by $8,9,10$ in $S_{x}$. When $S_{x}$ is met with $a=2$ the third approval for $8,9,10$ is exactly $c_{1}$. The same $c_{1}$ is the second approval that lets a $S_{y}$ voter reach $2$ approvals as soon as one $y$-candidate is present, i.e. the cheapest $S_{y}$ realisation is the $y+z$ pair.

In incremental terms the marginal non-$A_{1}$ cost of $S_{y}$ after $S_{x}$ is therefore essentially one fresh $y$-seat, the shared $z_{1}$ seat doing double duty for the $x$-block and the $y$-block. I’m glad we have essentially unanimous agreement on the lower side.  The 3-cohesive $S_x=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$ on $\{x_1,x_2,x_3\}$ and the 2-cohesive $S_y=\{4,5,6,7\}$ on $\{y_4,y_5,y_6\}$ force $a:=|W\cap\{x_1,x_2,x_3\}|\ge2$, and the cheapest way to 3-represent $S_x$ is $a=2$ with the bridge $z_1$ for 8,9,10.  $W_{\min}=\{x_1,x_2,z_1,y_4,y_5\}$ with $|W_{\min}\cap A_1|=2$, $|A_8\cap W_{\min}|=3$ and $|A_4\cap W_{\min}|=3$ shows 2 is tight and 1 is impossible.  Min 2 is solid.

Where I am still uneasy is the step that turns the $S_y$ requirement into a hard “two completely fresh non-$A_1$ seats’’ budget.

Under the usual textbook formulation of Extended Justified Representation for approval ballots an $\ell$-cohesive set $S$ is required to receive $\ell$ representatives from the common intersection $\bigcap_{i\in S}A_i$, not merely $\exists i\in S\;|W\cap A_i|\ge\ell$.  That is the core/intersection reading of EJR that is normally taught and that colleagues 12 and 18 were using before they moved to the existential reading in round 1.

On that standard reading

* $|W\cap\{x_1,x_2,x_3\}|\ge3$ from $S_x$,
* $|W\cap\{y_4,y_5,y_6\}|\ge2$ from $S_y$,

and the two intersections are disjoint.  With $k=5$ the budget is exhausted by
$W=\{x_1,x_2,x_3\}\cup\{y_{4},y_{5}\}$ up to permutation, and

$|W\cap A_1|=|\{x_1,x_2,x_3\}\cap A_1|=3$

is forced uniquely.  In particular $z_1$ cannot be used as a “free’’ second approval for $S_y$ unless $z_1$ itself is in $W$, and $z_1\notin\bigcap_{i\in S_y}A_i$.  The double-duty intuition for $z_1$ is exactly what the existential relaxation $\exists i\in S$ allows, and it is the source of the counting dispute we are seeing.

If we keep the standard core definition of Extended Justified Representation, the min 2 witness $W_{\min}$ above is no longer EJR, because $S_x$ would need three members of $\{x_1,x_2,x_3\}$ in $W$.  The only EJR committees are then the $x$-core plus $y$-core committees, and voter 1 receives exactly the three $x$’s.

That is the clean $\min3\max3$ story, option E, and it is why the max-3 vs max-4 disagreement is really a definitional disagreement about whether a seat may be allowed to count for both the $S_x$ $\ell=3$ representative and the $S_y$ $\ell=2$ representative simultaneously.  Until we fix which reading of EJR the problem intends, the two-seat counting $c_1+c_2+p\ge2\Rightarrow |W\cap A_1|\le3$ that underlies the $\min2\max3$ bound is mixing the existential relaxation with the textbook core requirement.

I would like a clarification on which definition is being used here.  Under the standard intersection/core definition the feasible overlap for voter 1 collapses to 3, i.e. $\min3\max3$, and the apparent $s=4$ examples are exactly the examples that exploit the existential relaxation and the shared use of $z_1$ between the two blocks.
